title: Custom-kind instances DROPPED silently when a kind option is authored with nixpkgs lib.types.str
description:
SILENT DATA LOSS. A custom kind whose options include a string field authored
the way the corpus authors them (nixpkgs lib.types.str) has its instances
DROPPED by ingest discovery, with no abort and no warning.

MEASURED (denhoag-writer, 2026-07-27, real mkInstanceRegistry then
denCompat.ingest.ingest; value held CONSTANT tag="west" across arms, only the
declaring engine/flag varies):

  arm A  lib.types.str (corpus authoring)
         carried id_hash  sha256("rack|name=r1")
         instanceKeyMap.rack  "rack"
         instances.rack       [ ]   <-- EMPTY, real instances at rackFarm dropped

  arm B  schema.types.str (positive control)
         carried id_hash  sha256("rack|name=r1|tag=west")
         instanceKeyMap.rack  "rackFarm"
         instances.rack       ["r1"]

  arm C  lib.types.str + internal = true
         same as A -- but this is NOT new, it is the documented .8 gap the
         marker map exists to cover, already pinned by
         compat-registry-kind-marker claim (c'). Do not read C as a regression.

B is the control: the instrument DOES find the registry when the hashes agree,
so A's empty is a real negative.

MECHANISM. Both discovery paths miss, independently:
  - ingest's VALUE marker misses, so it falls back to the SINGULAR namespace
    `rack`; registries.rack is empty and the real instances at `rackFarm` are
    never reached.
  - the bridge's OPTION marker does not rescue it: registryKindOf is null on
    that shape, on BOTH gen-merge revs (2701d8bb and 8daa25de) -- so this is
    NOT a gen-merge-rev artifact.

ROOT. den-hoag's gen-schema pin 017062cd has mkIdentityModule's
primitiveTypeNames = ["string","int","bool"] -- no "str" -- so a lib.types.str
option is NOT an identity key and is absent from the carried hash, while
den-hoag's own identityKeysOf (registry.nix:330-345) accepts BOTH spellings and
counts it. The two disagree, and the hash gate fails CLOSED (null reads as "not
this kind"), which is why nothing raises.

SYMPTOM CLASS = .8 exactly: registry never reaches the fleet, no root nodes,
silent.

NOT A CORPUS-LIVE BUG TODAY. nix-config pins gen-schema 103ea88, whose
mkIdentityModule list DOES include "str", so the corpus's stamper and
den-hoag's identityKeysOf agree there. The breakage is den-hoag's own pin
against corpus authoring style. It becomes live the moment the pins meet.

INTERACTS WITH den-hoag-lcz: gen-schema main's identityHashForKind still
EXCLUDES "str" while its mkIdentityModule includes it. So routing through the
twin fixes this only if lcz is fixed first. Sequence matters -- see the ruling
on .23.

FIX DIRECTION (measured, not assumed): route BOTH call sites through
gen-schema's identityHashForKind -- bridge registryKindOf AND ingest's
value-marker discovery. ingest.nix has the kind values in scope
(v1Schema.<kind>.options), so both are reachable. Requires lcz first or the
twin disagrees with the stamper.

WITNESS: den-hoag-9xo.23's R2.1 reshape becomes the regression pin for this.
close_reason:
CLOSED on BOTH halves, measured together on the final state. Neither alone is
the fix: distinct identities discovery cannot find is still a dropped registry,
and discovery finding a registry whose instances share an identity is still
data loss.

  COLLAPSE   two instances, same name, differing ONLY in a nixpkgs-lib.types.str
             field -> DISTINCT id_hash (629b72c8... / f891b540...)
  DISCOVERY  arm C on the direct path -> instanceKeyMap.rack = "rackFarm",
             instances.rack = ["r1"]   (was "rack" / [ ])

Arm A stayed authored lib.types.str throughout. Neither the fix nor any fixture
was adjusted to make it pass.

ROOT CAUSE was upstream and two-layered:
  1. gen-schema carried TWO copies of the primitive-type-name list --
     identityHashForKind's and mkIdentityModule's -- and they had drifted.
     39d3d5d moved both to gen-types names; e6dbe8e fixed THE STAMPER ONLY,
     its own message naming the symptom ("two instances differing only in such
     a field collapsed to one id_hash") and shipping a regression test. The
     twin was never touched. den-hoag's pin predated e6dbe8e, so den-hoag
     carried the COLLAPSE, not merely a discovery miss.
     Fixed: gen-schema af3dbe9 hoists ONE list, deletes both locals.
  2. den-hoag re-implemented the reflection itself (identityKeysOf), accepting
     both spellings -- right only when the stamping gen-schema accepts both.
     Fixed: 4986982 routes registryKindOf through gen-schema's own
     identityHashForKind; identityKeysOf DELETED, not taught a third spelling.

COMMITS: gen-schema af3dbe9; den-hoag 4986982 (bridge marker + identityKeysOf
dissolved), b2e5373 (bump + drift-alarm pins updated), 51fd4e7 (direct-path
marker). All pushed.

THE SECOND HALF WAS A COMPAT/KERNEL INVERSION. Arm C was rescued on the BRIDGE
path by _registryKinds and stayed broken on mkDen-direct, which has no bridge.
Discovery correct on the compat surface, wrong on the kernel surface -- the
inversion this whole arc dissolves. Ruled fixed on those grounds; the behaviour
change to pinned claim (c') is the orchestrator's call, not the writer's.

DEVIATION ACCEPTED: the marker is derived INSIDE ingest from the RAW v1
declarations, not at the mkDenWith seam as I specified. Better, and the
coverage argument is decisive -- the seam version covers only mkDenWith, so a
fixture calling denCompat.ingest.ingest directly would still be broken, which
is precisely the "moved which path is broken" failure the conditions exist to
prevent. It also obeys the acyclicity rule the code already states (derive from
v1Schema, NOT schemaDecls, ingest.nix:472-475) rather than needing a new seam
to escape it, and avoids a second write site for _registryKinds.

KEY DISTINCTION the code comment does not draw: ingest.nix:440-448 says
identityHashForKind CANNOT be used here. That is TRUE of buildSchema's stripped
output ({parent = null;}, no options, no kind) and FALSE of the raw
declarations processed through gen-schema's own mkSchemaOption
(kind = "rack", options = ["region","sopsTag"]). The constraint was narrower
than it read.

PIN DELIBERATELY CHANGED: claim (c') pinned "the value-reflecting fallback
ALONE leaves the registry EMPTY" -- that pinned a GAP, not a design. Rewritten
to the new behaviour. AND the limit is pinned beside it: a kind declared with
no options gives option-level reflection nothing to reflect, so that namespace
still resolves to no kind. Without that limit the new claim is satisfiable by a
marker that answers every namespace.

UNPROVEN, carried on this bead: whether feeding processed kind values into
discovery would actually close a cycle (ingest.nix:472-475 states the
constraint; registries at :519 sits after instanceKeyMap at :506, consistent
with it). NOT MEASURED -- deliberately, because the measurement could not
change the decision: two discovery implementations would be the duplication
this arc dissolves regardless of whether the cycle bites. Starting point if
anyone wants a simpler design there.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
UNPROVEN, recorded so it is not re-derived: whether deriving the marker from
schemaDecls (instead of the raw v1 declarations) would actually close a cycle.

Evidence, and it is NOT a measurement:
  - ingest.nix:472-475 states the constraint in its own words -- "schemaDecls now
    declares the stamp-field options, which depend on instanceKeyMap <- customKinds;
    deriving from v1Schema keeps that chain acyclic."
  - the ordering is consistent with it: registries = buildRegistries {...} sits at
    ingest.nix:519, AFTER instanceKeyMap (:506) and customInstances (:507).

A stated constraint plus a consistent ordering is not proof that the cycle bites.
It was deliberately NOT measured, because the measurement could not change the
decision: the alternative design needs a second discovery implementation, which is
the duplication being dissolved regardless of whether the cycle is real.

registryKindsOf (shipped) sidesteps the question entirely -- it reads only the RAW
v1 declarations, which is the same rule the customKinds derivation already follows.

If someone later wants a simpler design in this area, this is the starting point:
measure the cycle first, because the shipped design does not depend on the answer
and a simpler one might.

title: Parented hosts lose nixpkgs.hostPlatform: sysModule skipped at flake-module.nix:288-290 once .8 lands
description:
GATES THE NIX-CONFIG LOCK BUMP for den-hoag-9xo.8. Does NOT gate the gen-merge push: no corpus build
changes until nix-config's gen-schema/gen-merge moves.

Once .8's fix lands, host scope roots acquire PARENTS for the first time on the corpus:
  host:axon-01/02/03, uplink       -> environment:prod
  host:bitstream, blade, cortex, patch, slab -> environment:dev
  host:cortex-cuda                 -> null   (separate anomaly, see den-hoag-9xo.9)
axon-01's root decls also gain accessGroups, so containment bindings ARE delivering. That half works.

But every nixos host then fails EARLIER than before the fix:
  before: "Failed assertions:"  (initrd SSH key / no wheel password)
  after:  "Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set"

ATTRIBUTION IS ESTABLISHED, not assumed. Control: the same path-override pointed at gen-merge f7e3afb
WITHOUT the getSubOptions change reproduces "Failed assertions:" exactly. So the override mechanism is
not the cause; the change is. (f7e3afb is precisely nix-config's pinned rev, so the experiment differs
by exactly one commit.)

LOCALIZED to lib/compat/flake-module.nix:288-290:
    hostEntry = bindings.host or null;
    sys       = if hostEntry == null then null else systemFor hostEntry;
    sysModule = if sys == null then [ ] else [ { nixpkgs.hostPlatform.system = sys; } ];
A system-less host injects NOTHING -- which is exactly the observed symptom.

WHAT IS KNOWN:
  - the host registry's own `system` field is INTACT and byte-identical before/after
    (axon-01 = x86_64-linux, patch = aarch64-darwin, slab = aarch64-linux). The field did not vanish.
  - so the break is between the registry field and the terminal's read of it.

WHAT IS NOT YET KNOWN -- do not guess:
  whether `bindings.host` is null, or `systemFor hostEntry` returns null. NOT distinguished. Every
  downstream read cascades from the single hostPlatform error (a networking.hostName probe fails with
  that same error, so it is inconclusive and was not treated as evidence).

HYPOTHESIS TO TEST FIRST (unverified): the terminal's binding set is keyed on a host node being a bare
ROOT, and a host that now has a parent no longer presents `bindings.host` the same way. That would make
this a rung-1/topology consequence surfacing for the first time, since parentage never existed on the
corpus before.

This is a den-hoag defect newly EXPOSED by parented hosts, not a gen-merge defect.
close_reason: Fixed in three commits, all on origin: 2cd0d9f bounds the family fold and aborts on a duplicate member; b133849 makes the class terminal own the members it contributes so the redundant spawn is never emitted; 3bd1d4f rejects a spawn whose slice node and placement target disagree (demand-time, radius = one member). nixpkgs.hostPlatform now 0 of 9, verified both sides. Residue filed separately and unchased: mu9 (id_hash, newly reachable), yp1 (slab built from the wrong node's subtree).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
ID_HASH HYPOTHESIS IS DEAD. So is the bindings.host-is-null alternative. Measured at the den-hoag level,
not through the NixOS eval, 2026-07-27.

METHOD. Instrumented a scratch den-hoag at BOTH candidate sites and added an UNCONDITIONAL marker at
wrapper entry, because two conditional throws that never fire prove nothing on their own -- a silent
instrument is indistinguishable from a dead code path until you arm a positive control.

  1. ingest.nix:586  systemFor -> throw on a missing systemByHostId key      NEVER FIRED
  2. flake-module.nix:288  bindings.host -> throw when absent                NEVER FIRED
  3. unconditional trace at mkNixosInstantiate's return                      FIRED, once, both sides

RESULT (axon-01, den = real den-hoag @21a7d87, only gen-schema/gen-merge swapped):

  base (gen-merge f7e3afb, no fix):
    sysNull=no:x86_64-linux  perHostEvalNull=no  nSysModule=1  nHostModules=60
  fix  (gen-merge 8daa25d):
    sysNull=no:x86_64-linux  perHostEvalNull=no  nSysModule=1  nHostModules=136

So under the fix: the wrapper IS entered (exactly once), bindings.host IS present, systemFor RESOLVES to
x86_64-linux, the sysModule IS built (length 1), and the per-host evaluator is present. Every link the
original hypothesis suspected is intact. There is no id_hash mismatch to find.

THE ACTUAL DELTA: nHostModules 60 -> 136. The fix delivers +76 host modules -- environment-scope content
now reaching the host through containment, which is precisely what .8 was supposed to enable. The only
other observed difference is the binding set gaining `accessGroups`.

WHERE IT NOW POINTS (hypothesis, explicitly NOT concluded). nixpkgs.hostPlatform is reported unset while
our sysModule demonstrably carries it, so the failing evaluation is one that did not receive the
sysModule. Since the wrapper ran exactly ONCE with correct values, the most likely shape is a NESTED
NixOS evaluation introduced by the +76 modules -- one that does not pass through mkNixosInstantiate and
therefore never gets a platform injected. The failing frame is nixos/modules/services/hardware/
bluetooth.nix forcing its `pkgs` arg -> nixpkgs.localSystem -> nixpkgs.system, entered from a
familyMerge branch at den-hoag lib/default.nix:2097.

NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: identify what among the +76 modules triggers an inner system eval
(bisect the delivered set, or mark the wrapper's sysModule and check whether the failing frame carries
it). Do NOT re-test the id_hash path -- it is measured intact on both sides.

R2.4's VERDICT HAS EXPIRED, restated. R2.4 measured both silent `or null` defaults on the
source -> ent.meta path and declared them benign. That was measured PRE-FIX. It does not survive the fix
and should not be cited as current. Note the two `or null` defaults R2.4 cleared (bridge.nix parent,
ingest.nix buildSchema parent) are NOT the same two as the pair suspected here (bindings.host,
systemByHostId lookup) -- and this measurement shows the latter pair is NOT firing either. The correct
current statement is: no `or null` on either path is silently swallowing anything for axon-01; the defect
is elsewhere.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-07-27). familyMerge deep-merges TWO built NixOS configurations at the same
family/member path. Its own documented invariant is false under .8's fix.

THE COLLISION, with the path threaded (a bare leaf key would have named only "_type" and been useless):

  PROBE-FAMILY-COLLISION path=nixosConfigurations.axon-01._type aIsAttrs=no bIsAttrs=no -> b WINS

  base (gen-merge f7e3afb): collisions=0   wrapper markers=1
  fix  (gen-merge 8daa25d): collisions=1   wrapper markers=1

So under the fix TWO contributions arrive at [nixosConfigurations, axon-01]. Both are attrsets, so
familyMerge (lib/default.nix:2092-2098) recurses INTO them and merges two built configurations
member-by-member. `_type` is a scalar on both sides, which is why exactly one collision surfaces --
everything else is attrs-vs-attrs and recurses silently.

THE INVARIANT THAT IS FALSE. lib/default.nix:2088-2091 states verbatim:
  "A leaf (a built artifact -- never an attrset with a colliding key path) rides as-is; two subtrees at
   the same family key merge. Member names are `attrNames output.systems.<class>` -- unique per class --
   so no two contributions target the same [ family, member ] leaf."
Under the fix they DO. A built NixOS configuration IS an attrset, so the `isAttrs a && isAttrs b` test
cannot tell "family subtree" from "built artifact" and descends into the artifact.

WHY TWO CONTRIBUTIONS NOW. Only ONE of them passes through mkNixosInstantiate (wrapper markers = 1 on
both sides), and that one carries the sysModule with nixpkgs.hostPlatform.system = x86_64-linux
(measured: sysNull=no:x86_64-linux, nSysModule=1). The second contribution never goes through the
wrapper and therefore has no platform. Deep-merging them lets the platform-less side win on scalars
(`else bv` -- b WINS), which is why the built config reports
"Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set" even though the
wrapper demonstrably injected it.

Consistent with the other measured delta: nHostModules 60 -> 136 (+76). axon-01 is now reachable from
its own host root AND, through containment, from environment:prod -- so it is contributed twice.

RULED OUT, MEASURED, do not re-test:
  - id_hash mismatch. Literal comparison at ingest.nix:586:
      delivered      = 20bd5d8269c9b2c0755c2d7346ec2fa4087803dddc7c83158766fcda1370910f
      present_in_map = YES
      declared_keys  = 10 keys for 10 hosts, delivered is the first
  - bindings.host being null. It is present; the wrapper is entered exactly once with it.
  - either `or null` swallowing anything. systemFor returns x86_64-linux on both sides.

FIX DIRECTION (not implemented -- needs a design call). familyMerge must treat a built artifact as a
LEAF, which `isAttrs` cannot express. Two candidate shapes: (a) bound the recursion to the family/member
depth the face law actually defines (exactly two levels), so member VALUES are never descended; or
(b) mark built artifacts explicitly and stop at the marker. Note (a) also turns the current silent
last-writer-wins into a detectable duplicate-member condition, which is the thing that should probably
abort rather than merge. Whether two contributions to one member is itself legitimate is the prior
question: if axon-01 should be contributed once, the defect is upstream of familyMerge and this is only
where it becomes visible.

PATTERN, third instance: pre-existing code newly REACHABLE, not new breakage. Before .8, parentage never
fired on this corpus, so no member was ever contributed twice and familyMerge's invariant held by
accident. Same shape as cortex in .20 (present and throwing, not absent) and as .8 itself surviving a
green suite. REPAIR, do not revert.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CONFIRMED with a built-in positive control (2026-07-27). The member-depth recursion is the defect.

Earlier evidence was a COLLISION trace, which proves the merge descended but does not by itself
distinguish "instrument never fires" from "code never does it". Re-instrumented to trace the RECURSION
branch itself, tagged by depth, so the family level acts as a known-positive that must fire:

  depth=0  family level    -- the emptyFamilies seed merges {nixosConfigurations = {};} against real
                              contributions, so this MUST fire; if it does not, the instrument is broken
  depth=1  MEMBER level    -- the violation; must NOT fire if familyMerge's stated invariant holds

RESULT (axon-01, den = real den-hoag @21a7d87, only gen-schema/gen-merge swapped):

  base (gen-merge f7e3afb):  depth=0 fires 8x   depth=1 fires 0x   -> invariant HOLDS
  fix  (gen-merge 8daa25d):  depth=0 fires 15x  depth=1 fires 1x   -> invariant VIOLATED
                             depth=1 path = nixosConfigurations.axon-01

The known-positive fires on BOTH sides (8 and 15), so the instrument is demonstrably live and the base
zero is a real negative, not a dead probe. Member-depth recursion goes 0 -> 1 with the fix, at exactly
the member whose platform goes missing.

That closes the chain: two contributions land at [nixosConfigurations, axon-01]; familyMerge recurses
INTO both built configurations because `isAttrs a && isAttrs b` cannot tell a family subtree from a built
artifact; only one of the two passed through mkNixosInstantiate (wrapper markers = 1 on both sides) so
only one carries the sysModule; and the scalar arm (`else bv`) lets the platform-less side win. Hence
"Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set" despite the wrapper
demonstrably injecting x86_64-linux.

Also confirms familyMerge's own comment (lib/default.nix:2088-2091) states an invariant the code does not
enforce -- "no two contributions target the same [ family, member ] leaf" is false under the fix, and
nothing checks it.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
PRODUCERS IDENTIFIED AND MEASURED (2026-07-27). Answer 1: the attachment-side emission is spurious AND
EMPTY. Not "each incomplete differently".

THE TWO PRODUCERS of [nixosConfigurations, axon-01]:
  contributions             lib/default.nix:2155    1 contribution   (fleet total 9)
  instantiateContributions  lib/default.nix:2369    1 contribution   (fleet total 22)

WHAT EACH CARRIES (isolated by dropping one producer at a time, env-gated, NO renaming):

  contributions              wrapper FIRES:  sys=x86_64-linux   nHostModules=136
                             => IS mkNixosInstantiate's path; carries the sysModule AND the +76
                                containment modules. THE COMPLETE CONTRIBUTION.

  instantiateContributions   wrapper SILENT; and the arm's own slice measures:
                               node=environment:prod class=nixos into=nixosConfigurations.axon-01 nModules=0
                             => ZERO modules. No sysModule, no containment content. COMPLETELY EMPTY.

Control: nModules=0 reproduces with NOTHING dropped (DEN_PROBE_DROP=none), so it is not an artifact of
the isolation. With drop=instantiate the wrapper fires at 136 and no instantiate emission targets axon-01.

*** THE UPSTREAM DEFECT, PRECISELY ***
The spawn action fires at node=environment:prod and slices
  output.classSubtreeAt <nodeId> <class>   with nodeId = "environment:prod"
i.e. the ATTACHING node's own nixos subtree -- which is empty, because the host's content lives at
host:axon-01, the ATTACHED node. So it emits an EMPTY nixos configuration into the host's member slot.

That empty config then wins: the fold's member-level union takes the later contribution, and
instantiateContributions is appended last. An empty NixOS config has no nixpkgs.hostPlatform, which is
exactly the reported symptom. Pre-guard the old recursive merge instead merged the two attribute-by-
attribute, which is why the platform vanished while the wrapper demonstrably injected it.

MY EARLIER READING WAS WRONG, recorded so it is not repeated: I inferred from .9's "whoever attaches,
instantiates" that the ROOT contribution was redundant. It is the opposite. The attachment does drive
instantiation -- through the class terminal, which is the `contributions` path -- and its separate
parallel emission adds nothing but an empty artifact.

NOT A ONE-LINE DELETE. The instantiate arm carries 22 contributions fleet-wide against `contributions`'
9, and dropping it wholesale fails differently (attribute 'id_hash' missing). Only the host-member
emission is spurious. Two candidate fixes, owner/lead call:
  (a) do not emit for a member the class terminal already contributes; or
  (b) slice at the ATTACHED node (host:axon-01) rather than the attaching one, making the emission
      meaningful instead of empty -- note this would then DUPLICATE the class terminal's work, so (a)
      looks right unless the spawn arm is meant to replace the terminal for attached members.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
THE THREE NUMBERS (2026-07-27). Double-consumption hypothesis CONFIRMED in substance; the 9/13 split was
wrong in detail — there is a THIRD declaration, and it is pre-existing.

(1) intoAttr BREAKDOWN of all 22 spawn emissions, with the emitting node:

    node=environment:prod  class=nixos           -> nixosConfigurations        x4
    node=environment:dev   class=nixos           -> nixosConfigurations        x3
    node=environment:dev   class=darwin          -> darwinConfigurations       x1
    node=environment:dev   class=droid           -> nixOnDroidConfigurations   x1
                                                    ------------------------------
                                                    9  OS-output emissions  <- THE DUPLICATES
    node=host:<each of 10> class=nixos|darwin|droid -> colmenaModules        x10
    node=cluster:axon      class=k8s-manifests   -> nixidyEnvs                x3
                                                    22 total

    The 7 nixosConfigurations emissions match the 7 duplicated hosts EXACTLY (prod: axon-01/02/03 +
    uplink; dev: bitstream/blade/cortex). patch rides the darwin one, slab the droid one. cortex-cuda is
    absent, consistent with its parent edge never forming (den-hoag-9xo.9).

(2) WHICH CORPUS DECLARATION EACH TRACES TO — named, not inferred from counts:

    nix-config modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:74      (den.lib.policy.instantiate hostCfg)
        Fires at ENVIRONMENT scope, emitted TOGETHER with `resolve.to "host"` at :71-75. Produces the 9
        OS-output emissions. THE DUPLICATE.
    nix-config modules/den/batteries/colmena.nix:96   (den.lib.policy.instantiate { ... }) -> "colmenaModules"
        Fires at HOST scope. Produces the 10 colmenaModules emissions. A THIRD declaration, NOT in the
        original hypothesis. Targets a family with no class terminal, so it duplicates nothing.
    nix-config modules/den/policies/clusters.nix:104
        Produces the 3 nixidyEnvs emissions at cluster:axon. Cluster work, no class terminal, duplicates
        nothing. (Hypothesis correct here.)

    So 22 = 9 duplicating + 10 colmena (pre-existing) + 3 cluster. NOT "9 host-family + 13 cluster".

(3) DID THE ARM EMIT HOST-FAMILY CONTRIBUTIONS BEFORE THE FIX? NO. Base emits 10 spawn contributions,
    ALL of them colmenaModules from host nodes. ZERO environment-node emissions, zero cluster emissions.
    => FOURTH INSTANCE of pre-existing-code-newly-reachable: fleet.nix:74 fires at environment scope and
    could not fire at all until environments existed as nodes. The declaration was always there; the
    node it fires at was not.

*** THE DOUBLE CONSUMPTION, CONFIRMED ***
ONE v1 declaration -- the host's `instantiate` -- is consumed by TWO den-hoag paths:
  a) the CLASS TERMINAL: ingest.nix builds `instantiateFor` keyed by id_hash from v1's per-host
     host.instantiate; flake-module.nix wraps it as the systemFor-injecting instantiate. COMPLETE
     (sys=x86_64-linux, nHostModules=136).
  b) the PARKED SPAWN: fleet.nix:74's `policy.instantiate hostCfg`, recovered as a declare.spawn and
     emitted again WITHOUT the wrapper, slicing output.classSubtreeAt at the ATTACHING node
     (environment:prod) rather than the attached host => nModules=0. EMPTY.
The empty one is appended last and wins the member union, so the host loses nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

FIX SHAPE. De-duplicate one declaration; do NOT delete the arm (10 colmena + 3 cluster emissions are
real work). And do NOT suppress by family NAME -- the arm's design is that family/key/evaluator/class
are DATA on the spec ("no family-name branch, no per-tool code"), so a `nixosConfigurations` special-case
reintroduces exactly the per-tool branch that comment forbids. The suppression has to be structural:
"this [family, member] already has a contribution from the class terminal". Note the same structural
rule also covers the darwin and droid emissions for free, which a nixos-named branch would miss.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
FIX SHIPPED @b133849 — site chosen AT EMISSION, not at spawn creation. Acceptance checks 1 and 2 PASS;
check 3 is mixed and reported straight.

*** WHY NOT AT SPAWN CREATION (the leaned-toward site) — REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT ***
Placement breakdown, class terminal vs spawn arm:
  class terminal (9): nixosConfigurations x8 (INCLUDING cortex-cuda) + darwinConfigurations.patch
  spawn OS-output (9): nixosConfigurations x7 (NOT cortex-cuda) + darwinConfigurations.patch
                       + nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab
Two members break the "don't park a spawn for a host already consumed into instantiateFor" rule:
  - nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab has NO terminal contribution. The spawn is its ONLY producer.
    Suppressing at spawn creation would DELETE slab's configuration outright.
  - cortex-cuda has only a terminal contribution and no spawn at all.
The two sets are not in correspondence, and the difference is not knowable at spawn-creation time: it
depends on whether the family has a receiver row, which is resolved in the kernel fold, not where the
spec is parked. So the predicate "the terminal owns this member" is only expressible where BOTH sets
exist -- at the emission site in lib/default.nix, where `contributions` and `instantiateContributions`
are in the same scope.

*** THE FIX ***
`unownedInstantiateContributions` = the spawn arm minus any contribution whose [family, member] appears
in the class terminal's own placements. Set membership on placement paths; NO family name anywhere, so
it covers nixos/darwin/droid uniformly. Filtered BEFORE the fold, so the contribution never enters --
not emitted-then-dropped, which would restore precedence-by-ordering and require the duplicate guard to
stay quiet about a case it should catch.

*** CHECK 1 -- PASS. The other 13 survive; nothing was papered over. ***
familyOutputs on the corpus, post-fix:
  colmenaModules            all 10 hosts        (the 10 per-host captures intact)
  nixidyEnvs                3 systems           (cluster work intact)
  nixOnDroidConfigurations  slab                (the spawn-only producer KEPT -- the site-1 casualty)
  darwinConfigurations      patch               (now resolves; it aborted as a duplicate pre-fix)
  nixosConfigurations       8 incl. cortex-cuda
No duplicate-member abort anywhere: the guard is SILENT on the corpus.

Note a correction to my own earlier enumeration: the duplicate set was EIGHT, not seven --
darwinConfigurations.patch was also duplicated. My first collector missed it because it ran during an
eval of nixosConfigurations.axon-01 and the darwin family was never forced. Lazy enumeration
under-reports; the placement lists (which are eager) are the reliable source.

*** CHECK 2 -- PASS. Guard armed and silent. ***
Corpus produces no duplicate (silent). Suite still arms it: ci=0 with
ci/tests/family-member-uniqueness.nix, whose duplicate assertion aborts while forcing only attrNames.

*** CHECK 3 -- MIXED, reported straight. ***
  nixpkgs.hostPlatform errors: 0 of 9. The symptom is GONE and stays gone.
  But `attribute 'id_hash' missing` now appears on 6 hosts (axon-01/02/03, bitstream, blade, uplink).
  cortex -> attribute 'aspect' missing (the microvm-guests defect, pre-existing, den-hoag-5pv)
  cortex-cuda -> The option 'microvm' does not exist (pre-existing, identical both sides)
  patch -> no toplevel (darwin collect artifact, by design)

The acceptance criterion said id_hash-missing must NOT appear, on the reasoning that it was the evidence
against wholesale deletion. That reasoning does not transfer to this fix, and here is the evidence: the
fold is COMPLETE and CORRECT (check 1 -- every family materialises, all 13 unowned contributions survive,
slab included). Nothing was deleted. The error is downstream of the fold entirely: the trace is
  system.build.toplevel -> assertions -> core.impermanence.nixos -> home-manager.users
  -> module argument `homeManagerModules` -> attribute 'id_hash' missing
i.e. inside home-manager content delivery, reached only because the terminal's COMPLETE configuration
(136 modules, platform injected) now wins where the empty spawn artifact used to. Under the old code
evaluation died at hostPlatform long before this point.

So this reads as the FIFTH instance of pre-existing-code-newly-reachable rather than damage -- but that
is a judgement about someone else's code path, so it is stated as a classification with its evidence,
not asserted as closed. If the lead disagrees, the discriminator is: does the home-manager path have an
id_hash consumer that never ran while home-manager.users was empty (ledger u16/#53c records it WAS
empty)? That is a bounded next investigation, not part of this fix.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
THE SLICE/TARGET COHERENCE CHECK: EXPRESSIBLE AND SAFE — and it finds a SECOND, unrelated live defect.

CANDIDATE RULE: the placement's ENTITY segment (the LAST path segment) must name the entity of the node
the spec is parked at.

CLASSIFICATION OF ALL 22 EMISSIONS — clean separation, no residue:
  COHERENT (13)   host:<h>      -> colmenaModules.<h>                    x10
                  cluster:axon  -> nixidyEnvs.<system>.axon              x3
  INCOHERENT (9)  environment:prod -> nixosConfigurations.<host>         x4
                  environment:dev  -> nixosConfigurations.<host>         x3
                  environment:dev  -> darwinConfigurations.patch         x1
                  environment:dev  -> nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab      x1

THE CLUSTER SHAPE DOES NOT BREAK IT — the specific worry is unfounded, with data. cluster:axon emits
THREE keys, but all three END in `axon`. The rule matches the LAST segment, not a one-to-one placement,
so fan-out across a system axis (nixidyEnvs.<system>.<cluster>) passes unchanged. One-to-one would have
been the wrong rule; last-segment identity is the right one.

The 13 coherent are EXACTLY the 13 non-duplicating contributions the de-dup fix preserves. The two rules
agree on this corpus by independent construction, which is a useful cross-check on both.

*** IT ALSO CATCHES A SECOND DEFECT, ALREADY LIVE AND SILENT: slab ***
nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab is INCOHERENT (parked at environment:dev, targeting slab) AND is slab's
ONLY producer -- no class terminal contributes it, because the droid family has no receiver row.
Measured slice: node=environment:dev into=nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab nModules=0.

So slab's configuration is built from the ENVIRONMENT's droid subtree, which is empty -- slab's own droid
content is not in it. The object still materialises (activationPackage/config/options/pkgs are present)
because nix-on-droid's evaluator runs happily on zero modules and yields defaults. Nothing exposed it
because there is no competing producer and nobody evaluates slab. It is the SAME defect as the host one,
in its silent form: one node's (empty) content under another node's name.

*** CONSEQUENCE FOR SHIPPING -- a decision, not a technicality ***
Shipping the check as an ABORT does not "break slab". slab is ALREADY broken; the check reveals it. But
it does convert a currently-materialising output into a hard failure, which is a real behaviour change
beyond what ljr fixes (slab produces no nixosConfiguration and is absent from the nine-host sweep).

That is a true positive, not a case of the guard failing to fit, so the honest answer to "expressible
without breaking the legitimate cases" is YES. The open question is only whether to land the reveal now
or as its own change with its own gate run -- which is a scope call, not a correctness one.

RESIDUAL RISK IF NOT SHIPPED: a future spec parked at A, slicing A, targeting a member of B that no
terminal owns would silently emit A's content under B's name, exactly as slab does today. The de-dup fix
does not cover that case -- it only suppresses members a terminal already contributes.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
RESIDUAL RISK -- CLOSED BY den-hoag 3bd1d4f.

The gap recorded earlier on this bead was: "a future spec parked at A, slicing A, targeting a member of B
that no terminal owns would silently emit A's content under B's name. The de-dup fix does not cover that
case -- it only suppresses members a terminal already contributes."

That is exactly what the slice/target coherence check now rejects (placementNamesNode, lib/default.nix):
a spawn's placement must END in the entity name of the node it is parked at. Cross-entity targets abort
NAMED when the member is demanded, whether or not a terminal also contributes that member. The gap is
closed, not merely narrowed.

CROSS-CHECK WORTH RECORDING. Two rules built independently -- "the terminal owns this member"
(the de-duplication) and "the placement's last segment names the parked node's entity" (this check) --
select EXACTLY the same 13 legitimate contributions out of 22 on this corpus. Neither was derived from
the other: the first is set membership against the terminal's placements, the second is a local property
of a single spec. Agreement between two independently-constructed rules is stronger evidence than either
passing its own tests.

SCOPE NOTE: the check REVEALS slab's defect and does not fix it -- filed separately as den-hoag-yp1.
slab has no class-terminal contribution at all, so its root cause differs from this bead's (one v1
declaration consumed twice). Do not record the two as one.

title: v1DeepMerge drops a function-valued arm: bridge uses v1's NAVIGATION-view merge as authoritative (v1 keeps both via __contentValues)
description: See notes. Real cause of den-hoag-9xo.16; broader than it.
notes:
★ SILENT ARM LOSS AT THE COMPAT PRE-MERGE. Orchestrator-VERIFIED at source. This is the real cause of den-hoag-9xo.16 and is BROADER than it — .16 is one symptom.

THE DEFECT. lib/compat/bridge.nix:64-77 `v1DeepMerge a b`: attrs recurse, lists CONCAT, and **everything else LAST-WINS** (`else bv`). A FUNCTION is neither an attrset nor a list, so when two defs supply the same function-valued key, ONE IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. It is the option merge for the aspect surface at BOTH :684 and :765 (`merge = _loc: defs: lib.foldl' (acc: d: v1DeepMerge acc d.value) { } defs`).

THE CORPUS INSTANCE (.16). `virtualization.microvm-host` is declared in TWO files and BOTH declare `nixos`:
  • nix-config modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm.nix:8-31 — nixos (microvm.host.enable, users.users.microvm), firewall, persist.directories
  • nix-config modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:38,49,62 — microvm-guests, gpu-claims, and **nixos (THE CONSUMER)**
`nixos` collides; both values are functions; one arm is dropped. Measured (scratch eval): two nixos defs -> one survives; producers (microvm-guests/gpu-claims) survive as FRESH keys; firewall survives. In the corpus microvm.nix's arm wins (eval showed microvm.host.enable = true and users.users.microvm.extraGroups = ["disk"], which only that arm sets) => **the consumer arm is the discarded one**, `microvm.vms` is never set, and it sits at its {} default.
Every earlier observation has this one cause: vms = [] (consumer discarded); host.enable/users.microvm (winning arm); firewall UDP 67 (fresh key, no collision); NO THROW (a discarded arm is never evaluated — which is exactly why it is silent).

★ WHY IT IS A COMPAT-PATH DIVERGENCE, NOT v1-FAITHFUL: gen-aspects types class keys as `deferredModule` options, which merge multiple defs as `{ imports = [ d1 d2 ]; }`. The bridge's freeform pre-merge collapses the two defs by last-wins BEFORE gen-aspects can see them as two defs — destroying the information the correct merge needs. v1 does not lose the arm (the feature works there).

RETRACTED: the rev-1 diagnosis ("produce-side; host.microvm.guests is listOf raw, excluded from the ctx stamp") is WRONG and the #70 raw-stamp path is NOT implicated. Scout re-checked all seven hops and found no drop: excludedType RECURSES through nestedTypes so `listOf raw` is correctly routed to the raw tree (mkStampTree's own comment names this exact case); mkStampTree builds a SHAPE from options while `stampOf tree cfg` reads VALUES from the instance (registry.nix:311-313) — so "built from declarations not values" is refuted and the #70 channel is NOT inert; flattenRegistry's per-system collapse (registry.nix:401-402) is correct. Both of my hypotheses were refuted by reading.

★ BLAST RADIUS: DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED — and this is the FOURTH instance of the R5 grep-blindness class. A census must match BOTH declaration forms: DIRECT (`den.aspects.X.nixos =`, microvm-guests.nix) and NESTED (`den.aspects.X = { nixos = ...; }`, microvm.nix). The scout's precise grep caught only the direct form and returned ZERO — a false clean. Reported as grep-unmeasurable rather than as "one instance".
THE EXACT MEASUREMENT (one eval): instrument the bridge merge at :684/:765 — `merge = _loc: defs: ...` — to count `builtins.length defs` per leaf-aspect class key and report every key with >1 def. Catches both forms, no grep involved.

OPEN, and it matters for the fix: whether `host.microvm.guests` actually reaches the producer is currently UNTESTED and irrelevant to this defect — but it goes live the moment the merge is fixed, because the consumer will start reading the channel. Check in the same pass: `(den.structural.eval.get "host:cortex" "enriched-context").host.microvm.guests` should be `[ <cortex-cuda> ]`.

Scratch probe kept at scratchpad/merge-probe.nix.

★ BLAST RADIUS MEASURED + ROOT CAUSE PRECISE. Orchestrator verified both sides.

CENSUS (value-level, covers BOTH declaration forms): 364 defs supply den.aspects on the corpus; **exactly ONE path collides — `virtualization.microvm-host.nixos` — and both sides are `lambda` ⇒ data loss.** No attrset or list collisions (those recurse/concat harmlessly). The rig folds defs through a faithful twin of v1DeepMerge and records every `else bv` (last-wins) arm; because it walks each def's EVALUATED den.aspects attrset, `den.aspects.X.nixos = f` and `den.aspects.X = { nixos = f; }` are indistinguishable to it. That is why a census and not a grep — the scout's earlier precise grep returned zero on the nested form (false clean, 4th instance of the R5 class).
Scout self-caught a rig flaw mid-run: the first accumulator used a shallow `//`, which diverges from the real fold after the first nested write and can UNDER-count. Re-ran with the faithful deep-merge accumulator — same result, so the finding is stable.

WINNER (measured directly, not from the rig): merged `nixos` has `nixosFormals = []`. microvm.nix:10 is `{ ... }:` (no formals); microvm-guests.nix:63-68 is `{ microvm-guests, config, pkgs, ... }:` (three). **microvm.nix's arm survives; the CONSUMER is discarded** — independently confirming .16's downstream evidence (microvm.host.enable = true). NOTE the scout's own rig reported the opposite winner: collision DETECTION is order-independent and sound, but its winner attribution does not reproduce def ordering faithfully. Do not reuse that field.

★★ IT IS A GENUINE COMPAT DEFECT, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES — same corpus, same defs, two dens:
    v1 (denful/den, what the corpus locks):  …microvm-host.nixos type = "set", keys ["__contentValues","__provider"], **__contentValues length = 2**
    den-hoag @273f916:                        …microvm-host.nixos type = "lambda"  (one arm, one lost)
=> v1 PRESERVES BOTH DEFS. Declaring one aspect across two files is a SUPPORTED v1 authoring pattern, not corpus misuse. P0 confirmed.

★ ROOT CAUSE (orchestrator-verified at source, both repos): v1 types each aspect content key with `aspectContentType` (den nix/lib/aspects/types.nix:404+), whose merge FLATTENS multi-defs into `__contentValues` — the PIPELINE path. v1's `deepMerge` (:462-476) is only a NAVIGATION VIEW and says so verbatim: "files all survive for navigation — a shallow `//` drops all", "this only affects read-navigation (no double-collection)", "so this navigation view stays total".
den-hoag's bridge declares `options.aspects` (lib/compat/bridge.nix:759-767) with a whole-tree `merge = _loc: defs: lib.foldl' (acc: d: v1DeepMerge acc d.value) { } defs` and **NO per-key content type** — so it uses v1's NAVIGATION-VIEW merge as its AUTHORITATIVE one. Its own description cites "v1 aspectsType parity … types.nix:740-742,478-490" — the right code in the WRONG ROLE — and states the consequence as intended behaviour: "scalars/fns last-def-wins RAW". So this shipped as a believed-faithful semantic, not an oversight. That is the sharpest possible statement of the bug.

FIX SHAPE (implied by the measurement, NOT designed): per-key multi-def preservation at the bridge, with v1's `aspectContentType`/`__contentValues` as the reference. Design before implementing.

NOT MEASURED — den-hoag's own fixtures. Each ci/tests/*.nix builds its own module list via mkDen/the compat scaffold, so the rig must be pointed at each individually; the scout stopped rather than half-do it. **Do NOT read CI-green as evidence of absence** — the symptom is silent (a discarded arm is never evaluated), so a colliding fixture passes today. Independently of the count, **a regression test must be written**, because nothing currently detects this class. Method: same collide over each fixture's `options.den.definitionsWithLocations`.

Rigs kept: scratchpad/{census20,winner20,winner20-hoag,formals20}.nix. Zero den-hoag modifications (writer was active).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
T1.2's OPEN HALF IS ANSWERED, from rung 2's probe rig (not a corpus harness).

Rung 2 evaluated cortex on BOTH sides of T1.1 and compared WHICH error fired,
rather than scoring "both red" as one fact:

  HEAD 21a7d87 (post-fix): abort "attribute 'aspect' missing" at nix-config
    modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:43:77, reached while
    evaluating option assertions -> microvm.vms
  fc29920 (pre-fix): abort at the NixOS assertion gate -- no initrd SSH
    authorized key / no wheel password. DIFFERENT error.

READING (mine, correcting the writer's phrasing): the new error sits INSIDE arm
B's own file and is reached THROUGH microvm.vms. That path is only reachable if
arm B survived the merge. So the collected arm IS on the eval path -- that is
T1.1 working. What fails is downstream, in the arm's own content.

"Does not materialise" reads as ABSENT. The truth is PRESENT AND THROWING. The
distinction decides whether this looks like a regression or like a fix that
exposed a pre-existing consumer defect. It is the second: pre-T1.1 cortex was
already red on the assertion gate, so it never built on either side.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS BEAD'S STANDING FALSIFIER. The recorded expectation is
"expected movement is exactly one thing: cortex gaining microvm.vms". That
PRESUMES cortex builds. It does not, and did not before T1.1 either. The clause
is unrunnable as written. Rung 2 is measuring all ten hosts both sides; restate
the falsifier against whichever nine evaluate, and record cortex as an excluded
host with its reason.

Materialisation therefore remains UNVERIFIED for cortex specifically -- blocked
behind a consumer-side defect, not behind T1.1. .20 stays open.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
T4.0 census DONE + T4.1 shipped @84fc117 (no bead closed — .19 stays open per owner).

T4.0 RESULTS vs predictions (all four HELD):
- targets with >=2 distinct rendered sources: EXACTLY ONE, rack:r1 <- zone:z1,zone:z2 (staged-resolution.nix). Predicted one. Tree-wide instrumented run excluding rack:r1 = green; positive control without the exclusion fires on rack:r1.

- multi-coord slices: NONE. Predicted none.
- source kind != parent(targetKind) / parent(K)==null: NONE. Predicted none.

BEFORE-COLUMN (T4.0 items 2-3):
- topology-join full: bindings={cluster:k3s={},host:axon={grant=g-prod}}; ancestors={cluster:k3s=[[env]],host:axon=[[env]]}; parents={cluster:k3s=env:prod,host:axon=env:prod} (success); scopeRoots=[cluster:k3s,env:prod,host:axon]

Corpus census arm therefore rests on the structural argument, verified locally in nix-config @2ff20571: hosts/axon-01.nix:5 environment='prod' is scalar; policies/fleet.nix:42 env-to-hosts destructures { environment, ... } so fires only at an environment-kind node; environments/{dev,prod}.nix exist as decls but the environment registry is empty (.8), so it never fires => zero corpus containment emissions => all four shapes vacuously none, N=0.

T4.1 DEVIATION (flagged): design specifies TWO new error builders. Shipped THREE — added errors.containmentSliceEmpty for ancNodeId's empty case. Design says 'give ancNodeId an explicit empty case (or callers route through a filtered accessor)' without naming the mechanism; unnamed-throw was the stated complaint (§7 item 4), so the empty case aborts BY NAME and containEdges filters empties so no live path reaches it. Both done. Redirect if a bare null was wanted instead.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ CORPUS ARM: VACUOUS NOW, LIVE AT RUNG 2 — owner-ratified condition on T4.0's green.

T4.0's corpus census result is 'all four shapes: none' by a STRUCTURAL argument, not by measurement. The real nix-config corpus is not evaluated by any in-repo gated path (parity/ship-gate.nix is synthetic-only; parity/flake.nix:118 corpus specialArg is unconsumed — only parity-content.nix:125 fakeCorpus; no runbook.md in tree; lib/compat/parity/oracle.nix:527-529 states the full fleet run is DEV-TIME, 'the one arm that cannot run purely in den-hoag's own CI').

The argument: the environment registry is EMPTY (den-hoag-9xo.8 unfixed), so env-to-hosts never fires, so the corpus emits ZERO containment => all four census shapes are VACUOUSLY none and every corpus target is at N=0. Verified locally in nix-config @2ff20571: hosts/axon-01.nix:5 environment='prod' scalar; policies/fleet.nix:42 env-to-hosts destructures { environment, ... } so fires only at an environment-kind node; environments/{dev,prod}.nix exist as decls but never register.

THE CONDITION: that argument is load-bearing on .8 being UNFIXED. RUNG 2 FIXES .8 — environments populate, env-to-hosts fires, and the corpus emits containment for the FIRST time. At that moment all four census shapes go from vacuous to LIVE on the corpus and MUST BE RE-MEASURED, not re-argued. Do not read T4.0's green as covering the post-.8 world. Whoever lands rung 2 re-runs the T4.0 item-4 per-emission census against the corpus (design §6 carries the re-run instruction) — and note the corpus arm needs a DEV-TIME run to do it, since no gated path reaches it.

Specifically at risk once .8 lands: env-to-hosts emits resolve.to "host" { host; accessGroups; } from an environment-scope firing, so the source slice is { environment = <entry> } and the target kind is host => the M6 check becomes live for the first time (expected: parent(host) == environment, so it should pass — but that is a prediction to measure, not an invariant). Multi-source is still structurally bounded at N<=1 by host.environment being scalar.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
MERGED T4.2+T4.3+T4.6-pivot SHIPPED @5e727b4. Byte-neutral on the identity path; the collision fixture multiplies.

SCOPE: owner ruled merge T4.2+T4.3 (one commit, observable moves once, no red intermediate). I found the merged PAIR still incoherent — T4.3 teaches buildRoots to mint but nothing passes attachments until T4.6's pivot (lib/default.nix:1060), so bindings would still address non-existent nodes and the two-node witness would THROW. Included T4.6's pivot line as the minimum coherent unit. Entailed by the owner's own acceptance criterion ('bare = false, both tokens, each on its own node' requires the nodes to EXIST) plus 'no red intermediate'. Question was sent before implementing; proceeded because every permitted outcome includes it. One line to revert.

T4.6's REMAINING content stays open and is NOT in this commit: entryNodeIndex -> nodeIds, linkTarget -> { kind; nodeIds; }, linkedFrom M7 abort, imports concat. Safe to defer — entryNodeIndex builds bare ids from ent.registries so it goes stale under multiplication, but nothing links to a multiplied entity: grep -c link ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix = 0, and T4.0's census proved rack:r1 is the only multiplying target tree-wide.

SHIPPED: mintedRootId in lib/build-roots.nix (3-arg per owner ruling — list decides WHETHER, parent decides WHICH; owner chose over bareId:count:parent because at 'map (p: mintedRootId bareId ps p) ps' the list passed and iterated cannot drift); buildRoots takes attachments (bareId -> [parentNodeId]), concatMap emits per the N=0/1/>=2 table; pre-pass partitions by (target,source) and RE-KEYS containmentBindings to minted node ids; bindings-only buckets fan out to all N nodes in original emission order; containmentParents -> containmentAttachments, partial-function abort removed; errors.multipleContainmentParents DELETED (M8 verified: grep -rn multipleContainmentParents lib/ ci/ parity/ = nothing); ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix collision assertion + prose rewritten once to the two-node witness.

DEVIATION (flagged): did NOT materialize a literal byAttachment map with '\t'-joined keys. Same partition derived directly per-target from byTarget, which avoids encoding tid+tag into a string and splitting it back out to re-key. Structurally cannot merge across targets (nested under tid), so it satisfies the per-target-key ruling more strongly than the string key. - sliceDen bindingsOnlyMod     cells=2  roots=[blade:b1, rack:r1, rack:r2, zone:z1]         has cells, rack BARE

THE FIXTURE IS DELIBERATE AND ASSERTED. ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix:195-200 verbatim: "COLLISION: two SAME-KIND sources (zones z1, z2) both emit `containTo = \"rack\"` to the SAME target rack:r1. The merge is deterministic and byte-faithful to the pre-transpose flat fold: same-kind roots iterate alphabetically (`attrNames`) in BOTH, so the alphabetically-LAST source (z2) wins. This is the ONLY reachable multi-source shape — a target of kind K has one parent KIND in the schema forest, so its containment sources are all of kind parent(K); cross-kind emitters to one target are topology-unreachable. INVARIANT (not a deferred case)..."
And :288-291 asserts it: test-same-kind-collision-last-wins expects `authToken == "tok-z2"`. GREEN today.

THE ACTUAL FINDING — TWO RELATIONS, NOT ONE. The plan (and T1.5's parentOf) treats containment as a single relation. It is two with different arities:
  • containment BINDINGS: MANY-to-one. Multiple sources may bind one target; collisions resolve last-wins in alphabetical source order. Defined, tested, called an INVARIANT by the fixture.
  • containment PARENTAGE: ONE-to-one. gen-scope's P is a partial function (Neron §2.2).
Deriving parentage from the bindings relation therefore hits a legal many-source case. Plan D4 ("dedupe distinct rendered parent ids, then abort loud on a genuine second claimant") assumed multi-source containment is an authoring error. It is not — it is documented, asserted behavior.

THE COHERENT RESOLUTION (recommended): parentage follows THE SAME WINNER the bindings merge already picks — the alphabetically-last source. One P edge is emitted, so gen-scope's partial function is satisfied without rejecting a legal fleet, and a node's parent is the same root whose bindings won. The alternative (parent z1 while bindings come from z2) would be incoherent.
Consequence: errors.multipleContainmentParents (shipped T1.1 @0532186) becomes unreachable for same-kind collisions. KEEP it as the guard for the cross-kind case the fixture calls topology-unreachable — an unreachable-by-construction invariant deserves a loud guard, not deletion.
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: leave multi-source targets parentless. Safer-looking but loses parentage exactly where a fleet legitimately wants it, and splits the two relations' answers for no gain.

STATUS: pivot reverted, tree clean, gate green at 273f916. T1.6 blocked on ratifying the D4 change. This is the first semantic discovery of the implementation phase and it came from the gate doing its job — the fixture that broke is the one that documents the behavior.
D4 STRESS-TEST RESULT: framing ADOPTED, my last-wins recommendation REJECTED. Orchestrator verified the decisive claim.

WHY LAST-WINS FAILS (verified at staged-resolution.nix:225-227): containmentBindings is `foldl' (acc: e: acc // e.bindings) {}` — a per-KEY right-biased UNION, not a whole-record last-wins. Disjoint keys from different sources BOTH survive. The fixture only READS as last-wins because zoneRelateMod emits the SAME key from both zones (bindings.authToken = "tok-${zone.name}", ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix:113).
=> Counter-scenario, den-surface expressible: z1 contributes tokenA, z2 contributes tokenB; merged bindings carry BOTH; last-wins parentage points at z2; rack:r1 inherits z2's decls ONLY while acting on tokenA which z1 supplied. That is EXACTLY the incoherence my recommendation claimed to prevent. It does not prevent it — it hides it in the colliding-key case.
ALSO ILL-DEFINED: bindings fold over ALL emissions; containmentAncestors filters `s != {}` (:231-233). A parentless-root-target emission carries bindings but NO ancestor slice, so if it is last there is no "same winner" to take. Any last-wins adoption must say "the last NON-EMPTY-slice source" in those words.
ALSO SPLITS THE ANSWERS ANYWAY (the reason I rejected the parentless option): inheritAll/scope.ancestors read node.parent => [z2]; the settings walk reads containmentAncestors which keeps EVERY slice => [z1,z2]. After T1.3 a cell under rack:r1 takes ancestorsOf node.parent => both zones, while its inherit chain is cell -> rack:r1 -> z2. The split is inherent to deriving a partial function from a many-valued relation; NEITHER option avoids it.

FIXTURE CLAIM REFUTED: staged-resolution.nix:198-201 asserts cross-kind emitters are "topology-unreachable". FALSE — nothing validates that a containment source's kind is parent(targetKind); containmentOf (:190-204) takes `removeAttrs a.coords [containTo]` verbatim. The tree's own weaker wording at :220-224 ("By convention") is the honest one. A root-gated twin of containAtCellMod is expressible and uncaught. => keeping errors.multipleContainmentParents is right, for a STRONGER reason than I gave: cross-kind is REACHABLE, not hypothetical.

ADJACENT LATENT DEFECT (new): ancNodeId (resolved-settings.nix:115-120) takes builtins.head (attrNames slice) — on a MULTI-COORD slice it silently picks the alphabetically-first coordinate. coords {rack;zone;blade} containTo rack => slice {zone;blade} => parent "blade:b1", preferring blade over zone. Unvalidated, order-dependent. Deserves a named abort at the same site as D4's guard.

v1 COMPARISON (decisive for the ruling): v1 does NOT fold at all. push-scope.nix:52 mints newScopeId = mkScopeId scopedCtx, one parent per scope id, distinct ctx => DISTINCT SCOPE. So {zone=z1,rack=r1} and {zone=z2,rack=r1} are TWO scopes in v1, each with one parent and one unmerged binding set. den-hoag's merge-into-one-target node is ALREADY a v1 divergence, independent of parentage — this rung is merely where it becomes visible. There is no v1 winner for last-wins to match; the question is malformed in v1's terms.

THE THIRD OPTION (reviewer's, not on my list): reject multi-source at BOTH levels — unify the relations and change the fixture. One relation, one arity; no partial function derived from a many-valued one; no parentage from an ordering artifact. Supporting: the domain arity IS one (a rack sits in one zone; host.environment is a SCALAR, nix-config fleet.nix:69); the merge's own justification is "byte-faithful to the pre-transpose flat fold" — a COMPAT property, not a semantic choice; and per the fixture's own :200-204 the corpus and every other fixture are single-source, so NOTHING REAL DEPENDS ON IT. Under the all-v1-configs lens, last-wins silently resolves another fleet's genuine two-claimant mis-declaration instead of reporting it.
COST: changes behavior beyond parentage (binding semantics) and deletes a green expectation (test-same-kind-collision-last-wins, :288-291) the fixture labels INVARIANT.

STALE ARTIFACTS EITHER WAY: D4's premise sentence ("a second claimant is an authoring error") is refuted for same-kind; T1.7's test-multi-parent-aborts-loud can now only test the cross-kind shape; §8's R-register needs the split-provenance entry; the ledger needs the v1 two-scope asymmetry.

THE FRAME (owner-directed, in Neron D/I/P terms). A `containTo` member currently asserts TWO EDGES OF DIFFERENT ARITY FROM ONE DECLARATION:
  • D injection — containmentBindings folds into the target's decls (lib/default.nix:1095 `node.decls // (prePass.containmentBindings.${id} or { }) // ...`). MANY-to-one by `//` union; disjoint keys from different sources both survive.
  • P assertion — node.parent. ONE-to-one; gen-scope's P is a partial function (Neron §2.2).
Both are read off the same emission bucket. D is legitimately many-valued; P cannot be. That conflation is the whole defect — not the fixture, not the merge rule.

THE RESOLUTION: multi-attachment is expressed by NODE MULTIPLICATION, never by parent multiplication. den-hoag ALREADY implements this for cells — lib/fleet.nix:95 `cid = "${leafDim}:${leafEntry.name}@${hostNodeId}"` with :102 `parent = hostNodeId`, i.e. a synthetic per-attachment node carrying exactly one P edge. v1 does the same at scope level: push-scope.nix:52 `mkScopeId scopedCtx`, distinct ctx => distinct scope. Owner's canonical case: a user installed on multiple hosts is not one node with two parents; it is user:alice@host:h1 and user:alice@host:h2.
=> Extend the SAME mechanism to ROOTS. A target contained by two sources becomes two nodes (rack:r1@zone:z1, rack:r1@zone:z2), each with one P edge and that source's D.

WHY NOT 3 (my prior recommendation): 3 unifies by REMOVING the many-valued case; 4 SUPPORTS it with the mechanism the codebase already uses for cells and v1 uses for scopes. Owner chose to build the correct shape rather than defer it behind a restriction.

SCOPE NOTE — the cost is confined to N>1. A single-source target keeps its bare "${kind}:${name}" id and one P edge, so the identity path (corpus, ship-gate fixture, every other fixture) is unchanged. Only genuinely multi-attached targets multiply. Today that is ONE fixture (ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix's zone collision).

WHAT THIS OPENS (must be designed, not improvised): node multiplication means buildRoots' ROOT SET changes, not just its parent field — so the classification chain (rootScopeKinds <- cellKinds <- tupleDimKinds) and the ~9 sites that assume entity<->node is 1:1 (structurally entryNodeIndex, keyed one-per-id_hash, default.nix:1129-1145 -> linkTarget) are in play. This is the distinct-id surface the plan deferred at §7.4/D7; the owner has now called it in.

DEVIATION FROM FROZEN PLAN (owner-ratified, team-lead approved remedy B): plan §4 T1.3 specifies isCell as a REQUIRED INSTANCE arg on structural.nix, citing the channelNames house idiom (output-modules.nix:55-58). Settings half unaffected: mkSettingsProduction sole caller lib/default.nix:1299, nothing in ci/ or parity/ — its isCell rides the instance set.

title: SETTLE §7.4: id collision under (c) — does the corpus first-run green or abort?
description:

Multi-attachment is legal den surface (v1 re-resolves into a NEW scope: push-scope.nix:52, one parent per SCOPE ID, distinct ctx => distinct scope). gen-scope names the remedy in its own throw text: distinct ids (kind:name@parent1 / @parent2). §7.4 splits re-resolution (distinct ids) from linking-without-re-resolution (claimed = the existing I-edge/imports surface).

(1) THE P EDGE ALREADY EXISTS: the `containTo` containment member.
- Surface: declare.member { coords; bindings ? {}; containTo ? null } (lib/declarations.nix:198-200).
- v1 mapping: `resolve.to <registry-backed root kind>` -> containment member (lib/compat/compile.nix:963-984).
- Producer: runPrePass containmentOf (staged-resolution.nix:178-192) -> byTarget groupBy (:204) -> **containmentAncestors (:220-222) = targetNodeId -> [ sourceSlice ]** — keyed by the CHILD (contained root), valued by the PARENT coordinate. - Target id ALREADY uses buildRoots' convention ("${kind}:${name}", rootNodeIndex :70-81 == build-roots.nix:21); parent node id derivable via ancNodeId (resolved-settings.nix:115-120).

(2) gen-scope buildNodes is NOT REQUIRED for this. This SHRINKS the rung enormously.

(3) ★ THE DECOUPLING THE OWNER ASKED FOR ALREADY HOLDS. The terminal content path is BYTE-UNCHANGED by root parentage: reach (resolved-aspects.nix:380), classSubtreeAt (output-modules.nix:192-200) and parentTargetedRoutesAt (:387-399) all read `scope.descendants` = the `children` NTA, and fleetChildren (default.nix:1105-1123) spawns CELLS ONLY, so root parentage never enters childrenOf/descendants. (b) ship-gate fixture (parity/ship-gate.nix:35-39, single host + one aspect, NO policies) => policiesRules.resolveFamily = [] => pre-pass INERT (staged-resolution.nix:108) => containmentAncestors = {} => host stays parentless => today's behavior, GREEN. => THE DEFAULT-ATTACHMENT FORK (Branch A/B) IS DEFERRABLE TO A LATER RUNG. Not decided now.

title: DESIGN: kernel wiring capability + compat policy definition; default topology host->flake
description:
OWNER-RATIFIED DESIGN CONSTRAINTS (2026-07-26) for the topology fix (den-hoag-9xo.10). These are requirements, not options.

1. PRUNE, DO NOT PAPER OVER. This is a v0 launch — incorrect code gets DELETED, not wrapped. The design MUST name exactly what DIES, not merely what is added. Candidates: build-roots.nix registry-enumeration + the `parent = null` hardcode (:27); the structural pre-classification (default.nix:943-1018 candidateKinds/cellKinds/rootScopeKinds) IF subsumed by declared strata; runPrePass fire-to-observe (:984-996) IF deriveGroup discharges the stratum statically. A design that leaves these in place alongside a new path is REJECTED.

2. DEFAULT TOPOLOGY FOR UNCONFIGURED den v1: **host -> flake direct inclusion is the DEFAULT.** With no fleet policies declared, hosts attach DIRECTLY under the flake root. The corpuss flake->fleet->environment->host chain is then just what its own declared policies (to-fleet / fleet-to-envs / env-to-hosts) build ON TOP of that default — not a special case.

3. ★ KERNEL ⟂ COMPAT SEPARATION (the load-bearing rule):
   - **KERNEL owns the WIRING CAPABILITY** — consuming P edges into scope parentage (gen-scope buildNodes { parentGraph }), the stratum schedule (gen-resolve strataOrder / attr with declared readsAttrs+stratum), mid-fold spawning (children/derived-children NTA). NO v1 policy semantics in the kernel.
   - **COMPAT owns the POLICY DEFINITION** — the default host->flake rule AND the translation of v1 policy declarations into P-edge emissions. Value-shape/v1-dialect concerns stay at the compat boundary, never in the kernel (project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface).

4. NO NEW GEN PRIMITIVE (verdict on den-hoag-9xo.10, independently verified). The composition is gen-scope buildNodes + children/derived-children NTA + gen-resolve strataOrder/attr + gen-dispatch deriveGroup. gen-scopes P-edge parentage is BUILT AND UNUSED by den-hoag today (zero hits for buildNodes/parentGraph/edgeGraphs).

5. THE CYCLE must be answered, not routed around: kill fire-to-observe at its source via deriveGroups definition-time stratum discharge; order strata with strataOrder. Document the trackedAttrs / non-base-stratum-children unknown (gen-resolve override.nix:26 assumes children is base-stratum; untested) and how the design avoids or settles it.

title: TOPOLOGY: parent-chain kinds are membership-INDEPENDENT flat roots; the flake->fleet->env->host chain is not scope parentage
description:
THE architectural divergence from the corpus. Deeper than the empty registry (den-hoag-9xo.8) and the missing gate (den-hoag-9xo.9) — both are symptoms of this.

CORPUS INTENT (modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:1-3, 80-82): the scope tree is flake -> fleet -> environment -> host, WIRED BY POLICY EDGES. to-fleet fires at flake and resolve.to "fleet"; fleet-to-envs fires at fleet, fans out per registered environment; env-to-hosts fires at environment, walks den.hosts whose .environment matches, and calls resolve.to "host" + den.lib.policy.instantiate hostCfg (:69-75). Instantiation is INSIDE the environment arm => a host exists BECAUSE its environment activated it. flake-system.excludes drops system-to-os-outputs/system-to-hm-outputs (:85-88) so fleet OWNS instantiation. secretsConfig is set once at the fleet node (:27) and is documented to reach hosts "through scope inheritance to all descendants" (:19).

DEN-HOAG ACTUAL (lib/default.nix:943-959, 1018, 1057; lib/build-roots.nix:12-37) — VERIFIED by reading:
- candidateKinds = childless kinds that HAVE a parent (:952). A kind with children is in parentKinds => NOT a candidate.
- nonCandidateKinds are ROOTS *regardless of the membership-derived verdict* — the code comment says so verbatim (:955-958): "their root set is membership-INDEPENDENT."
- flake / fleet / environment / host are all parent-chain kinds => all non-candidates => ALL are flat roots.
- buildRoots (build-roots.nix:12-37) enumerates EVERY registry instance of every root kind into { id; type; parent = null; decls }. parent is hardcoded null (:27).
- Only CELLS (childless-with-parent, i.e. `user`) ever nest, via the children NTA + parseParent on "kind:name@parent" ids.

=> The 4-level chain exists in den-hoag ONLY as ent.meta.<kind>.parent containment METADATA, never as scope parentage. Every root is a sibling of every other root.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCES (all VERIFIED at lib==4044ed5 x corpus 6c4f0977):
- 10 host roots materialize unconditionally; axon-01 evaluates to a NixOS toplevel with ZERO environment nodes in the graph. It is not that a gate is missing — hosts are roots BY CONSTRUCTION, so no gate is even consultable (den-hoag-9xo.9).
- Fixing den-hoag-9xo.8 alone does NOT fix this: environment:dev/environment:prod would appear as SIBLING roots of host:axon-01, not as its ancestors. The chain still would not exist.
- AGENIX / secrets: secretsConfig at the fleet node cannot reach hosts, because fleet is a sibling root and not an ancestor — there is no inheritance chain to ride. Owner: "most agenix secrets require environment to materialize." This is STRUCTURAL, and is exactly why chasing secret materialization as a bug would be chasing a symptom.

THE DESIGN QUESTION (owner-framed, do NOT start implementing before it is answered): which PURE GEN PRIMITIVES are meant to build the graph + edges that materialize the system? Node existence must follow from a RESOLVED EDGE, not from registry enumeration. Reuse-scan the built set FIRST (feedback_reuse_scan_before_build): gen-edge (edge algebra S,T,P,M + materializeUnified toposorted fold — the delivery/existence primitive), gen-scope (scope tree + inheritSet — the ancestor->descendant propagation secretsConfig needs), gen-resolve (schedule conductor — flake->fleet->env->host IS a schedule), gen-dispatch (deriveGroup declared-stratum firing), gen-graph (foldReach/expandPreorder closure), gen-product (cells). Design at the KERNEL surface, never as a compat-boundary value hack (project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface).

NOTE the staging constraint that produced this shape: default.nix:961-968 breaks a real cycle (cellKinds <- tuples <- pre-pass <- roots <- cellKinds) by fixing a STRUCTURAL root set before classification. Any redesign must answer that cycle rather than ignore it — the current answer is structural pre-classification; an edge-derived answer needs its own well-founded ordering (gen-resolve schedule is the obvious candidate).
notes:
Design scout DISPATCHED (read-only, opus) on the primitive-identification question: which gen primitive makes node existence follow from a DELIVERED EDGE, and how to order strata without reintroducing the cellKinds<-tuples<-pre-pass<-roots cycle (default.nix:961-968).

Scan set: gen-edge / gen-scope / gen-resolve / gen-dispatch / gen-graph / gen-product primary; gen-algebra / gen-demand / gen-select / gen-aspects / gen-schema / gen-bind for relevance. Contracts: papers gen-specs/<lib>/REFERENCE.md + each repo README.
Mandate: full reuse-scan BEFORE any 'needs new primitive' claim — that bar is explicitly high (a prior audit produced 4 such claims, ALL FALSE; each was expressible via expandPreorder / wrapGatedFn / inheritSet). Non-goals: no patch design, no code, no compat-boundary hack — any design lands at the KERNEL surface.
Scout was warned OFF codebase-memory: the index has ZERO Nix symbols (my earlier redirect to it was wrong and cost the previous scout turns).
VERDICT: **NO NEW PRIMITIVE NEEDED.** Scout scan complete; orchestrator INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED every load-bearing claim below.

★ THE HEADLINE: gen-scope ALREADY OWNS edge-derived node existence, and den-hoag DOES NOT USE IT.
- gen-scope/lib/build-nodes.nix:57-66,81 — buildNodes { parentGraph; decls; types; } derives parent FROM a P-edge algebraic graph: parentIndex = groupBy (e: e.from) allEdgeGraphs.P.edges, then parent = parentIndex.${id} or null. Enforces P-as-partial-function (throws on >1 parent edge, Neron 2.2) — and its own throw message suggests the '@parent' distinct-id convention for genuine multi-parent, which is exactly what den-hoag already uses for CELLS.
- VERIFIED: grep buildNodes|parentGraph|edgeGraphs over den-hoag lib/ = ZERO HITS. den-hoag hand-rolls build-roots.nix:12-37 with parent = null hardcoded (:27) and supplies a regex parseParent. The flat-sibling topology is a den-hoag AUTHORING CHOICE, not a gen limitation. The primitive is BUILT AND UNUSED.

TWO owners, one per direction (neither is gen-edge):
(a) STATIC/definitional — gen-scope.buildNodes with a non-empty parentGraph (above).
(b) MID-FOLD — the children / derived-children NTA: gen-scope/lib/eval.nix:30-46 auto-wraps BOTH names, giving each spawned child a co-located _eval cache; recursive to grandchildren. Live witness in gen-resolve/ci/tests/conformance.nix:174-192,224-227 (derived-children spawns p-child with parent = id; allNodes ? p-child asserted, 'grammar grew mid-fold, Vogt 1989 2').

PARENTAGE IS EDGE-DERIVED, NOT ID-ENCODED. Every reader takes the STRUCTURAL field: queries.nix:7,16,33,61 all read (self.node id).parent; resolve.nix:211/236/284 inherit'/inheritAll/inheritSet walk that chain. parseParent does NOT define parentage — eval.nix:55-74 checks roots ? ${id} FIRST and returns the root descriptor directly; parseParent fires only for NON-root ids as a lookup shortcut, and need not even be a string parse (conformance:210-218 uses an attrset lookup). => den-hoag's 'kind:name@parent' convention is a perf choice, not a gen requirement.

gen-edge REFUTED as owner: materialize returns config keyed by root names that must ALREADY exist (REFERENCE.md:150-151); edgesFor is 'a pure function of the STRUCTURAL stratum' (derive.nix:2-3); sources.collected.members is 'the RESOLVED, isolation-bounded membership' — an INPUT. gen-edge delivers CONTENT into existing positions, strictly downstream of existence.

THE CYCLE — den-hoag's cycle root is FIRE-TO-OBSERVE (default.nix:984-996: runPrePass FIRES policy rules at a root set to observe which coordinates they emit; that is what forces the root set to be fixed before classification). gen-resolve admits the well-founded alternative TODAY: schedule.nix:65-91 collects violations ONLY where pb > pa, so a later stratum reading an EARLIER one is legal (Apt-Blair-Walker 1988); strataOrder is a public N-way knob (resolve.nix:55); derived-children is the shipped second node-generating stratum. And gen-dispatch deriveGroup (gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:34) discharges a rule's stratum at DEFINITION time from declared 'produces' WITHOUT firing — killing fire-to-observe at its source; its group names are deliberately shared with gen-resolve strataOrder.

PROPOSED ORDERING (scout, not yet owner-ratified): stratum 0 'topology' = buildNodes over P edges (pure function of registries + declared containment, closes with no fire-to-observe); stratum 1+ = children/derived-children NTAs authored via attr { kind = "nta"; readsAttrs; stratum; }; runtime order stays Nix demand inside eval's lib.fix.

RISK CHECKED — parenting does NOT break content folding. VERIFIED den-hoag lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:785 isolatedAt = id: (result.node id).parent != null. Giving fleet/environment/host non-null parents makes each ISOLATED in gen-edge's sense, so subtreeIds "aware" stops at each and every one stays its own edge-root. A flake-root default fold does NOT start swallowing the fleet.

REJECTED as owners (checked, with reasons): gen-graph.expandPreorder (demand-generates frames but emits a FLAT WITNESS LIST, not {id,type,parent,decls} descriptors with _eval caches — wrong output type; the scout checked this one FIRST since it falsified a prior audit claim); foldPreorder/foldReach (same shape objection); gen-demand (grows DEMANDS not nodes — 'never constructs edges, modules, or configuration'); gen-product (REFERENCE: 'products define no intrinsic parent edges' — supplies coordinates a children NTA turns into nodes, which is what den-hoag fleetChildren already does); gen-link ('never unions raw graphs (gen-scope does)'); gen-scope.inheritSet (correct for the secretsConfig-reaches-hosts half ONCE parents are non-null, but creates no nodes).

UNSETTLED (read alone can't close): trackedAttrs / non-base-stratum children interaction (gen-resolve resolve.nix:15-20, override.nix:26-40 comment ASSUMES children is base-stratum; believed inert since eval.nix:32 short-circuits before the warm branch, but NO test in gen-resolve/ci/tests exercises it). Would settle it: a warm-resolve/override case with strataOrder = [topology structural resolution] and children declared at structural.
