title: Hosts instantiate WITHOUT environment activation (axon-01 must be gated by prod)
description: OWNER-RATIFIED: a host must NOT be initialized without activation. TWO declared facts den-hoag ignores: (1) environment activation (env-to-hosts filters hostCfg.environment == environment.name); (2) intoAttr = [ ] — the standalone-output opt-out for EMBEDDED/GUEST hosts (cortex-cuda is a microvm guest of cortex, cortex.nix:14). Both ignored because hosts materialize by REGISTRY ENUMERATION -> scope root -> native nixos class terminal, not by activation. Per 9xo.14 the gate must target THAT path, not instantiate. Half (2) is independently fixable and testable NOW (assert cortex-cuda absent from nixosConfigurations); half (1) waits on 9xo.10/9xo.12.
notes:
★ OWNER REFINEMENT + LIVE WITNESS (2026-07-26): cortex-cuda is an EMBEDDED MICROVM HOST. VERIFIED: nix-config modules/den/hosts/cortex.nix:14 `microvm.guests = [ den.hosts.x86_64-linux.cortex-cuda ];` (option declared at modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm.nix:43 "Guest MicroVMs to run on this host. List of den hosts").

So `intoAttr = [ ]` at hosts/cortex-cuda.nix:5 ("do not emit a standalone nixosConfiguration output") is not a preference — it is the DECLARED OPT-OUT for a host that exists ONLY as a guest delivered INTO cortex. den-hoag emits it standalone anyway.
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: nix eval .#nixosConfigurations --apply builtins.attrNames over the corpus returns ["axon-01","axon-02","axon-03","bitstream","blade","cortex","cortex-cuda","uplink"] — cortex-cuda IS there.
=> the guest config materializes via TWO paths: embedded into cortex (the microvm guest delivery) AND standalone at the flake top level. The standalone one is built off the registry-enumerated root, i.e. WITHOUT the guest-delivery context.

★ THIS WIDENS 9xo.9: there are (at least) TWO corpus-declared activation/opt-out facts den-hoag's registry-enumeration -> root -> native-class-terminal path ignores:
1. ENVIRONMENT ACTIVATION — env-to-hosts filters on hostCfg.environment == environment.name (fleet.nix:69); no environment nodes exist, so nothing filters.
2. intoAttr = [ ] — the standalone-output opt-out for embedded/guest hosts. Per 9xo.14's settled trace, den-hoag's ONLY intoAttr consumers are the option declaration (registry.nix:165-192), a CLI attr-path builder (nh.nix:26), and the parked-spec placement path (default.nix:2313). NOTHING in the native terminal path reads it as a gate.

Both are the same defect shape: a host materializes because it is IN A REGISTRY, not because anything ACTIVATED it. Per 9xo.14 Q4 the gate must target the registry-enumeration -> root -> terminal path (NOT instantiate — gating instantiate would not touch host materialization at all).

RELATED PRIOR ART (check before designing the fix): den v1 keeps a delivered-child route mechanism — route reinstantiate + id_hash re-key for guests (den #111 / the delivered-child route fix). The guest path is a KNOWN v1 mechanism, so den-hoag's gap is likely that it never implemented the delivered-child route rather than that the semantics are undecided.

★ IMPLICATION FOR SEQUENCING: 9xo.9 now has a LIVE, REPRODUCIBLE symptom that needs NO part of the topology arc. `intoAttr = [ ]` gating is independently fixable and independently testable (assert cortex-cuda absent from nixosConfigurations). The environment-activation half still depends on 9xo.10/9xo.12.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CORTEX-CUDA MEASURED, 2026-07-27, with den-hoag-9xo.8's fix applied (environments now register).

Every other host root acquires an environment parent; cortex-cuda does NOT:
  host:axon-01/02/03, uplink                 -> environment:prod
  host:bitstream, blade, cortex, patch, slab -> environment:dev
  host:cortex-cuda                           -> null

And this is NOT a missing-field case -- cortex-cuda's registry entry carries environment = "prod",
same as axon-01/02/03/uplink which all parented correctly. So the source field is present and the
containment edge still did not form for this one host. That is the .9 shape stated precisely: it
materializes without being gated by its environment, and now there is a measurable structural
witness for it rather than only a behavioural complaint.

Also measured, independent of the above and present on BOTH sides of the .8 fix (so not caused by it):
cortex-cuda is the one host whose drvPath eval fails with
  "The option `microvm' does not exist. Definition values: - In <gen-merge>, via option cortex-cuda.nixos"
distinct from the cortex microvm failure tracked on den-hoag-9xo.20 / den-hoag-5pv.

Separately: `slab` is in the host registry (registrySizes.host = 10) but emits NEITHER a nixos NOR a
darwin configuration -- 9 configurations exist for 10 registry hosts. Absent on both sides of both the
.8 fix and T1.1, so it is long-standing. It does parent correctly (-> environment:dev).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CAVEAT ON THE CORTEX-CUDA CONTROL (2026-07-27) — it is a control BY ACCIDENT and it EXPIRES.

In den-hoag-ljr, cortex-cuda is the single nixos host that is NOT contributed twice to
nixosConfigurations, and that correlation is what identified the containment attachment as the source of
the second contribution:

  duplicated (7): axon-01 axon-02 axon-03 bitstream blade cortex uplink   -- all have an environment parent
  NOT duplicated: cortex-cuda                                            -- parent = null

cortex-cuda stays single ONLY because its parent edge failed to form, which is THIS issue. It is not
evidence that some hosts are legitimately single-contributed, and nothing about it is by design.

WHEN .9 IS FIXED, THE CONTROL EXPIRES: cortex-cuda will acquire environment:prod as a parent (its
registry field already says environment = "prod") and will then duplicate exactly like the other seven.
Do not later read "cortex-cuda was single" as a counter-example to the duplicate-member analysis, and do
not treat a fix that leaves it single as correct.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER COMMENT ON THIS BEAD (2026-07-27). A fact I recorded here was WRONG.

I previously wrote that slab "emits NEITHER a nixos NOR a darwin configuration" and summarised it as
"9 configurations for 10 registry hosts". The count is right; the CONCLUSION drawn from it was not.

slab DOES emit a configuration: nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab. My check enumerated only
nixosConfigurations and darwinConfigurations -- it was FAMILY-BLIND, so a host in a third family read as
producing nothing. That is the same predicate-blindness failure this arc keeps hitting: the predicate did
not cover the space it claimed to.

Why it mattered rather than being a harmless slip: on the strength of "slab emits nothing", suppressing
the parked-spawn arm at spawn-creation time looked safe. It is not. slab's ONLY producer is that spawn
(the droid family has no receiver row, so no class terminal contributes it), and site-1 suppression would
have DELETED slab's configuration outright. The wrong fact nearly justified the wrong fix; the measurement
that caught it was the placement breakdown in den-hoag-ljr.

Corrected statement: 10 registry hosts -> 10 configurations, across THREE families --
  nixosConfigurations   8  (all hosts except patch and slab)
  darwinConfigurations  1  (patch)
  nixOnDroidConfigurations 1 (slab)
The .9 defect for slab is NOT "emits nothing". Separately measured and filed on den-hoag-ljr: slab's
emission is INCOHERENT (parked at environment:dev, targeting slab) and its slice is nModules=0, so slab's
configuration is built from the environment's empty droid subtree rather than slab's own content -- a
silent wrong-content defect, not an absent-output one.

cortex-cuda remains correctly described: it has parent = null despite environment = "prod", and it is
contributed by the class terminal only.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
CORRECTION (2026-07-27): cortex-cuda's parent = null is NOT a defect, and this
bead's framing of it as one is WRONG. Also corrected: the orchestrator relayed
"the containment edge failing to form is a separate, still-live defect" as
fact. It is not.

The corpus gate is a CONJUNCTION, nix-config modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:69:

  lib.optionals ((hostCfg.environment or "prod") == environment.name
                 && hostCfg.intoAttr != [ ]) [
    (resolve.to "host" { host = hostCfg; inherit accessGroups; })
    (den.lib.policy.instantiate hostCfg)
  ]

cortex-cuda SATISFIES the environment conjunct ("prod") and FAILS the
intoAttr != [ ] conjunct, so the policy deliberately emits no attachment for
it. Working as declared.

MEASURED, exact correlation: it is the ONLY corpus host declaring
intoAttr = [ ] (grep over modules/den/hosts/ -> one hit) and the ONLY host with
parent = null. Mechanism from source: build-roots.nix:8-11 "a root is
parentless unless the caller names its attachments", fed by containmentAncestors
from containTo members (staged-resolution.nix:111).

So it is not a third defect and not half (1)'s inverse -- it is half (2)'s SAME
declared fact seen on the attachment side.

★ THE TRAP THIS CREATES, and it is why the shape was reported before coding:
implement half (1) as "filter enumeration by environment match" and cortex-cuda
is excluded FOR THE WRONG REASON -- its environment matches; it is the intoAttr
conjunct that excludes it. The exclusion would look correct while reasoning
from a mechanism that is not the one operating.

--- HALF (1) RULING (orchestrator, 2026-07-27) ---

MATERIALISATION FOLLOWS REACHABILITY, NOT ATTACHMENT:
    a node materialises iff it is REACHABLE FROM A DECLARED ROOT.

Rejected: attachment-driven ("a policy attached it"). The KERNEL CANNOT DEPEND
ON A CORPUS POLICY EXISTING -- a kernel-native fleet has no env-to-hosts, and
under a strict attachment rule its hosts would all vanish. Reachability is a
property of the graph, so it needs no policy.

Reachability also states the corpus's own intent structurally (flake -> fleet ->
env -> host: the host materialises BECAUSE it is reachable through the chain;
the policy is merely how v1 spells the edge), and excludes cortex-cuda for the
RIGHT reason -- unreachable because nothing attached it, not by reading
intoAttr.

It survives .14's counter-example: corpus batteries/colmena.nix:93-104 emits
instantiate UNGATED with no resolve.to beside it, so "whoever attaches,
instantiates" is a corpus authoring convention, NOT a framework guarantee.
Under reachability that spawn is parked at a host node and fires if the host is
reachable -- the rule never has to claim attachment implies instantiate.

WHAT DIES (per .12's prune-do-not-paper-over): build-roots.nix's unconditional
"every registry instance is a root". A registry instance becoming a root MERELY
BY EXISTING is the structural reason BOTH halves of .9 were ignored -- hosts
materialise by registry enumeration, so the policy that computes attachment
never governs materialisation.

Half (2)'s emitsNamedResult placement gate (ab1112a) MAY BE SUBSUMED and should
then be deleted -- two mechanisms for one fact. PROVE subsumption before
deleting; if reachability alone leaves cortex-cuda absent it is redundant, if
not they are two facts and both stay.

SEAMS ARE DIFFERENT AND MUST NOT BE MERGED: half (2) gates the family
PLACEMENT (late, artifact deliberately survives -- intoAttr says where a result
LANDS, not whether it is produced). Half (1) gates ROOT CONSTRUCTION, where
parentage now lives; activation is the stronger claim, "not initialised" rather
than "not published". A placement gate for half (1) would leave a
non-activated host fully built and merely unpublished -- papering over.

ACCEPTANCE: the seven currently-materialising hosts must ALL be reachable, and
the enumeration must change by EXACTLY cortex-cuda.
FALSIFIER: if any of the seven is not reachable, the formulation is WRONG --
stop and report, do not add an exception. An exception list is the name-list
lie one level up.

title: ROOT: _registryKinds = {} — ingest kind-discovery misses environments/clusters
description:
THE live blocker upstream of both #52 and F3. Framework-correctness defect in the compat ingest boundary, NOT a corpus problem: the corpus surface is FINE (fleetEnvironmentNames = [dev prod], fleetClusterNames = [axon], envIsInstanceRegistry = true, entries carry id_hash).

MEASURED MECHANISM (VERIFIED by scout, decisive numbers independently reproduced by orchestrator):
- _registryKinds = {} while _entityStamps keys = [clusters environments groups hosts] => consumerRegistryKeys non-empty => registryKindOf IS CALLED, and returns null for all three.
- Why null: envSubOptionKeys / clusterSubOptionKeys / groupSubOptionKeys are ALL []. bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf yields {} => identityKeysOf {} = [] => hash mismatch.
- Fallback: ingest drops to the VALUE-marker path, which catches groups (34) but MISSES environments and clusters (0/0).
- Consequence chain: no environment/cluster nodes => zero environment:*/cluster:* scope roots => env-to-hosts cannot fire => prePass.containmentBindings = {} => no accessGroups on any root => no human user cells (only 2 cells exist, both sini@patch/slab) => #52 empty edge set + F3 nothing to deliver.

The option-reflecting registry-kind fix (registryKindOf/_registryKinds, bridge.nix:292/340, registry.nix:355, ingest.nix:481) IS in-tree but INERT over this corpus. git log c82b729..HEAD over bridge.nix/registry.nix/ingest.nix is EMPTY - no den-hoag change since the diagnosis rev, so this is not a regression introduced after it.

=> F3 blocker-table row #1 ("Empty env/cluster registries - SHIPPED") must be RE-OPENED: the fix exists but does not work over this corpus.

OPEN QUESTION (UNVERIFIED, blocks the fix design): when did options.den.<registry>.type.getSubOptions stop yielding sub-options? Ruled OUT: the corpus gen-schema bump e6dbe8e7->c6331f30 (one commit, feat(refined): re-export checkRefinements). Would settle it: bisect corpus history for when getSubOptions went empty. Determines whether the fix belongs in den-hoag subOptionsOf, in gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry, or in how the corpus declares these registries.

NORTH-STAR FRAMING: this is NOT a corpus-eval chase. Kind-discovery that cannot reflect an option-declared registry is a compat-boundary correctness defect - the value-marker fallback is precisely the kind of v1 holdover the arc exists to dissolve.
notes:
★ OWNER-RATIFIED (2026-07-26): the registry sizes are WRONG — environment MUST populate (corpus declares dev + prod). den-hoag's current behavior is BROKEN, not merely incomplete. Raised to P0.

Owner also states a SEPARATE semantic requirement this exposes: **axon-01 must NOT be initialized in the config without being activated by its environment (prod).** Today it is: 10 host scope roots materialize and axon-01 evaluates all the way to a NixOS toplevel with ZERO environment nodes in the graph, so no activation gate exists to hold it back. Split to a sibling bead — same root, distinct correctness requirement (populating the registry alone does not create the gate).
RE-SCOPED by den-hoag-9xo.10: fixing the empty environment registry is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT. environment:dev/prod would appear as flat SIBLING roots of host:axon-01 (buildRoots hardcodes parent = null), so the flake->fleet->env->host chain still would not exist and hosts would still materialize unconditionally.
★ OWNER RULING (2026-07-26): NO BISECT. den-hoag is a GREENFIELD implementation — _registryKinds was most likely NEVER populated correctly, per how the gen module system was built. This is not a regression with a last-good commit; it is a path that never worked. Drop the 'when did getSubOptions stop yielding sub-options' line of inquiry entirely.

RE-SCOPED: investigate bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf against how gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry ACTUALLY exposes sub-options — i.e. was the option-reflecting kind-discovery ever correct against the real gen-schema surface, or was it written against an assumed one? Fix belongs wherever that mismatch actually lives. Per the prune mandate: if the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover this never-working path, it is DEAD CODE to delete, not a fallback to preserve.
★ ROOT CAUSE FOUND — confirms the owner's greenfield call exactly: this path NEVER worked. No bisect could have found a last-good commit. All VERIFIED by orchestrator.

THE CHAIN:
1. registry.nix:369 `ikeys = identityKeysOf opts`; :373-375 gates on `hashIdentity k ikeys (...) == carried id_hash`. With ikeys empty the hash never matches => hits empty => registryKindOf null.
2. identityKeysOf (registry.nix:330-345) reflects the DECLARED OPTION SURFACE — needs opts.<n>.type.name / .internal / .identity.
3. It gets opts from bridge.nix:248 `subOptionsOf k = t.getSubOptions ["den" k]`, guarded by `if t == null || !(t ? getSubOptions) then <empty>`.
4. ★ gen-merge NEVER IMPLEMENTS getSubOptions ON ANY TYPE. attrsOfWith (gen-merge lib/types.nix:198-225) builds via mkOptionType { name; elemType; nestedTypes; merge; } — no getSubOptions. submodule (:142-168) sets getSubModules + substSubModules — no getSubOptions. mkOptionType's normalization (:122) then DEFAULTS it: `getSubOptions = t.getSubOptions or (_prefix: <empty>)`.
   => the field EXISTS (so den-hoag's `t ? getSubOptions` guard PASSES) but returns an EMPTY ATTRSET UNCONDITIONALLY. den-hoag takes the else-branch and gets nothing.
   => opts empty => ikeys empty => null for EVERY kind. Systemic, not env/cluster-specific.

WHY IT LOOKS ENV/CLUSTER-SPECIFIC: registryKindOf returns null for ALL kinds; the VALUE-marker fallback then silently covers hosts+groups (34) and misses environments/clusters. The fallback masks a TOTAL failure of the option-reflecting path.

THE TELL — the accommodation was made ONE LEVEL TOO SHALLOW. registry.nix:327-329 verbatim: "nixpkgs names primitives str/int/bool, gen-merge string/int/bool — both accepted". The author KNEW gen-merge types were in play and handled the type-NAME difference, but not that gen-merge implements no getSubOptions at all. Written against nixpkgs lib.types introspection semantics (attrsOf.getSubOptions delegates to elemType; submodule.getSubOptions returns evaluated sub-options) over a merge-plane library that never had them.
Per that same comment the hash gate makes a wrong key set "a LOUD miss (null), never a misclassification" — true, but the value-marker fallback converts that loud miss into a SILENT one end-to-end.

FIX CANDIDATES (choose before implementing; A is the route-through-gen-native shape):
(A) den-hoag reads the identity surface from gen-schema's KIND RECORD instead of reflecting the merge-plane option type. gen-schema mkInstanceRegistry's guard requires `kindValue ? options` (instance.nix:274-277) and entry-type.nix:166 says the kind result carries them "so mkInstanceRegistry can consume them automatically". gen-schema DECLARES the identity surface; re-deriving it by type reflection is the duplication. NO gen change. NEEDS ONE VERIFICATION: does den.schema.<kind>.options carry .type.name/.internal/.identity as identityKeysOf requires?
(B) gen-merge implements getSubOptions faithfully on attrsOf/submodule (nixpkgs parity). A real parity gap — BUT gen-merge deliberately exposes `nestedTypes` as its walker accessor instead (listOf:174-176 verbatim: "nixpkgs-parity introspection alias — lets a consumer's type-tree walker recurse unchanged"), so adding getSubOptions may be out of character. ALSO a gen-lib change => owner-confirmed requirement only, never pre-authorized.

PRUNE NOTE: if (A) lands, the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover a path that never worked => DEAD CODE per the owner's prune ruling, not a fallback to preserve.
FIX (A) IS AVAILABLE AND NEEDS NO GEN CHANGE — the declared option surface is ALREADY COLLECTED in-tree, one scope away from the consumer that needs it.

VERIFIED: lib/compat/bridge.nix:496-498
  rawOptionsOf = kindName: lib.foldl' (acc: d: lib.recursiveUpdate acc ((d.${kindName} or { }).options or { })) { } schemaDefs;
That is the merged DECLARED option surface per kind, taken from the schema DEFS — exactly what identityKeysOf (registry.nix:330-345) reads (.type.name / .internal / .identity). Corroborating: gen-schema entry-type.nix:230 `options = userOptions` — the kind record carries them; ingest.nix:249 passes tree.config.den.schema.<kindName> into mkInstanceRegistry.

=> THE FIX: registryKindOf's `opts` should come from the kind's DECLARED options (rawOptionsOf-shaped), not from bridge.nix:248 subOptionsOf's `t.getSubOptions` type-reflection, which is dead on arrival because gen-merge implements getSubOptions on NO type (it defaults to `_prefix: {}` at gen-merge/lib/types.nix:122).
Threading note: rawOptionsOf lives in a `let` around bridge.nix:488 (the belt section); subOptionsOf is at :248. Different scopes — the rung must thread the value or hoist the helper. Small, but not literally one line.

RESIDUAL RISK (settle during implementation, degrades SAFELY): rawOptionsOf reads each def's inline `.options` only. If a kind's identity fields arrive via kind IMPORTS (rawImportsOf, :494-495) rather than inline options, the key set is incomplete. Per registry.nix:327-329 the hash-equality gate makes a wrong key set a LOUD MISS (null), never a misclassification — so an incomplete set fails closed, it does not mis-attribute. Settling test: compare identityKeysOf(rawOptionsOf k) against the keys gen-schema's mkIdentityModule actually hashed, for environment/cluster/group/host.

PRUNE CONSEQUENCE (owner ruling): once (A) lands and registryKindOf resolves for every kind, the VALUE-marker fallback exists only to cover a path that never worked => DELETE it, do not keep it as a fallback. Its presence is what converted registryKindOf's loud null into a silent end-to-end miss.

SEQUENCING: independent of the topology rung (different plane — ingest/identity, not scope parentage). Can land before, after, or in parallel. Note it is UPSTREAM of the corpus chain in effect: with environment/cluster registries empty, env-to-hosts has no environment root to fire at, so containmentAncestors stays empty for env->host and the topology rung has nothing to thread for those links. **Rung 1 will be exercised by whatever containment members DO fire; the corpus's flake->fleet->environment links need .8 fixed to appear at all.**

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
R2.0 STOPPED, correctly, past where the plan predicted. Plan's R2.2 remedy
source (rawOptionsOf) is EMPTY for all ten kinds -- corpus declares kind options
under den.schema.<kind>.imports, never .options, 5/5 kind files. R2.2 as written
would have shipped a silent no-op and passed.

Absence is trustworthy: known-positive on the SAME fold (rawImportsOf returns
1/1/1/1/7, host 7) proves the fold is live, so the empty result is real and not
a blind predicate.

Correct surface MEASURED: merged instance option surface (den-hoag's existing
hostInstanceOptions pattern, registry.nix:384) + withInjectedName reproduces the
carried id_hash for all three kinds:
  clusters     ikeys ['environment','name']
  environments ikeys ['domain','id','name','timezone']
  groups       ikeys ['description','name']
Without name: no match anywhere.

RULING: route (a) -- implement getSubOptions on gen-merge, completing the
nixpkgs mkOptionType protocol. bridge.nix:509-514 already names that completion
as this seam's RETIREMENT CONDITION (verified verbatim by orchestrator). Route
(b) would re-implement a gen-merge capability inside compat and deepen the seam
we plan to delete. (a) dissolves, (b) mimics.

OWNER AUTHORIZED THE GEN-MERGE PUSH (2026-07-27). Direct to main, no PR.
Authorization covers the change, NOT a shortcut past proof. Push gated on, in
order: C2 consumer census, C1 ikeys reproduction, gen-merge's own suite (its
checks.default is a homegrown asserter not nix-unit -- expectedError CRASHES
the gate), docs in the same commit (README + gen-specs/gen-merge/REFERENCE.md,
THEORY citations), format. Then den-hoag pin via
  nix flake lock ./ci --update-input den-hoag/gen-merge
NEVER nix flake update on the parent.

C1 falsifier: any ikeys deviation -- including a different membership that
still matches id_hash -- is a STOP, not an expectation to adjust. The claim
that withInjectedName becomes unnecessary is DERIVED, not measured.

DO NOT retire the bridge seam in this rung. Record whether the retirement
condition is now met and what still blocks severance; separate decision, own
blast radius.

Also settled at R2.0: R2.4 measured EARLY and PASSES (host parent ==
environment, cluster -> environment, user -> host; both silent `or null`
defaults benign) -- retires E2's misleading-abort risk. R2.1 premise VERIFIED:
the existing marker test builds zoneOpts from nixpkgs submoduleWith, which
DOES implement getSubOptions; the real path is gen-merge, which does not.
That is exactly why .8 survived a green suite -- the test could not fail for
its own reason.

Anchor drift: plan validated @fc29920, HEAD 21a7d87. All bridge.nix anchors
+26 (subOptionsOf :248->:274 etc). registry.nix + ingest.nix anchors unchanged.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AND FIXED UPSTREAM (2026-07-27). Not a den-hoag defect.

gen-merge lib/types.nix:122 completed the nixpkgs mkOptionType protocol with
  getSubOptions = t.getSubOptions or (_prefix: { });
a stub on EVERY type. Only field PRESENCE was pinned (ci/tests/nixpkgs-protocol.nix
test-protocol-complete), never behaviour. Correct for a leaf; on a STRUCTURAL type it reports
"declares nothing" indistinguishably from a type that genuinely declares nothing. The hash gate then
fails CLOSED (null = "not this kind"), which is why this was silent.

FIX: implement getSubOptions on gen-merge submodule / attrsOf / listOf. gen-merge commit 8daa25d
(local; push pending owner-authorized go-ahead). ZERO den-hoag edits required.

MEASURED, corpus, with the fix:
  registryKinds  {} -> {clusters=cluster, environments=environment, groups=group}
  registrySizes  environment 0->2, cluster 0->1, host 10->10, group 34->34
  scopeRoots     44 -> 47, gaining exactly cluster:axon, environment:dev, environment:prod
  identity keys  cluster ['environment','name']; environment ['domain','id','name','timezone'];
                 group ['description','name']  -- each reproduces the carried id_hash
  den-hoag gates ci=0, parity=0, ship-gate=0/true

*** DEPLOYMENT CHAIN -- THE FIX DOES NOT FLOW THROUGH den-hoag's GRAPH ***

The corpus builds its registries with its OWN inputs.gen-schema (nix-config
modules/den/schema/cluster.nix:97, environment.nix:140), so the option types the bridge reflects are
NIX-CONFIG's, not den-hoag's. Verified by overriding ONLY gen-schema/gen-merge -- den/gen-merge left
at its pin -- and that alone fixed it.

  Shipping end-to-end = gen-merge -> gen-schema -> NIX-CONFIG lock.
  den-hoag's own bump serves only its fixtures (the R2.1 witness).

This confirms the bridge seam comment's claim that the type half is the corpus's, at its pin.

VERSION NOTE. nix-config's gen-schema/gen-merge is pinned at f7e3afb -- exactly the base of the fix --
so the override introduces ONE commit and nothing else (no confound). den-hoag's gen-merge is
2701d8bb, FIVE commits behind, so a den-hoag bump pulls those five in as well; classify that delta
separately, it is not part of this fix.

*** DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE -- NEW, ATTRIBUTED, NOT YET DIAGNOSED ***

With environments materializing, host scope roots acquire parents for the first time:
  host:axon-01/02/03, uplink -> environment:prod
  host:bitstream, blade, cortex, patch, slab -> environment:dev
  host:cortex-cuda -> null   (ANOMALY: its environment field IS "prod" -- see den-hoag-9xo.9)
axon-01's root decls also gain accessGroups, so containment bindings are now delivering.

But all nixos hosts then fail EARLIER than before:
  before: "Failed assertions:" (initrd SSH key / wheel password)
  after:  "Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set"
ATTRIBUTION CONTROL RUN: the same path-override pointed at f7e3afb WITHOUT the getSubOptions change
reproduces "Failed assertions:", so the override mechanism is not the cause -- the change is.
Localized to lib/compat/flake-module.nix:288-290:
  hostEntry = bindings.host or null;
  sys       = if hostEntry == null then null else systemFor hostEntry;
  sysModule = if sys == null then [ ] else [ { nixpkgs.hostPlatform.system = sys; } ];
The host registry's own system field is INTACT and identical before/after (axon-01 = x86_64-linux), so
the field did not vanish. Which of the two is null -- bindings.host or systemFor's read -- is NOT yet
distinguished; downstream reads all cascade from the single hostPlatform error, so a probe of
networking.hostName is inconclusive and was not treated as evidence.

This is a den-hoag defect newly EXPOSED by parented hosts, not a gen-merge defect. It does not affect
any corpus build until nix-config's lock moves, so it does not gate the gen-merge push -- it gates the
nix-config bump.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
THE SEAM'S RETIREMENT CONDITION WAS NEVER A REAL GATE (2026-07-27).

lib/compat/bridge.nix:509-514 names the pass-through seam's severance condition as "once the consumer's
gen-schema is PROTOCOL-COMPLETE -- pins a gen-merge at/past the mkOptionType nixpkgs-protocol
completion". That condition was ALREADY SATISFIED before any of this work: gen-merge
ci/tests/nixpkgs-protocol.nix test-protocol-complete asserts field PRESENCE over the 14-field surface
and was green, because completeType stamped getSubOptions -- as a stub.

So a condition written to gate severance was met by a type surface on which one of its methods answered
"declares nothing" for every type. A completeness gate that tests PRESENCE and not BEHAVIOUR does not
gate anything. This is the same failure mode that kept .8 silent for den-hoag's whole life:
presence-checked, behaviour-unchecked.

MEASURED, so severance can be decided on data rather than argument: under the fix, belt
(passThrough = true) vs severed (passThrough = false) produce IDENTICAL corpus output -- registrySizes,
registryKinds, metaParents, rawSchemaParents all equal; scopeRoots 47 vs 47.

STILL BLOCKING SEVERANCE -- do not retire the seam on the strength of that:
 1. The seam's own bar is corpus-RESULT equivalence and there is NO OBSERVABLE: zero of nine
    configurations produce a toplevel drvPath. The comparison above is structural only.
 2. The in-code severability witness's second half ("activated with the types work") is not activated;
    no CI witness pins belt == severed.
 3. passThrough is a bare bridge ARGUMENT, not a den.features gate -- severance today is a code edit,
    not a flag flip. The comment's "passThrough makes the severance one flag" is aspirational until it
    actually is one; per the feature-flag/removability convention this wants a real den.features.<name>.
 4. Structural equality measured on THIS corpus (three consumer registries) -- not a general proof.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
R2.1 PREREQUISITE ANSWERED (2026-07-27): the targeted bump moves the WRONG NODE. R2.1 would be a false
witness.

den-hoag ci/flake.lock carries TEN gen-merge nodes across THREE revs:
    2701d8bb  x4   (gen-merge, _4, _6, _9)
    fa5d5cc2  x4   (gen-merge_2, _5, _7, _10)
    fdbf140b  x2   (gen-merge_3, _8)

R2.1's fixture builds its registry through mkInstanceRegistry, which comes from den-hoag's gen-schema.
Resolution path, measured:
    root.den-hoag              -> den-hoag
    den-hoag.gen-schema        -> gen-schema_3
    den-hoag/gen-schema.gen-merge -> gen-merge_5  = fa5d5cc2f56d

But the instructed bump, `nix flake lock ./ci --update-input den-hoag/gen-merge`, moves the node
`den-hoag.gen-merge` = gen-merge_4 = 2701d8bb -- a DIFFERENT node that the fixture never resolves
through. Bumping it would leave the fixture evaluating against fa5d5cc2, which has the stubbed
getSubOptions, so a reshaped R2.1 would report the defect as still present (or pass for an unrelated
reason) while the pin it was supposed to exercise had not moved at all.

That is the same class as the ORIGINAL .8 defect surviving a green suite: the witness exercising a
surface other than the one under test. Here it would have been the marker fixture reading a gen-merge
that never changed, instead of a nixpkgs submoduleWith.

CORRECT TARGET for R2.1 to be trustworthy:
    nix flake lock ./ci --update-input den-hoag/gen-schema/gen-merge
(and verify afterwards that gen-merge_5, not gen-merge_4, carries 8daa25d). Whether the other eight nodes
should also move is a separate question -- they feed other libs' own gen-schema/gen-aspects chains and are
not what R2.1 exercises. Do NOT run a bare `nix flake update`.

STILL HELD: the bump is not run. This comment records the prerequisite answer only.
