GATE PASS 1 — VERDICTS (independent adversarial reviewer, fresh context, 2026-07-27). Read-only.
FIRST EXERCISE OF THE GATE. Outcome: 1 REDESIGN, 1 REJECTED-with-reason, 1 new live-code finding.

★ PATH ERROR, ORIGINATING IN W1 AND PROPAGATED BY THE ORCHESTRATOR'S DISPATCH.
W1 cited lib/compat/concern-policies.nix. NO SUCH FILE. It is lib/concern-policies.nix — a KERNEL file,
enumerated in ci/tests/boundary.nix:37 coreFiles. The dispatch then reasoned "lib/compat/ IS the compat layer
by construction, so 'it lives in compat' is not automatically a defect" — CORRECT REASONING APPLIED TO THE
WRONG LOCATION. probeOf, the 3-way branch, mkExpanded and mkDeclaredSlices are ALL KERNEL. Only the 5-entry
TABLE is compat, and the kernel takes it as a parameter (:99, default { } at :444) so boundary guard 2 holds —
but the hazard is reachable from the PUBLIC KERNEL OPTION den.producesByName (lib/default.nix:981-987), not
only via compat.

════ CANDIDATE A — REDESIGN ════
STATED FINDING REJECTED. A DIFFERENT, STRONGER DEFECT AT THE SAME SITE: CONFIRMED — AND IT INVERTS W1's
POLARITY.

Why the stated finding fails: the den surface IS expressible without the table. Measured against kernel
internal.compilePolicies with NO compat table, a policy carrying __produces = ["member"] on its value gives
ids=["p3"] groups=["structural"] produces=[["member"]] — one rule, bare name, group stamped at definition
time, identical to the table path. den.producesByName is a PUBLIC KERNEL OPTION defaulting to { }; the kernel
is name-agnostic (compile = compileWith { } [ ] [ ] { }); the table is injected only at the compat seam
(lib/compat/default.nix:143, flake-module.nix:560). A v1 body is an opaque closure whose kinds cannot be
detected, so compat owning that fact is the documented legitimate boundary (same precedent as
resolve-family-names.nix). AND branch 3 is GEN-NATIVE, not a v1 holdover — gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:31
"A rule without produces (declared = null) is returned UNCHANGED: undeclared means 'infer as before'." That is
gen-dispatch's own undeclared-rule path.

★★ THE REAL DEFECT, MEASURED — POLARITY REVERSED. Policy named env-to-hosts (a table key), value-conditional,
body emits `member` (structural) AND `edge` (resolution). Net declarations across all compiled rules, real ctx:
    noTable_fanFallback    (branch 3): ["member","edge"]   <- TOTAL, nothing lost
    withTable_declaredPath (branch 2): ["member"]          <- edge SILENTLY DROPPED
BRANCH 3 IS THE SOUND BRANCH; BRANCH 2 IS THE LOSSY ONE. W1 called branch 2 "the real dissolution" and branch
3 "the un-dissolved blind fan" — on TOTALITY that is backwards.
MECHANISM: mkDeclaredSlices (lib/concern-policies.nix:305-319) instantiates slices only for DECLARED groups;
mkSlice's produce filters builtins.filter (a: declare.stratumOf a == s) (:267). Emissions outside the declared
family are filtered into nothing. gen-dispatch then skips validation BY DESIGN — gen-derive dispatch.nix:104-107
"Declared rules are trusted." Name-keying is what makes a WRONG declaration reachable: compile.nix:93 stamps
__produces on ref.name ALONE, and flake-module.nix:560 installs the 5-key table for EVERY compat consumer with
no check that the body matches.
NOT HYPOTHETICAL: ~/Documents/repos/den-configs/nixfos/ independently defines env-to-hosts
(modules/den/policies/fleet.nix:42) and env-users (users.nix:93) — two of the five keys. The kinds happen to
match. COINCIDENCE, NOT VERIFICATION. No CI coverage: every __produces test
(compat-policy-expansion.nix:421,451,498) declares kinds that MATCH the body.

RUBRIC: C1 VIOLATED — gen-dispatch's declared-stratum trust presupposes the declaration is the BODY AUTHOR's
statement about their OWN body (what makes gen-resolve's per-equation stratum sound); a name-keyed EXTERNAL
table violates that precondition. C2 — single violation is total: the trust result does not transfer at all
for table-supplied declarations. C6 FAIL — no mechanism makes violation impossible, no named abort, and the
asymmetry is decisive: resolveFamilyNames has a loud twin (resolveFamilyUntagged), excludeFamilyNames likewise
(excludeFamilyUntagged), PRODUCESBYNAME HAS NO TWIN GUARD — which the file's own "the resolveFamilyNames twin"
framing CONCEALS.
STANDING BAR: the table is NOT disqualified as v1-compat convenience — it is a defensible compat boundary. The
disqualifying part is THE MISSING GUARD.
IF IT ENTERS AFTER REDESIGN, CITE: criterion (6) invariants documented but unenforced; site
lib/concern-policies.nix:305-319 + :267; provenance gen-derive/lib/core/declared.nix:22-34 +
dispatch.nix:104-107 (declared-rules-are-trusted and its precondition). NOT ABW.
DESIGN QUESTION TO RESOLVE FIRST: fire-once verification, or a loud untagged/mismatch catch mirroring
resolveFamilyUntagged, or make trust conditional on same-author provenance.

════ CANDIDATE B — REJECTED ════
Mechanism reproduces exactly (:171-188, `if try.success then try.value else [ ]`, called :345 for every
policy). THE CONSEQUENCE CLAIMED DOES NOT.
 1. "Broken policy degrades instead of aborting named" — FALSE. Fired at real ctx: fire1 = CAUGHT-THROW. The
    throw is NOT swallowed; it is deferred to FIRE TIME with the body's own message. tryEval affects
    CLASSIFICATION ONLY, never execution.
 2. The misroute is DECLARATION-PRESERVING: a genuinely single-group policy that throws at the sentinel gives
    net ["structural:member"] — identical to the honest single-group compile. Only rule count and produces
    differ. The documented "expansion is the CONSERVATIVE branch" claim (:43-44) holds empirically.
 3. The ONE semantics-changing case ABORTS NAMED: a misrouted enrich policy fired gives ABORTED-LOUD via
    errors.expansionEnrich (lib/errors.nix:146-148), text naming policy and cause. C6 SATISFIED — defined
    violation behaviour, named abort, not "by convention".
 4. The asymmetry is Nix's tryEval semantics, DOCUMENTED AS AN HONEST LIMIT (:27-30) with a named escape hatch
    (sentinelFields :62-64, :134-144). Measured: the missing-attr arm escapes even an OUTER tryEval and aborts
    the whole eval NAMING THE OFFENDING BODY LINE. W1 framed it as the hazard; it is the arm with the BETTER
    diagnostics.
REASON RECORDED SO IT CANNOT BE RE-PROPOSED: probeOf's tryEval is a CLASSIFICATION-only guard. Measured: the
throw survives to fire time; the misroute preserves net declarations exactly; the sole semantics-changing case
(enrich) aborts named via errors.expansionEnrich. C6 discharged. RE-PROPOSAL REQUIRES a measured case where a
declaration is LOST or a wrong answer is PRODUCED — not merely misclassified.
CARVE-OUT, not a defect: a misrouted enrich policy silently leaves the enrich FEED (nEnrichFeed 1→0) because
mkSlice hardcodes __isEnrich = false (:268); it goes loud only when fired at a matching node. Defensible ("if
it mattered, it aborts"). Revisit only if the enrich feed gains a non-fire consumer.

════ INCIDENTAL — THE ABW GLOSS IS LIVE KERNEL CODE, NOT JUST PROSE ════
Rubric rank-1 confirmed independently against the texts. THREE SITES: den-hoag REFERENCE.md:83 states the
over-strict rule ("a predicate may depend only on strictly-lower strata", also mis-naming ABW as "local
stratification"); REFERENCE.md:101 states it CORRECTLY ("positive same-stratum reads are permitted", a wide
gate "would false-reject"); gen-resolve REFERENCE.md:40 also correct ("Positive dependencies at strata <= own
are admitted"). den-hoag:83 contradicts the other two.
★★ AND IT IS IMPLEMENTED IN THE VERY FILE BOTH CANDIDATES OCCUPY: lib/concern-policies.nix:101-102 restates
the wrong rule VERBATIM and :129 implements it as `stratumIndex.${ks} >= r -> throw`, applied by BOTH branches
via projectedBase. Measured, a structural rule doing a POSITIVE read of a structural-tagged ctx fact:
    untagged (shipped)                 -> ok      (inert)
    sameStratum {structural=["host"]}  -> THROWN  <- ABW SAYS ADMIT
    higher     {resolution=["host"]}   -> THROWN  (correct; positive control)
INERT TODAY ONLY BECAUSE ctxKeyStrata = { } (:90-93). ONE POPULATED ATTRIBUTE FROM FIRING. This is the
rubric's predicted "over-strict errors masquerade as rigour" — as CODE, not documentation.

CONTRADICTING W1: (1) path is kernel, not compat; (2) branch-2/branch-3 polarity reversed on totality;
(3) Candidate B's "aborts into the fallback instead of aborting named" refuted by direct fire; (4) W1's
"unverified whether branch 3 is corpus-inert" partially settled — a second corpus config (nixfos) defines two
table-key names, and on this evidence branch-3 inertness is the wrong thing to worry about since branch 3 is
the SOUND branch.

REVIEWER'S OWN METHOD NOTE: two predicates initially could not match — a sentinel typo ("« probe »" vs
"«probe»") and an unforced ctx read. BOTH CAUGHT BY POSITIVE CONTROLS THAT SHOULD HAVE FIRED AND DIDN'T. All
results post-correction, controls green. Scratch probes retained and runnable:
scratchpad/{c6-probe.nix,c6-probe2.nix,c6-probe3.nix,misdeclare.nix,abw.nix}.

GATE REVIEW #1 — W2 F1 class-reroute confluence design. VERDICT: REDESIGN (independent fresh context, adversarial, default-reject posture, 2026-07-27).

CANDIDATE: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-27-class-reroute-confluence-design.md — replace the non-confluent whole-map reroute fold (lib/attributes/class-modules.nix:128-166) with a reflexive-transitive preimage closure. DOES NOT ENTER THE GRAPH. Repairs in flight.

WHY REDESIGN, IN ONE LINE: the spec's equations do not compute the spec's own denotation. The design says "union over the preimage"; the mechanism it specifies returns a PATH-INDEXED MULTISET.

*** F-1 FATAL — "byte-identical on every acyclic case" REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT.
mode="paths" ENUMERATES PATHS AND DOES NOT DEDUP NODES. queryPaths threads its visited set INTO each recursive call (gen-graph/lib/query.nix:115-118) = per-path acyclicity, NOT a global seen-set; sibling branches never see each other's visits. Diamond A->B, A->C, B->D, C->D, one aspect per class:
    current fold     D = [cD,cB,cA,cC]
    spec as written  D = [cD,cB,cA,cC,cA]   <- cA TWICE
    preimage from D  = [D,B,A,C,A]
THE CONTRACT SAYS SO AND NAMES THE CASE: den-hoag/lib/query.nix:108-110 "No node-dedup — that is a caller-specific concern (e.g. resolveKey's diamond dedup), not the general query contract." The design IS the caller. That text was read during authoring and not applied.
SEVERITY: without dedup the duplication is EXPONENTIAL IN OUTPUT, not eval cost. k stacked diamonds, measured sink-bucket length: k=1 -> 5, k=2 -> 13, k=3 -> 29, k=6 -> 253 (= 4*2^k - 3). That is Theta(2^k) duplicated MODULE INSTANTIATIONS. The owner accepted fan-out duplication ACROSS two targets; Theta(2^k) duplication INSIDE one target was never put to the owner.
ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISS: section 4 generalized from exactly two witnesses, BOTH TREES (a chain and a sibling fan-in). The first non-tree acyclic shape breaks it.

*** F-2 FATAL for the totality claim — NOT TOTAL ON THE PRIMARY INPUT SHAPE.
Section 3.1 builds inverse edges from RAW act.from/act.to, dropping the className normalization the current code applies (class-modules.nix:31-37, applied at :154-157). class-modules.nix:29-30 states the input is "an entry (identity law) or, defensively, a bare class-name string" — ENTRY IS PRIMARY, bare string is the FALLBACK. The spec handled only the fallback. Measured, entry-shaped reroute:
    current code     -> { A=[]; B=[cB,cA]; C=[cC]; D=[cD] }
    spec as written  -> error: expected a string but found a set: { __isEntry = true; name = "B"; }
and builtins.tryEval did NOT contain it.
=> "adds ZERO error classes" is FALSE: it adds an UNNAMED, UNCATCHABLE one — the exact class lib/query.nix:70-76's named guards exist to pre-empt. C6 answer to "what happens on the violating input": dies with a gen-graph-internal type error naming no den concept. NOT a discharge.

** F-3 C6 UNDISCHARGED — WRONG ARGUMENT TYPES.
condensation takes edges as a FUNCTION node -> [target] (gen-graph/lib/edge-maps.nix:3); the spec passes a flat list => "attempt to call something which is not a function but a list". The idiom is at gen-graph/lib/order.nix:40-45.
SEPARATELY: the spec NEVER NAMES condensation's nodes argument, which decides the SINK TEST'S DOMAIN (all classNames vs only classes appearing in acts). An unnamed domain is undischarged per C6 regardless of surrounding prose.

** F-5 C5 COORDINATE DEFECT.
Section 3.5 cites "queryPaths at lib/query.nix:89, an internal of the den query lowering". BOTH HALVES FALSE. den-hoag/lib/query.nix defines NO queryPaths; its :89 is the unparseable-follow throw; it exports only perLabelFromEdges and denQuery (:113-115). queryPaths is at GEN-GRAPH/lib/query.nix:89 — the line number coincides across the two files, which is presumably how the slip happened.
NOT COSMETIC: section 3.5 offered binding queryPaths as a live implementation choice, which reaches PAST den's query lowering into gen-graph and bypasses denQuery's named guards (:67-76) — guaranteeing F-2's unnamed-error mode.

F-7 OVERCLAIM — section 3.3 says both members "ALIAS" the union of a cycle SCC. Measured on A<->B: A=[cA,cB], B=[cB,cA]. SET-EQUAL, ORDER-DIFFERENT. On the list-typed options section 5 itself calls order "semantically meaningful", those are DIFFERENT MERGE RESULTS. The cycle test as worded ("both members carry the union") would PASS and not catch it.

FALSE PREMISE PROPPING UP A TRUE CONCLUSION (C2 re-source) — section 4 says "the preimage is a SET-VALUED closure ... permuting resolutionActs permutes neither". FALSE; permuting acts permutes the preimage list and on a diamond changes its multiplicity. The conclusion SURVIVES but must be re-sourced: bucket-assignment confluence holds because isSource and the NODE-SET of the preimage are order-invariant. The false premise is precisely what CONCEALED F-1.

==== FINDINGS THAT CUT IN THE DESIGN'S FAVOUR ====
- THE FOLD IS WORSE THAN THE SPEC CLAIMED. Diamond, four permutations of ONE act set, through live class-modules.compute: [cD,cB,cA,cC] / [cD,cB,cC,cA] / [cD,cB,cC] / [cD,cC,cB] — FOUR ANSWERS, TWO OF WHICH STRAND cA ENTIRELY. => "byte-identical to the fold" is NOT A WELL-POSED ACCEPTANCE CRITERION on non-tree shapes; the criterion there must be the DENOTATION.
- F-6 THE DEPENDENCY CONCERN WAS OVERSTATED, against the design's own interest. "A new dependency edge into the attributes stratum" is FALSE AS STATED: lib/attributes/default.nix:26 ALREADY takes graph and threads it into attributes/resolved-aspects.nix:53. The new edge is into one FILE of a stratum that already carries it; only condensation is genuinely new (control: condensation appears in den-hoag lib/ only in a comment at lib/demand.nix:44, while labeledFrom hits lib/query.nix and lib/receivers.nix). The dependency is ACCEPTABLE. The boundary-guard half IS correct and mild: boundary.nix's kernel check is a forbidden-token scan (:85-99) over a fixed file list (:30-78) with no import-shape guard, and its "sole graph traversal" line (:155-158) is scoped to the COMPAT shim, so a kernel-side traversal trips nothing.

==== PURE-GRAPH CRITERIA — THE DESIGN JUDGED AGAINST THE SAME BAR ====
1 state-accumulation-instead-of-query: PASS — the per-class bucket accumulator genuinely dissolves. THE DESIGN'S REAL MERIT.
2 underscore state carriers: PASS, none introduced.
4 bounded-depth traversal: PASS — rerouteInv* is a Kleene closure, correct on the 0/1/infinity rule.
5 effect-runtime holdovers: PASS — the sequential fold IS the accumulator shape and it is eliminated.
3 value-shape dispatch: NEUTRAL->NEGATIVE — className (class-modules.nix:31-37, "if builtins.isAttrs c") is value-shape dispatch and SURVIVES. Pre-existing, so not a new violation, BUT F-2 shows the design DROPS it BY OMISSION rather than replacing it deliberately. A replace-in-full that loses a normalization by accident is worse than one that keeps it knowingly.
6 invariants documented but unenforced: NEUTRAL — the spec correctly spots that class-modules.nix:8 ("NO EFFECT RUNTIME: the body is field reads + attrset assembly + list appends") becomes FALSE under a graph traversal; the remedy is comment -> comment, and F-6 confirms no gate enforces either.

==== INTERNAL CONTRADICTION THE DOCUMENT CANNOT HOLD ====
Section 2.3 commits to totality over everything the surface can express. Section 7 PARKS the case where a reroute "to" is outside classNames — which empties the "from" bucket, then genAttrs classNames drops the target key: SILENT TOTAL ANNIHILATION. Section 3.4 says "behaviour would otherwise be undefined; here it is defined" — it is defined AS SILENT ANNIHILATION, defined-but-WRONG, not the sense that sentence trades on.
ORCHESTRATOR RULING: resolve by NARROWING section 2.3, not by expanding scope. The behaviour is pre-existing (the current fold does the same), so it is not a regression and not this spec's job. Adding a guard would EXCEED the owner's decision, which was specifically that fan-out adds no error class.

==== C5 CITATION VERIFICATION — INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED TWICE ====
Mokhov 2017 section 4.6 "Preorders and Equivalence Relations" at used/markdown/mokhov-2017-algebraic-graphs.md:743-744; both quotes VERBATIM (:748-750, :754-755) including the (Graph g, Vertex g ~ Set Int) => g typing. Section 4.6 DERIVES the quotient (a construction, not an assumption), so it covers more than enumeration over an already-given quotient. Mokhov DELEGATES the SCC computation to containers' scc => gen-graph/lib/global.nix:136's split (algorithm -> Tarjan/Kosaraju, IDIOM -> Mokhov) is CORRECTLY APPORTIONED. The citation the design leans on HOLDS.
UNVERIFIED markings audited as HONEST, not convenient: Brzozowski appears only INSIDE van-antwerpen-2016-statix (a secondary citation, not the primary source); Kosaraju absent as a primary; reppy 0 hits; Tarjan 1972 absent (Mokhov:758 cites a DIFFERENT Tarjan — Tarjan & Van Leeuwen 1984). Control: mokhov hits 2 files.
SELECTIVE OMISSION (minor, C2-a-adjacent): the spec quotes global.nix:136 but not :131-133 directly above it, which DISCLAIM Tarjan — "closure-based O(n^2) ... NOT Tarjan's linear O(V+E) single-DFS — its mutable stack/lowlink is out-of-substrate for pure Nix." This does not break the design (closure-based co-reachability is a correct SCC DEFINITION), but presenting :136 as clean attribution while the adjacent lines disclaim the algorithm should be noted.

==== SPUN OUT — SEPARATE gen-graph FINDING, NOT THIS SPEC ====
gen-graph/lib/order.nix:5-6 cites "Mokhov 2017 section 4 quotient-graph TOPOLOGICAL ENUMERATION". OVERSTATES ON TWO COUNTS: (1) "topological" occurs ZERO times in Mokhov 2017 — verified independently by both orchestrator and reviewer, with positive controls in the same run ("condensation"=2, "graph"=421, stem "topolog"=0); (2) SCOPE — the paper constructs the quotient but says nothing about enumerating an order over it. Needs its own review candidate against the live theory-conformance audit.

==== SIX LOCATED REPAIRS — the reviewer verified the principal one ====
R1 order-preserving FIRST-OCCURRENCE DEDUP on the preimage node list. VERIFIED to restore exact parity: dedup [D,B,A,C,A] -> [D,B,A,C] -> [cD,cB,cA,cC] = the fold's d_p1. Must NOT be over-applied: dedup is WITHIN one class's preimage query; fan-out duplication ACROSS classes is the owner's decision and must survive.
R2 apply className when building BOTH the inverse edge list AND the condensation node set.
R3 give condensation a FUNCTION-shaped edges argument and NAME its nodes domain.
R4 bind denQuery { mode = "paths"; }, NOT queryPaths — keeps the named guards and settles section 3.5's open choice in the direction that does not manufacture unnamed errors.
R5 re-source section 4's premise (node-SET order-invariance, not "set-valued closure"); replace section 3.3's "alias" with "set-equal, order-differing".
R6 ADD A DIAMOND FIXTURE (its absence is why F-1 survived authoring); make the cycle test ASSERT ORDER, not membership; state that byte-identity is ill-posed on non-tree shapes.

DO NOT LET THIS BE RE-PROPOSED WITHOUT A DIAMOND IN THE TEST PLAN AND A DEDUP IN THE EQUATIONS. The failure mode was generalization from two tree-shaped witnesses to "every acyclic case", and it reproduces in one nix eval.

REVIEWER COVERAGE — HONEST: 7 nix eval probes against the live libs (import den-hoag/default.nix {}) plus gen-graph pinned from flake.lock; every absence claim positive-controlled on the same predicate in the same run; .worktrees/ excluded from every search; mode-trap discipline respected (M/A/Z plus a diamond, confirming all-sorts vs paths-traverses BEFORE relying on either).
NOT RUN: no CI gate invoked. Probes drive the synthetic internal.classModulesBuilder harness, NOT a real fleet through mkDen, so behaviour at a live node with real resolved-aspects and exempt sets is untested. The reviewer IMPLEMENTED section 3.1 itself in order to run F-1/F-3, so those refute the SPEC AS WRITTEN; an implementer would hit F-3 loudly on first run, but F-1 WOULD NOT BE REPAIRED BY ACCIDENT — paths mode returns plausible output on trees and diverges silently only on a diamond.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
GATE RUBRIC ADDITION — C7 CONSTRUCTION-VS-REPAIR, and C7-a PRIMITIVE GRANULARITY.
Added by the orchestrator 2026-07-27 on a standing owner directive, after GATE REVIEW #1 demonstrated that
C1-C6 cannot catch this class. Same form as the existing checks: a FAIL-IF predicate naming a concrete
artifact, so a reviewer either runs it or does not.

OWNER RULING THAT PROMPTED IT: "dedup is valid, but it's better if there's no duplication by
construction/traversal." Plus the standing rule that PERFORMANCE ISSUES ARE DEFECTS, not acceptable costs.

C7 CONSTRUCTION-VS-REPAIR — does the design REMOVE the defect class, or does it let the defect arise and
then correct it? FAIL IF the mechanism produces a bad intermediate that a later step filters, dedups,
normalizes, sorts or guards, AND a construction exists in the substrate where the bad intermediate never
forms. A repair is an invariant somebody must maintain: it regresses silently on any later edit, must be
re-applied at every new call site, leaves the CAUSE in place so the next caller reintroduces it, and runs
AFTER the bad work is done so it fixes the output while still paying the price.
  KNOWN-POSITIVE: the reroute-confluence design as submitted. Section 11.2 correctly argued that ELIMINATING
  the rewrite beats making it confluent — and section 3.1 simultaneously enumerated paths and proposed to
  dedup them. THE DESIGN'S OWN THEORY SECTION REFUTED ITS OWN MECHANISM and neither the author nor two
  adversarial review rounds noticed, because every check was aimed at whether the repair WORKED.
  THE TELL, and it is cheap to run: if the theory section argues "we eliminate the shape rather than
  constrain it" for one property while the mechanism constrains-and-corrects for a second property, the two
  have drifted apart. Read the theory section and the equations against EACH OTHER, not each against the
  prose around it.
  NOTE C7 IS NOT SATISFIED BY A WORKING REPAIR. GATE REVIEW #1 verified that the prescribed dedup restored
  exact fold parity on the diamond. It was still the wrong answer, because gen-graph/lib/preorder.nix makes
  the duplication unrepresentable. A verified repair is precisely the shape that closes this check falsely.

C7-a PRIMITIVE GRANULARITY — was the substrate scanned to PRIMITIVE granularity, or only to LIB granularity?
FAIL IF the design binds one surface of a lib without the spec showing that the lib's OTHER exports were
enumerated and rejected for a stated reason.
  KNOWN-POSITIVE: three review rounds spent on gen-graph's query/denQuery lowering — the CORRECT LIB —
  because the originating finding (W2 F1) named it. query's paths mode threads its visited set INTO each
  branch (gen-graph/lib/query.nix, per-path acyclicity), so it duplicates nodes on every non-tree shape and
  is enumeration-priced by its own header. gen-graph/lib/preorder.nix, ONE FILE OVER IN THE SAME LIB,
  threads visited ACROSS siblings via foldl', giving once-per-node first-occurrence-wins traversal in the
  same DFS pre-order and pruning subtrees WITHOUT FORCING THEM.
  WHY REVIEW CANNOT CATCH IT UNAIDED: adversarial review verifies CLAIMS against code. An unconsidered
  alternative primitive is not IN the spec, so there is nothing to attack. Both review rounds measured the
  consequences correctly (exponential duplication; a class silently lost on the diamond) and prescribed the
  repair, because the instrument itself was never in question.
  WHEN A FINDING NAMES AN INSTRUMENT, THAT IS A POINTER, NOT A DECISION. gen-* module headers state their
  own trade-offs explicitly — preorder.nix's header names itself "the DFS-preorder dual of the label-blind
  genericClosure surface" and says genericClosure "returns a SET in an unspecified visitation order". The
  information needed to choose correctly was in a header the design never opened.

C7-b COST IS A STATED PROPERTY — FAIL IF the design states its ANSWER but not its PRICE. Performance issues
are defects (owner, 2026-07-27), so a design that does not name the complexity of its chosen instrument is
incomplete in the same way one that does not name its violation behaviour is incomplete under C6. If a
cheaper instrument exists in the substrate, binding the dearer one needs a stated reason.
  KNOWN-POSITIVE: the same design reasoned about correctness throughout and said nothing about cost; the
  Theta(2^k) blowup was found only because a reviewer measured a k-diamond series, and it was initially
  mis-read as an output-duplication symptom rather than also a WORK series.

POSTURE, unchanged: default REJECT. C7 admits a design when the reviewer can name the defect class, name the
construction that makes it unrepresentable, and confirm the design binds THAT construction — or can point at
the spec's stated reason for binding a dearer or weaker one.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
GATE REVIEW #3 — W2 F1 class-reroute confluence design, after the preorder repair.
VERDICT: REDESIGN (narrow). C7 CORE PASSES. C7-a FAILS. C7-b FAILS (measured).
Same independent reviewer as rounds 1 and 2. Repairs dispatched; three items, none touching an equation.

★★★ C7 CORE PASSES, AND THE MECHANISM WAS VERIFIED BY EXECUTION NOT BY READING.
The reviewer transcribed section 3.1's equations VERBATIM into a probe and ran them on 18 shapes:
  diamond preimage D = [D,B,A,C]        each node ONCE, by construction
  diamond buckets  D = [cD,cB,cA,cC]    == fold d_p1
  chain C = [cC,cB,cA] == fold · siblings C = [cC,cA,cB] == fold
  fan-out B=[cB,cA] C=[cC,cA]           section 3.4 owner decision PRESERVED (per-class seen sets)
  cycle A<->B  A=[cA,cB] B=[cB,cA] · cycle+exit A=[] B=[] C=[cC,cB,cA] · self-loop A->A all buckets intact
  empty R: preimage A=[A], buckets == base (fast path degenerates correctly)
  ENTRY-shaped A->B: B=[cB,cA]  WORKS (F-2 closed)
  ★ perm1 == perm2, both C=[cC,cB,cA]   THE F1 DEFECT IS FIXED
ALL PRIOR FINDINGS CLOSED: F-1 (by construction), F-2, F-3, F-4 (as a documentation defect; behaviour
unchanged and still pre-existing), F-5, F-6, F-7, the section 5 category error, the alias overclaim, and the
ninth-input diamond adopted as both a table row and a test row.

THE C7 TELL COMES BACK CLEAN. Section 11.2 and section 3.1 now agree instead of contradicting:
"section 3.1 now uses a traversal that visits each node at most once ... so the duplication does not arise
rather than arising and being removed. The theory story and the mechanism agree ... IT WOULD BE THE RIGHT ONE
AT EQUAL COST." That last clause is the C7-correct posture — the construction is the warrant, cost is
corroboration.

★ THE REVIEWER RECORDED ITS OWN ROUND-2 PRESCRIPTION AS THE WRONG ANSWER. Its post-hoc dedupFirst on the
paths result was verified and restored exact fold parity on the diamond, and was still wrong twice over: it
maintains an invariant a refactor can drop, and it leaves the Theta(2^k) WORK in place — the enumeration
still walks every path before anything is discarded. A VERIFIED REPAIR IS THE SHAPE THAT CLOSES C7 FALSELY.
This is C7's first run and its own known-positive was produced by the check it now guards against.

IN-REPO PRECEDENT FOR THE C7 DISTINCTION, verified live — the same trap has caught three den-hoag sites:
  lib/receivers.nix:178-180        "DIAMOND DEDUP: per-path enumeration answers a diamond-reachable kind
                                    ONCE PER PATH"                     -> repaired after the fact
  lib/attributes/resolved-settings.nix:150  "gen-graph's global first-occurrence visited set dedups a
                                    diamond (shared-grandparent) slice the path-scoped walk emitted TWICE"
                                                                       -> changed instrument
  this design                                                          -> changed instrument
Two repaired downstream, two changed instrument. C7 has live witnesses in this repo.

════ C7-a FAILS — the reverse-reachability family is never enumerated ════
The spec enumerates and rejects THREE alternatives with stated reasons (queryPaths, denQuery/mode=all,
foldReach). It never names the family gen-graph exports for exactly this question. Occurrence counts in the
spec, positive controls same run (expandPreorder 26, condensation 34):
  dependentsOf 0 · impactOf 0 · dependents 0 · dependentsFrontier 0 · reachableFrom 0 · reachableWhere 0 ·
  canReach 0 · pathsBetween 0 · coScc 0 · coneRank 0 · transpose 1 (mentioned, never as a candidate)
dependentsOf IS LITERALLY THE PREIMAGE OF A TARGET. gen-graph/lib/global.nix:71-81 advertises it: "Single-
target reverse reachability via reverse traversal (Arntzenius 2016) ... Much faster than dependents for
single-target queries"; impactOf = dependentsOf at :196. The design instead hand-rolls the inverse relation
(invBy = groupBy tgt R) and walks forward over it — which is what dependentsOf does internally.
THEY ARE GENUINELY REJECTABLE, so expandPreorder STAYS. Both disqualifiers measured:
  dependentsOf/impactOf SORT — builtins.sort builtins.lessThan at global.nix:81, the same order-destroying
    ground as mode="all" that section 7 devotes a whole section to.
  traverse.reachableFrom EXCLUDES THE START NODE (traverse.nix:8 comment, filter :19), so the reflexive
    member must be re-added by hand — and NO section 9 test currently pins the reflexive member.
WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: section 7 warns at length about the sorting hazard for ONE export while three more
carry the identical hazard unnamed. An implementer who reads "use a reachability primitive, not a path
enumerator" and reaches for impactOf lands straight back in section 7's own trap AND silently drops the
reflexive member.

════ C7-b FAILS — MEASURED 43x, AND THE FAST PATH HIDES IT FROM THE CORPUS ════
The spec prices ONE preimage (3k+1) and condensation (O(n^2), global.nix:131-133). It never prices what
class-modules actually computes: keyedBucketsOf = genAttrs classNames OVER that.
Section 3.1 is genuinely ambiguous. "classSliceKeyedAt = THE PRIMITIVE (the direct per-(node,class) query)"
read literally says a self-contained per-class primitive builds invBy/fwdBy/nodes/cond ITSELF and pays it
ONCE PER CLASS; the equation block writes cond as a shared binding. Measured, chain relation over n classes,
deepSeq-forced with a sentinel positive control confirming the force actually happens:
    classes   cond shared   cond per-class
      20        0.352s        0.382s
      40        0.362s        0.853s
      60        0.404s        3.184s
      80        0.499s       10.614s
     100        0.675s       29.447s     <- 43x
Shared ~O(n^2) and near-flat in practice; per-class ~O(n^3).
★★ SECTION 3.2's FAST PATH HIDES IT ENTIRELY — zero reroute acts means no condensation at all, so the
multiplier appears in NO corpus test. THAT IS PRECISELY THE CLASS OF DEFECT THAT SHIPS.
Aggravated by adjacency: section 3.1's own "Scope of the traversal's seen-set — per class, and it must not be
widened" correctly pins the TRAVERSAL as per-class for the section 3.4 fan-out decision, which invites an
implementer to make EVERYTHING per-class. Nothing in the document says invBy/fwdBy/nodes/cond are functions
of R alone and must be hoisted to the per-NODE let.
THE HONEST TENSION, worth recording: the design's headline win — inverting primitive/derived so the per-class
query is primitive (section 4, "whole-map materialization dissolves") — IS what creates the multiplier. The
old whole-map form ran applyInjectReroute once per node. The inversion is still right; its price must be
named and the hoist must be pinned.

════ ONE STATED MEASUREMENT DOES NOT REPRODUCE ════
Section 3.1 claims 0.012s is the process floor, "measured with two controls in the same run (1+1 -> 0.012s,
importing gen-graph -> 0.012s)". Re-measured: bare 1+1 = 0.013s (matches); IMPORTING GEN-GRAPH = 0.176s
(claimed 0.012s); expandPreorder total = 0.26s (claimed "at the process floor").
Conclusion UNAFFECTED — flat-vs-doubling settles the instrument and that holds (expandPreorder flat ~0.26s
at k=14..30; queryPaths 0.341 -> 12.473s over k=14..20). But the document says "the probe outputs are
reproduced verbatim" and this is the one number that came back an order of magnitude off. expandPreorder is
at the GEN-GRAPH-IMPORT floor plus a traversal too small to measure, not the process floor.
THIRD FIGURE ON THIS DOCUMENT STATED AS MEASURED THAT WAS NOT (two line counts previously).

════ CONFIRMED IN THE TREE ════
Answer counts reproduce EXACTLY: queryPaths 5/13/29/61/125/253/1021 = 4*2^k-3; expandPreorder
4/7/10/13/16/19/25 = 3k+1.
den's `graph` DOES expose it: graph.expandPreorder is ALREADY CALLED at lib/attributes/resolved-aspects.nix:120
— same stratum, same graph that lib/attributes/default.nix:26 threads; preorder is merged into gen-graph's
top-level exports (gen-graph/lib/default.nix:10,21). So this is the stratum's own idiom, NOT reaching around
den's query lowering. condensation remains the one genuinely new combinator.
The sink test is now PINNED AS AN EQUATION with the warning that the two formulations' agreement is a
property of gen-graph's self-rep filter (global.nix:164) rather than a theorem — round 2's residual, adopted.
Both benign resolutions CLOSED in section 12 with strikethrough, not carried as open unknowns.
Section 9 goes beyond what the gate asked: on a two-cycle only ONE of the two roots has traversal order
differing from sorted order, so a suite asserting only the A side is mode-blind EVEN WITH GOOD NAMES —
assert both members. Sharper than the finding that prompted it.

════ THREE REPAIRS, NONE TOUCHING AN EQUATION ════
P1 one paragraph in section 3.5 enumerating the reverse-reachability family with the two measured
   disqualifiers (sorts at global.nix:81; excludes start at traverse.nix:19), plus one line in (E) on why
   groupBy rather than graph.transpose — transpose requires a `nodes` domain, the very thing (D) had to be
   careful about, while groupBy is O(|R|) with no domain.
P2 (a) PIN in section 3.1 that invBy/fwdBy/nodes/cond are per-NODE bindings hoisted to the per-node let, and
   only preimage/content are per-CLASS — stated adjacent to the seen-set note so the two scopes are read
   together. (b) STATE the complexity of keyedBucketsOf, not only of preimage.
P3 re-measure or restate the 0.012s control.

RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-PROPOSED: the correct instrument is graph.expandPreorder, because foldPreorder
threads `visited` THROUGH the sibling foldl' (gen-graph/lib/preorder.nix:65-70) while queryPaths passes it
INTO each branch (gen-graph/lib/query.nix:115-118). Post-hoc dedup on queryPaths reaches the same answer —
verified in round 2 — and is the wrong shape twice over: it maintains an invariant a refactor can drop, and
it leaves Theta(2^k) work in place. dependentsOf/impactOf/reachableFrom are NOT substitutes: they sort, and
reachableFrom drops the start node.

REVIEWER COVERAGE — HONEST: did NOT read all 1227 lines. Read in full: sections 3.1, 3.5, 5 head + full
degenerate table, 8, 11.2, 12, plus the heading map. Sections 6, 7, 10, 11.1, 11.3 reached by targeted grep
and excerpt; section 4 opening only. A defect confined to an unopened part of those would not have been
caught. Substrate read in full: gen-graph/lib/preorder.nix (all three combinators), gen-graph/lib/default.nix.
Ran: section 3.1 transcribed verbatim and evaluated on 18 shapes; ladder answer counts both instruments
k=1..8; wall-clock both k=14..30 with two process-floor controls; shared-vs-per-class cost n=20..100 with
deepSeq forcing and a sentinel control. NOT DONE: no CI gate; probes drive transcribed equations + the
synthetic internal.classModulesBuilder harness, NOT a real fleet through mkDen; Mokhov citation not re-run
this round (round-2 verification, text confirmed unchanged); "page 7" and DOI still unverified. The 43x
figure uses a CHAIN relation — one point in a space sampled once, relation shape not varied.
INSTRUMENT NOTE: the first cost probe returned a flat ~0.01s across all n; the reviewer caught that
attrNames NEVER FORCES VALUES, re-ran with deepSeq, and confirmed forcing with a sentinel before reporting
any number.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
GATE REVIEW #3 RE-ISSUED against the further-edited file. VERDICT: REDESIGN — one paragraph, one sentence
and one number from VALIDATED. Supersedes the round-3 comment above on two points.

CHANGED SINCE THE ROUND-3 COMMENT:
  C7-b now PASSES. Section 4 gained a Cost table; the reviewer checked every row against sources and they
  hold — invAdj/fwdAdj O(|R|) via two groupBy passes; preimage O(n+|R|) consistent with 3k+1 and flat
  wall-clock; isSink O(n^2) matching global.nix:131-133's own header; whole map = above x |classNames|;
  zero acts = fast path. The predicate asks for the price and the price is stated honestly and in the
  CONSERVATIVE direction. The 43x hoisting point survives as an IMPROVEMENT to take, not a failure: cond,
  invBy, fwdBy and nodes are functions of R alone and are hoistable to a per-NODE binding, so the table
  prices the AVOIDABLE cost.
  C7 CORE still PASSES, now verified against a BYTE-IDENTICAL equation block (md5 over the equation lines
  matched the reviewer's earlier copy), so the execution verification carries rather than being re-derived.

★★ THE SIGNATURE CHECK PASSES BY EXECUTION. gen-graph/lib/preorder.nix declares
    expandPreorder = { roots, key, edges, resolve ? (frame: frame), emit ? (_frame: payload: payload),
                       seen0 ? { }, nodes0 ? [ ] }: ... in { nodes = r.acc; seen = r.visited; };
so roots/key/edges are exactly the three required args, the other four default, and `.nodes` is a real
field. Two subtleties checked because they are where a plausible-looking call breaks: `edges` is applied to
the RESOLVED PAYLOAD (children = edges payload) and with the default resolve = frame: frame the payload is
the bare id string, so edges = invAdj receives a string — correct; `key` is applied to the FRAME, also the
id string, so key = id: id — correct.

★★★ C7-a STILL FAILS. THIS IS THE ONLY BLOCKER.
The spec now enumerates and rejects FOUR alternatives with stated reasons — queryPaths, denQuery/mode="all",
mode="layers" (new: queryLayers calls queryPaths, so it is no escape from the cost), and foldReach. ALL FOUR
ARE IN THE QUERY/PREORDER FAMILIES. The reverse-reachability family in global.nix and traverse.nix is still
absent entirely. Occurrence counts, positive controls same run (expandPreorder 41, condensation 34):
  dependentsOf 0 · impactOf 0 · dependents 0 · dependentsFrontier 0 · reachableFrom 0 · canReach 0 ·
  pathsBetween 0 · coneRank 0 · transpose 1 (cited as evidence the stratum uses graph, never as a candidate)
WHY DECISIVE RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING — THE OMITTED INSTRUMENT IS FASTER, NOT MERELY DIFFERENT:
  global.nix:71-81 — "Single-target reverse reachability via reverse traversal (Arntzenius 2016). O(n) to
  build reverse index + O(reachable in reverse) C-LEVEL BFS. Much faster than dependents for single-target
  queries on large graphs." impactOf = dependentsOf at :196. It routes through traverse.reachableFrom, which
  uses builtins.genericClosure — C-level — and traverse.nix:3-4 claims "~4-5x faster than Nix-level BFS".
  expandPreorder is a NIX-LEVEL DFS. So the cost table shows a Nix-level traversal with NO RECORD of why the
  faster C-level one is off-limits. That is exactly the shape C7-a exists to catch: a future optimiser swaps
  it in and silently loses the reflexive member.
VERIFIED UNUSABLE ON TWO INDEPENDENT GROUNDS, so expandPreorder STAYS and this is a gap in the RECORD:
  (1) dependentsOf/impactOf SORT — builtins.sort builtins.lessThan, global.nix:81. Identical ground to the
      mode="all" hazard section 7 devotes a whole section to.
  (2) traverse.reachableFrom EXCLUDES THE START NODE — traverse.nix:8 comment, filter at :19 — so the
      reflexive member roots = [ C ] supplies would be silently dropped. ★ NO TEST IN SECTION 9 PINS THE
      REFLEXIVE MEMBER against a traversal that drops it.
THE FIX IS ONE PARAGRAPH AND GEN-GRAPH ALREADY WROTE THE REJECTION — preorder.nix:1-11: "builtins.
genericClosure is C-level but BFS, single-keyed and payload-blind: it returns a SET in an UNSPECIFIED
VISITATION ORDER ... These combinators are the missing ORDERED, PAYLOAD-CARRYING, LABEL-EXPOSING analog ...
which genericClosure STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS." That is the principled rejection of the entire C-level
family in the library's own words — stronger than anything the author or orchestrator would compose, because
it is the author of BOTH instruments explaining why both exist.

★ THE REVIEWER CORRECTED ITS OWN ROUND-3 FRAMING. It had reported the self-loop row as "verified, the row
earns its place". The spec's NEW section 1.3 (the self-reroute abort) makes it stronger: the old behaviour is
not "keeps its content by a different route", it is DOES NOT EVALUATE. Verified exactly, with a positive
control (fold on A→B works: {A=[];B=[cB,cA];C=[cC];D=[cD]}) and a tryEval check (does NOT contain it):
    fold on A→A => error: dynamic attribute 'A' already defined
                     at lib/attributes/class-modules.nix:161:11 and :162:11
So section 5's self-loop row is a REPAIR, not a coarsening, and section 6 correctly declines to file it under
coarsening. Tracked as a shipped defect on den-hoag-4kh.12.

ALL PREVIOUSLY-FLAGGED CORRECTIONS LANDED: section 5's "harmless" row split into from/to with the to-side
marked SILENT TOTAL LOSS · section 6's count corrected to three with the diamond classified as a DIFFERENT
KIND ("a different value for the same class — a multiset superset within a single bucket — not a merging of
previously-distinguished inputs") and C2 invoked · section 6 reason 1 STRUCK with the section 2.3
contradiction named in the strike · the "alias" overclaim replaced · section 4's set-valued premise
re-sourced to isSink + node-set order-invariance · both section 12 items closed with strikethrough · the sink
test pinned as an equation WITH its reason (the two formulations agree only because global.nix:161-167
filters self-reps, "a property of gen-graph's current implementation, not a theorem about the design").

MEASUREMENTS RE-RUN FRESH THIS ROUND, all reproduce: diamond preimage [D,B,A,C] each node once, content
[cD,cB,cA,cC] == fold d_p1 · chain [cC,cB,cA] == fold · siblings [cC,cA,cB] == fold · cycle A<->B
A=[cA,cB] B=[cB,cA] · cycle+exit C=[cC,cB,cA] · self-loop all buckets intact, preimage [A] · perm1 == perm2
· entry-shaped B=[cB,cA] · unregistered support [A,X] with isSink A=false, isSink D=true.
WORK SERIES (work, not output): answers queryPaths 5/13/29/61/125/253/1021 = 4*2^k-3 vs expandPreorder
4/7/10/13/16/19/25 = 3k+1. Wall-clock: floor 0.012s; import gen-graph 0.175s; expandPreorder k=18 0.268s,
k=22 0.275s, k=30 0.272s FLAT ACROSS 2x NODES; queryPaths k=18 3.158s, k=20 12.980s.
DEN EXPOSES IT AND IT IS NOT A REACH-AROUND: preorder merged into gen-graph's top-level exports
(gen-graph/lib/default.nix:10,21) and graph.expandPreorder is ALREADY CALLED IN THE SAME STRATUM at
lib/attributes/resolved-aspects.nix:120, from the same graph lib/attributes/default.nix:26 threads.

════ THE 0.012s FIGURE, NOW MEASURED THREE TIMES AND STILL WRONG ════
Spec claims "measured with two controls in the same run (1+1 -> 0.012s, importing gen-graph -> 0.012s)" and
"expandPreorder at k=30 is still 0.012s". Reviewer: 1+1 = 0.012s matches; importing gen-graph = 0.175s;
expandPreorder k=30 = 0.272s. Orchestrator, independently: bare 1+1 = 11-13ms; gen-graph lib forced via
attrNames and via deepSeq = 20ms. The two external figures differ from each other because different amounts
were forced — BUT BOTH MEASURE THE IMPORT AS STRICTLY MORE THAN THE BARE FLOOR, and a traversal cannot cost
less than importing the library it runs in. THAT IS AN INTERNAL IMPOSSIBILITY, NOT A HARDWARE DISAGREEMENT:
the author's series was almost certainly never forced. The CONCLUSION is unaffected — flat-versus-doubling
settles the instrument and reproduced in both directions. The answer-count series is sound (arithmetic on
returned lists, not timing). FOURTH figure from this author stated as measured that was not.

════ REMEDY — the reviewer states that if these land, its verdict is VALIDATED ════
  one paragraph in section 3.5 citing preorder.nix:1-11 (the C-level-BFS rejection gen-graph already wrote),
    global.nix:81 (sorts) and traverse.nix:19 (drops the start node), naming the family explicitly so the
    enumeration is searchable; consider a section 9 test pinning the reflexive member
  one sentence in section 3.1 pinning invBy/fwdBy/nodes/cond as per-NODE and preimage/content as per-CLASS
  one number either restated or re-measured under deepSeq with a sentinel

REVIEWER COVERAGE — HONEST: read in full this round only the new section 1.3, the section 3.1 equation block
and instrument argument, section 4's Cost and what-is-not-claimed, section 6, plus the heading map. Sections
2, 5's table body, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11.1, 11.3 and 12 were NOT re-read line by line against the current text —
verified against the earlier version and the specific corrections confirmed by targeted grep. The edit was
+239 lines; the reviewer located the new section 1.3 (+27) and expansions in 4/6/7/10 but DID NOT ACCOUNT FOR
EVERY ADDED LINE. A defect in an added passage inside a grep-only section would not have been caught.
Mokhov citation carried from round 2, text unchanged; page-7 and DOI still unverified, no network call.
No CI gate run. All probes use transcribed equations + the synthetic internal.classModulesBuilder harness,
NOT a live fleet through mkDen. The 43x figure is one relation shape (chain), sampled once.

★ PROCESS NOTE FOR THE RECORD: the document moved between review dispatch and review start, and the
orchestrator's dispatch brief carried a stale line count and a stale claim that the headings were unchanged
(a new section 1.3 had been added). Three distinct line-count figures were in circulation for one document.
FREEZE THE ARTEFACT BEFORE DISPATCHING A REVIEW, and re-measure any figure in the brief at dispatch time
rather than relaying an earlier snapshot.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
GATE REVIEW #4 (FINAL) — W2 F1 class-reroute confluence design.
★★★ VERDICT: VALIDATED — THE DESIGN. First design to pass this gate.

════ SCOPE OF THE VALIDATION, STATED PRECISELY — read this before treating anything as settled ════
VALIDATED IS: section 3.1's equations and the properties claimed for them.
VALIDATED IS NOT: an implementation. NONE EXISTS. Section 9's test plan is SPECIFIED BUT UNWRITTEN.
All parity against the live fold was measured through the synthetic internal.classModulesBuilder harness and
a verbatim transcription of section 3.1 — NEVER A LIVE mkDen FLEET. A SEPARATE GATE IS OWED ON THE
IMPLEMENTATION.
★ VALIDATED AGAINST A SPECIFIC ARTEFACT: 1606 lines, 111067 bytes, md5 c6ab541805da1bf9d2f1133738b434d7,
mtime 2026-07-27 18:10:51. THE FILE HAS SINCE MOVED TO 1664 LINES (md5 34fec05e0ea13cc511808881c1178a65).
THE 1606->1664 DELTA IS UNREVIEWED — it contains the P3 timing rewrite, the preorder.nix:1-11 citation, and
a new section 9 reflexive-member row. A delta review is owed before the design is treated as validated AT
HEAD. The orchestrator's re-anchor arrived after this review completed; that is an orchestration failure,
not a reviewer one.

════ HOW IT WAS VERIFIED ════
Equation block extracted from the fence, comments and blanks stripped: SEVENTEEN EXECUTABLE LINES,
md5 9a7b62f73db397487c18fe99fae754ed, a LINE-FOR-LINE MATCH with the transcription run at 17:50. Only
comments were added inside the block. The twelve shapes were therefore NOT re-run; round 3's execution
verification carries. (They were also re-run identically against the 1466-line version.)

════ THE REVIEWER RETRACTED ITS OWN ROUND-3 FINDING, BY ITS OWN MEASUREMENT ════
It had claimed "no section 9 test pins the reflexive member against a traversal that drops it". It
substituted dependentsOf into the fixtures itself. ALL THREE ROWS FAIL:
    diamond    Z = [cZ,cR,cM,cA]  ->  [cA,cM,cR]   FAILS (order + missing cZ)
    fan-out    B = [cB,cA]        ->  [cA]         FAILS (missing cB)
    self-loop  A = [cA]           ->  [ ]          FAILS (empty)
The suite CATCHES the substitution. The finding was FALSE and the remedy it prescribed (add a test) was
UNNECESSARY. The correct remedy is LABELLING — nothing said those rows were holding the reflexive member, so
a future edit could remove the defence without knowing it was one. The document adopts exactly that and
records it as "a weaker finding than 'unguarded', and it is the one supported by the measurement".
THE AUTHOR FOUND THIS BY RE-RUNNING A CLAIM FROM ITS BRIEF RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. The orchestrator had
propagated the false version.

★ REFINEMENT WORTH RECORDING — THE TWO FAILURE MODES ARE NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THE FAMILY:
    expandPreorder (ships)  = [Z,R,M,A]   reflexive, traversal order
    dependentsOf            = [A,M,R]     SORTED and no Z      <- fails BOTH ways
    impactOf                = [A,M,R]     byte-identical (confirms impactOf = dependentsOf)
    traverse.reachableFrom  = [R,A,M]     unsorted BFS, no Z    <- fails ONLY on the reflexive member
dependentsOf/impactOf fail both ways because they WRAP reachableFrom AND sort on top. A reader must not
infer that every member of the family sorts.

════ C7-a PASSES ════
Presence is not the predicate; the REJECTIONS were checked. All four coordinates verify against source:
  "sorts"                  global.nix:81  builtins.sort builtins.lessThan (traverse.reachableFrom ...)  OK
  "excludes startId"       traverse.nix:8 comment + :19 builtins.filter (id: id != startId)             OK
  impactOf = dependentsOf  global.nix:196                                     OK (byte-identical output)
  reachableWhere inherits  traverse.nix:22-23 delegates to reachableFrom      OK
Eleven exports named; the global.nix:71-73 advertisement quoted verbatim; the M/R/A/Z table in the document
MATCHES the reviewer's independent run VALUE-FOR-VALUE. Crucially the paragraph CONCEDES the cheaper-
instrument point rather than dodging it — "dependentsOf has the right name and the better headline
complexity" — and rejects it on MEASURED CORRECTNESS. That is the direct answer to C7-a's standing form: the
cheaper instrument IS enumerated and IS rejected with stated, sourced reasons.
NOT REQUIRED, judged by the reviewer: the preorder.nix:1-11 genericClosure rejection it had itself proposed
in round 3 was absent at 1606 (grep: zero genericClosure mentions). Its ruling — C7-a's predicate is about
the LIB'S EXPORTS, and genericClosure is a Nix BUILTIN, not a gen-graph export; every gen-graph export that
wraps it is enumerated and rejected. "The author's route — measure the exports, give two concrete
disqualifiers — is STRONGER than the provenance citation I suggested. Nice-to-have, not a gap."
(NOTE: the author states it ADDED that citation in the 1606->1664 delta, so at HEAD it is present. Strictly
an improvement over what was validated.)

════ C7-b PASSES ════
Binding scope pinned INSIDE the equation block (:311-316), not merely discussed nearby, and marked "part of
the design, not implementation latitude":
    PER NODE   R, src, tgt, invBy, invAdj, fwdBy, fwdAdj, nodes, cond
    PER CLASS  preimage C, isSink C, content C
The line that invited the misreading is annotated AT THE POINT OF MISREADING (:318-319): "'direct' = no
whole-map materialization; NOT 'self-contained'. It CLOSES OVER the per-node bindings; it does not rebuild
them." And "Scope of everything ELSE — per NODE, and it must not be narrowed" explicitly contrasts with the
per-class seen-set pin, warning that the two scopes are OPPOSITE — which was precisely the hazard.
Cost table prices keyedBucketsOf BOTH ways: hoisted O(n^2) + |classNames|*O(n + |R|); hoist omitted
|classNames|*O(n^2). Framing sentence: "pricing one preimage is not pricing what class-modules computes."
Reviewer's 29.447s recorded against the author's 28.872s; the floor-dominated row correctly marked as NOT
reproducing (0.334s vs 0.675s) and shown only as evidence of divergence. Identical output verified at n=40;
force controls include a sentinel that ABORTS to prove deepSeq reaches values.

════ ERRATUM FOUND — reported, not a blocker, FIX OWED ════
Cost-table row "isSink C | O(1) on the built quotient — per class | two attr reads on cond" is WRONG ON BOTH
HALVES. condensation exports condEdges = condEdgesOf at global.nix:192 — THE RAW RECOMPUTING FUNCTION — not
the memoized condMat built at :171 (used internally at :173, never exported). Confirmed empirically:
builtins.isFunction cond.condEdges = true. So cond.condEdges (cond.sccOf C) is TWO FUNCTION CALLS, the
second recomputing unique (filter (map repOf (concatMap edges (membersOf.${r})))) on every call.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SHIPPED FIGURE: NONE. condEdgesOf is bounded by O(n + |R|), which the keyedBucketsOf row
already multiplies by |classNames|. One intermediate row overstates its precision. Fix to
O(|SCC| + out-degree) and drop "two attr reads".

════ TIMING QUESTION SETTLED ════
Mechanism verified at source: gen-graph/default.nix:9-13 derives gen-prelude through builtins.fetchTree from
flake.lock, so the import floor depends on local tree resolution. Three floors across three machines
(0.011s author, 0.020s orchestrator, 0.175s reviewer) is EXPECTED, not contradictory.
The document handles it correctly: it RECORDS THE FAILED REPRODUCTION BY NAME AND NUMBER (:382 "On
re-measurement by an independent reviewer, importing gen-graph took 0.176s"), states the cause, rests the
claim on SHAPE only, and records the work-dominated control that DOES reproduce (k=20 queryPaths 12.417s
author vs 12.473s reviewer, :389-390).
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTIONS, both retracted: the "internal impossibility" argument was a cross-machine
comparison of floor-dominated numbers; the "unforced timings" hypothesis was disproved by the author's
sentinel controls (emit returning throw "SENTINEL-FORCED" ABORTS on both instruments). The author also
explained why `length` sufficed — producing expandPreorder's list spine already runs the foldl' — and
switched to deepSeq anyway because length would not be sound for a lazier payload.
THE USEFUL GENERALISATION: WORK-DOMINATED FIGURES REPRODUCE CROSS-MACHINE; FLOOR-DOMINATED ONES DO NOT.
The reviewer notes for the record that it never made the impossibility argument — it reported only that the
figure did not reproduce, which was accurate.

════ C7 CORE AND C1-C6 ════
C7 core PASSES: no dedup survives as mechanism; section 3.1 (P) still states "There is NO dedup step, and
none can be forgotten." C1-C6 discharged, carried against a byte-identical executable block: F-1 closed BY
CONSTRUCTION, F-2 by (N), F-3 by (F)/(D), F-4 recorded as SILENT TOTAL LOSS and carried as the one open
question a gate might decide differently, F-5/F-6 corrected, section 4's set-valued premise re-sourced,
section 6's third divergence named with C2 invoked and the corpus-presence reason struck-and-recorded,
section 5's Claim 1 / Claim 2 split, section 12 items 1-2 closed. The section 1.3 self-reroute abort verified
verbatim with a positive control (tracked separately on den-hoag-4kh.12).
PRESERVED VERBATIM: section 11.2's "but it would be the right one at equal cost" (:1520) — the C7-correct
posture, construction as warrant and cost as corroboration. Section 9's two-cycle observation (:1320-1321).

════ ★★ PROCESS FINDING — THE MOST REUSABLE OUTPUT OF THIS ARC ════
"The document has not outgrown review, but only because of a property that could easily be lost."
1606 lines is far past what a reviewer can responsibly read end to end each round. WHAT MAKES IT REVIEWABLE
IS THAT THE VERIFICATION SURFACE IS SMALL AND SEPARABLE: section 3.1's executable core is SEVENTEEN LINES —
mechanically extractable, transcribable into a runnable file, and hashable. EVERY SUBSTANTIVE VERDICT ACROSS
FOUR ROUNDS RESTS ON RUNNING THOSE SEVENTEEN LINES, NOT ON READING THE PROSE.
The risk this document actually exhibited is PROSE DRIFTING FROM EQUATIONS — round 2 was five sections added
around a byte-unchanged equation block, asserting properties it did not have. The control that catches it is
what was used from round 3 on: AN MD5-ANCHORED FREEZE PLUS A COMMENTS-STRIPPED DIFF OF THE EXECUTABLE LINES.
RECOMMENDATION ADOPTED INTO THE GATE: treat "executable lines, comments stripped, hashed" as THE REVIEWABLE
ARTEFACT, and the prose as commentary that must be re-derivable from it. If a future revision makes the
executable core non-extractable — inlining equations into paragraphs, or splitting them across sections —
the document becomes genuinely unreviewable at this length, and THAT is the point at which to split the spec
rather than grow it.

════ REVIEWER COVERAGE — HONEST, AND STATED AS A LIMIT ON THE VALIDATION ════
READ IN FULL this round: section 3.1's equation block (extracted and hashed) and its binding-scope pin
(:305-332); "Scope of everything ELSE" (:425-467); the reverse-reachability paragraph (:743-818); the
section 4 cost table (:849-866).
TARGETED GREP/EXCERPT ONLY: the timing text (:376-395), section 11.2's preserved sentence, section 9's
preserved observation, the genericClosure absence.
NOT READ THIS ROUND: sections 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, most of 9, 10, 11.1, 11.3, 12 — THE MAJORITY OF 1606 LINES.
Verified against the 1227- and 1466-line versions in earlier rounds and specific corrections confirmed by
grep, but the ~140 lines added between 1466 and 1606 were NOT read except where they fall in the sections
above. ★ "A DEFECT INTRODUCED IN THAT DELTA, INSIDE A SECTION I DID NOT OPEN, WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN CAUGHT. I
am stating that as a limit on this VALIDATED, not as a hedge."
RAN FRESH: the freeze-anchor hash; the equation-block extraction and executable-line hash; the
dependentsOf/impactOf/reachableFrom substitution across M/R/A/Z and all three section 9 fixture rows; the
condEdges-is-a-function check with sccOf as control.
CARRIED, NOT RE-RUN: the twelve shapes (executable lines unchanged); the round-2 Mokhov verification; the
k-diamond series and wall-clock. "Page 7" and the DOI remain unverified in every round — not locally
checkable, no network call ever made.
DISCIPLINE: every absence claim positive-controlled in the same run (expandPreorder 45 / condensation 39
against the genericClosure zero; sccOf against condEdges; A->B fold success against the A->A abort).
.worktrees/ excluded throughout. The ordering probe used M/R/A/Z, never A/B/C — WHICH IS WHAT MADE THE
dependentsOf SUBSTITUTION VISIBLE AT ALL.

GATE REVIEW #5 (FINAL) — W2 F1 class-reroute confluence design, at the 1664-line anchor.
VERDICT: VALIDATED — THE DESIGN. Confirms review #4's verdict against the later artefact.

SCOPE, unchanged and still binding: section 3.1's NINETEEN executable equation lines and the properties
claimed for them. NOT an implementation — none exists; section 9's test plan is specified but UNWRITTEN; all
parity is via a verbatim transcription of section 3.1 and the synthetic internal.classModulesBuilder
harness, NEVER A LIVE mkDen FLEET. A SEPARATE GATE IS OWED ON THE IMPLEMENTATION.
Anchor verified twice two seconds apart: 1664 lines, md5 34fec05e0ea13cc511808881c1178a65, mtime 18:16:31.
Equation block extracted, comment-stripped, diffed against the 1606 extraction: IDENTICAL, md5
9a7b62f73db397487c18fe99fae754ed both times. The twelve shapes were NOT re-run; round-3 execution carries.

SEQUENCING CORRECTION — THE ORCHESTRATOR WAS WRONG, THE ANCHOR MECHANISM WORKED. The orchestrator told the
reviewer its round-4 md5 was stale and that stopping would have been correct. IT WAS NOT STALE AT CHECK
TIME: all four fields verified matching (1606 lines, 111067 bytes, 28 headings, mtime 18:10:51.882547534,
md5 c6ab541805...). The file moved to 34fec05e at 18:16:31, AFTER review #4 completed. So review #4 was
rendered against a genuinely settled file and the freeze anchor did exactly its job. Recorded because the
orchestrator's "third sequencing failure" self-attribution was itself an error.

REVIEWER CORRECTED ITS OWN COUNT: "17 executable lines" in round 4 was a MISCOUNT; it is 19, as the author
stated. The md5 was identical across both rounds so the CONTENT claim was correct — only the count was not.
The reviewer recorded it against itself, having held every number in this document to reproduction.

════ THE ORCHESTRATOR'S PRIORITY QUESTION — DOES THE DOCUMENT FOLLOW ITS OWN TIMING RULE? NO, TWICE ════
The rule (:384-390): floor-dominated figures "labelled as environment-specific" and "never load-bearing";
work-dominated figures "quoted only alongside its independently-measured counterpart". Most of the file
complies and several sites are exemplary (:400 quotes 13.556s against 12.473s; :450-451 label the two rows
explicitly; :315's equation comment now reads "28.872s per-class against a per-node form at its
environment's floor", confirming the bare 0.334-vs-28.872 comparison was genuinely removed).

★★ E1 :1452 — A WORK-DOMINATED ABSOLUTE QUOTED BARE, no counterpart, no label:
   "16,777,213 answers and 50 SECONDS at k = 22 (a 67-node graph), against 67 nodes and UNMEASURABLE TIME
    for expandPreorder."
   The document knows the compliant phrasing and uses it 1050 lines earlier at :401-403 — "queryPaths is in
   the tens of seconds IN EVERY ENVIRONMENT while expandPreorder remains indistinguishable from THAT
   ENVIRONMENT'S floor ... not a claim about any particular floor value." Section 3.1 got it right; section
   11 states the discarded form. THE "STATES A DISCIPLINE AND VIOLATES IT TWO SECTIONS LATER" FAILURE.
   ★★★ AND THIS FIGURE WAS REPORTED REMOVED. IT WAS ONLY REWORDED. Greps: `~50` = 0 hits; `50 second` = 1
   hit. THE TILDE WENT, THE CLAIM STAYED. A verification grep for "~50 seconds" returns zero and READS AS
   SUCCESSFUL REMOVAL. That is VERIFICATION-PREDICATE BLINDNESS — the predicate stopped matching for a
   reason unrelated to the claim's removal. Named, repeated failure mode in this project, here caught only
   because the reviewer ran an EXHAUSTIVE regex sweep for timing figures rather than checking the reported
   string.
E2 :410 — a floor-dominated figure unlabelled: "builtins.length ... gives the same timing as the full
   deepSeq (0.010s either way at k = 20)". 0.010s sits BELOW the 0.011-0.175s import-floor range the same
   passage quotes two paragraphs earlier, so it is floor-dominated by the document's own definition, and it
   is doing work (establishing an equality). Milder — the substantive point is argued structurally in the
   next clause — but unlabelled.
E3 — review #4's isSink cost-row erratum STILL UNFIXED: "O(1) ... two attr reads on cond" is wrong on both
   halves. condEdges = condEdgesOf at gen-graph/lib/global.nix:192 is the RAW RECOMPUTING function, not the
   memoized condMat at :171 (used at :173, never exported); builtins.isFunction cond.condEdges = true.
   Bounded by O(n + |R|), absorbed by the |classNames|*O(n + |R|) term, so THE SHIPPED-COST ROW IS
   UNAFFECTED — one intermediate row overstates its precision.
ALL THREE ARE EDITS TO TEXT, NOT TO DESIGN. Dispatched. Why not REDESIGN: the errata live in prose that does
not specify the mechanism; the equation block is byte-identical to what was executed and re-verified by
diff; no C1-C7 predicate trips; and E1's compliant phrasing already exists in the document, so the fix is
deleting a clause.

════ C7-a PASSES at this anchor ════
Re-counted with the reviewer's own controls INCLUDING A ZERO CONTROL proving the predicate discriminates:
dependentsOf 13 · impactOf 5 · reachableFrom 6 · transpose 4 · genericClosure 4 · dependentsFrontier 1 ·
canReach 1 · pathsBetween 1 · reachableWhere 2 · coScc 1 · coneRank 1 — controls expandPreorder 47,
condensation 39, ZZZNOTATOKEN 0.
Rejections re-verified at source: global.nix:81 sorts · traverse.nix:8 + :19 drops startId · global.nix:196
impactOf = dependentsOf · traverse.nix:22-23 reachableWhere inherits · traverse.nix:3-4 "~4-5x faster than
Nix-level BFS on large graphs" VERBATIM. The preorder.nix:1-11 quotation is VERBATIM; its ellipsis elides
only a parenthetical describing what the combinators ARE, not a qualifier on the claim.
★ THE FRAMING IS STRONGER THAN THE CITATION THE REVIEWER ITSELF PROPOSED IN ROUND 3 — :778-781: "this is not
a slower alternative being passed over; it is a FASTER one being declined. That is the case this check
exists to catch", followed by the point that the speed is "bought by discarding exactly what the design
requires" — order, which genericClosure "structurally cannot express."
Section 9's reflexive-member row landed and is CORRECTLY SCOPED (:1319-1330): it states plainly that the
property was ALREADY covered, that three existing rows fail under substitution, and that "what was missing
was any row stating that it is what they hold." It does NOT retroactively claim the gap the reviewer falsely
reported in round 3.
C7-b PASSES: binding scope pinned inside the equation block (:311-317) and again in a dedicated section,
marked "part of the design, not implementation latitude", misreading annotated at the point of misreading
(:318-320); cost table prices keyedBucketsOf both ways; 29.447s recorded against 28.872s.
C7 core and C1-C6 discharged, carried against a byte-identical executable block.

════ ★★★ THE PROCESS FINDING — SHARPENED, AND THE REVIEWER NOW JUDGES IT THE MORE IMPORTANT ONE ════
452 -> 611 -> 1227 -> 1466 -> 1606 -> 1664. Six versions, five reviews.
THE DESIGN HAS BEEN STABLE FOR THREE VERSIONS — the executable core is nineteen lines with an IDENTICAL md5
at 1606 and 1664, and the round-3 execution verification has carried unchanged through two revisions.
EVERYTHING THAT GREW IS PROSE, now 3.7x its original size. AND EVERY DEFECT FOUND IN THE LAST TWO ROUNDS IS
PROSE-VS-PROSE INCONSISTENCY: a rule stated in section 3.1 and violated in section 11; a cost row
contradicting the library it cites; a figure believed removed that was only reworded.
"EQUATION VERIFICATION NO LONGER FINDS ANYTHING, AND PROSE AUDITING IS UNBOUNDED. I read perhaps a fifth of
this file this round and found two rule violations in it. I cannot tell you what a full read would find, and
at 1664 lines growing ~10% per revision, neither can the next reviewer."
RECOMMENDATION, ADOPTED: FREEZE THE PROSE OR SPLIT THE DOCUMENT. The reviewable artefact is the
comments-stripped executable block plus its hash — that has worked flawlessly four rounds running and takes
minutes. The prose needs a different discipline than adversarial review, because what it now fails at is
INTERNAL CONSISTENCY ACROSS 1600 LINES, which review SAMPLES rather than covers.
★ THE HONEST POSITION, WHICH THIS BEAD NOW RECORDS: THE GATE IS VERIFYING THE EQUATIONS AND *SAMPLING* THE
PROSE. Anyone reading VALIDATED should read it as: the nineteen executable lines are verified by execution
and diff; the surrounding 1645 lines are sampled.
ORCHESTRATOR ACTION TAKEN: prose frozen PERMANENTLY after E1/E2/E3 and a change log. Anything further goes
in a NEW document. The extractable-hashable-equation-core property is required of future specs.

════ COVERAGE — HONEST ════
READ AT THIS ANCHOR: the equation block (extracted, stripped, hashed, diffed); the wall-clock rule and its
evidence (:373-412); the per-node/per-class section (:445-460); section 3.5's reverse-reachability and
genericClosure passages (:767-813); section 9's reflexive-member and fan-out rows (:1319-1345); section 11's
instrument comparison (:1440-1462).
NOT READ: sections 1, 2, 4 except the cost table, 5, 6, 7, 8, most of 9, 10, 11.1, 11.3, 12 — THE LARGE
MAJORITY OF 1664 LINES. Specific corrections confirmed by targeted grep. An EXHAUSTIVE regex sweep for
TIMING FIGURES was run across the whole file, which is how E1 and E2 surfaced. The ~58 lines added between
1606 and 1664 were NOT read except where they fall in the sections above — a defect in that delta, in an
unopened section and not matching a timing pattern, WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN CAUGHT.
RAN FRESH: anchor hash x2; equation extraction, hash and diff against the 1606 copy; exhaustive timing-figure
regex sweep with removal checks and a positive control; C7-a family re-count with a zero control; verbatim
diff of the preorder.nix:1-11 and traverse.nix:3-4 quotations against source.
CARRIED, NOT RE-RUN: the twelve shapes; the dependentsOf/impactOf/reachableFrom M/R/A/Z substitution and the
three section 9 fixture rows; the condEdges-is-a-function check; the k-diamond series; the round-2 Mokhov
verification. "Page 7" and the DOI remain UNVERIFIED in every round — not locally checkable, no network call
