title: [codebase-memory-mcp] Nix def extraction drops every definition in a function-headed file
description:
Measured against codebase-memory-mcp HEAD (d587deab). If a .nix file's ROOT expression is a function (the standard '{ prelude, ... }:' library/module header), every Function def in that file is dropped. Nesting depth is not the trigger.

Minimal repro (indexed with mode=full):
  bare.nix           let ... in       -> alpha, beta        FOUND
  attrset.nix        { ... }          -> epsilon, zeta      FOUND
  nested_let.nix     let in let       -> theta              FOUND
  wrapped.nix        { prelude }: let -> (none)             MISSING
  wrapped_attrset.nix { prelude }: {} -> (none)             MISSING

Blast radius: 242 of 320 .nix files in den-hoag (76%). Whole-repo effect: 39 Functions from 6 of 332 files, 26 of them from lib/errors.nix (which happens to open with a bare let). gen-scope 22, gen-schema 11 — same suppression.

Likely site: internal/cbm/extract_defs.c:827 — the Nix resolver only fires when ts_node_parent(function_expression) is a 'binding'. A file's top-level '{ prelude }:' is itself a function_expression matching nix_func_types whose parent is source_expression, so it resolves null. Behavior is proven; the mechanism by which that failure suppresses the subtree is NOT yet confirmed and is the first thing the spike must establish.

Secondary, separate: nix_var_types = {"binding"} has no Nix name resolver at HEAD either — Variable count stayed at 10 across the version bump.
design:
ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, extract_defs.c:6750-6769):

    if (cbm_kind_in_set(node, spec->function_node_types)) {
        if (!is_template_class_node(node, ctx->language)) {
            extract_func_def(ctx, node, spec);
            bool descend_into_func = (WOLFRAM || TYPESCRIPT || JAVASCRIPT || TSX || ADA);
            if (!descend_into_func) { continue; }   // <-- abandons the subtree
        }
    }

Nix is absent from descend_into_func. A Nix library/module file's ROOT expression is itself a
function_expression ({ pkgs, lib, ... }: <body>), which matches nix_func_types. extract_func_def
resolves a null name (the resolver at :827 requires ts_node_parent == "binding"; here the parent
is source_expression), mints nothing, and then the continue abandons the entire file body. Nothing
below the header is ever walked.

WHY IT SHIPPED — tests/test_extraction.c:1137 TEST(nix_function) is the only Nix extraction test.
Its fixture is function-headed (the broken shape), its binding is an application not a function
(hello = pkgs.writeShellScriptBin ...), and it asserts only ASSERT_NOT_NULL + ASSERT_FALSE(has_error).
It omits ASSERT(has_def(r, "Function", ...)) — the helper every adjacent language test uses. The
test cannot fail for this bug.

FIX (candidate, one line): add CBM_LANG_NIX to descend_into_func. Inner curried lambdas
(f = a: b: ...) have a function_expression parent, resolve no name, and mint nothing, so the extra
descent should add defs without adding noise — VERIFY this empirically, do not assume.

FIX MUST ALSO: replace the nix_function test fixture with real function bindings and add
has_def assertions; add cases for all five shapes in the repro matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Spike identifies the exact suppression mechanism with evidence; spec proposes a fix that makes wrapped.nix/wrapped_attrset.nix yield their defs without regressing the three passing shapes
notes:
FIX VERIFIED. One line: add CBM_LANG_NIX to descend_into_func (extract_defs.c:6764). Branch spike/nix-function-header-defs, build at scratchpad/cbm-fix.

Repro matrix, patched — 8/8 expected defs, zero extras:
  bare.nix            alpha, beta      (unchanged)
  attrset.nix         epsilon, zeta    (unchanged)
  nested_let.nix      theta            (unchanged)
  wrapped.nix         gamma, delta     WAS EMPTY
  wrapped_attrset.nix eta              WAS EMPTY

den-hoag, mode=fast:
                   v0.8.1(live)   HEAD    HEAD+fix
  Function              7 (py)      39       1871
  CALLS                 8           38       1424
  files with defs       1            6        253 / 332
  nodes/edges       818/1415   846/1529  2678/8939

Quality: lib/identity.nix yields exactly the 7 functions nil documentSymbol reports, plus one real
inner binding. Zero anonymous/malformed names across all 1871 (regex probe for empty/_/punctuation
returned 0). Over-minting from curried inner lambdas did NOT materialise — they resolve no name.

Change is gated on ctx->language == CBM_LANG_NIX, so cross-language regression is structurally
impossible. REMAINING GATE before PR: run make -f Makefile.cbm test-focused TEST_SUITES=extraction,
and rewrite TEST(nix_function) (fixture is function-headed AND binds a non-function AND asserts no
defs) to cover all five shapes with has_def assertions.

SEPARATE, NOT FIXED: nix_var_types = {"binding"} still has no Nix name resolver — Variable stayed
at 10 across all three builds. Needs its own attrpath resolver, mirroring extract_defs.c:827.

Artefacts: repro repo scratchpad/nixrepro (5 shapes, git-init'd); baseline build scratchpad/cbm-head; patched build scratchpad/cbm-fix; all indexes isolated via CBM_CACHE_DIR so the live index was never touched.

SHIPPED to fork: https://github.com/sini/codebase-memory-mcp @ spike/nix-function-header-defs
  3822ae42 fix(extract): descend past a Nix file's root function so its bindings are reached
  f79ea8ed test(nix): cover the five root shapes, and assert defs rather than absence of error
Both carry Signed-off-by (DCO 1.1 required by CONTRIBUTING.md).

NEGATIVE CONTROL PASSED — with 3822ae42 reverted, only the three new function-header tests fail,
each on its own assertion (gamma / eta / iota); the three pre-existing shapes stay green. With it
applied: 259 passed, 0 failed. (Two objectscript UBSan warnings in vendored grammars are
pre-existing and non-failing.)

nix-config ce852380 carries the patch via pkgs/overlays.nix + pkgs/patches/. Verified end to end:
the cortex-built binary (/nix/store/hkxb8ay9x4md53k6s788gklp4h799aq0-...) returns all 8 repro defs
including both wrapped shapes.

NOT DONE: upstream PR to DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp not opened — awaiting go-ahead.

title: [gen-merge] mergeOptionDecls silently right-biases a redeclared option; nixpkgs throws
description:
DIVERGENCE, measured 2026-07-27 by the den-hoag-y53 review (finding F3).

gen-merge mergeOptionDecls is plain `av // bv` (gen-merge/lib/modules.nix:100-121). Two modules declaring the SAME option merge attribute-wise, last-wins per attribute, with NO error. nixpkgs throws in that situation: mergeOptionDecls guards on bothHave 'default'/'example'/'description'/'apply' and raises "The option 'X' in 'A' is already declared in 'B'" (nixpkgs/lib/modules.nix:1035-1040), never reaching mergedType = t.typeMerge.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (the concrete case that surfaced it): under gen-merge, one declaration's extra option attribute can survive while ANOTHER declaration's TYPE survives — the option record and its type come from different declarations and silently disagree. In the probe, an attached descriptor read 'rack' while the instances were 'blade' and hashed as blade (id_hash matched blade exactly). No error, no warning. Positive control in the same run: two declarations with no descriptor throw identically under nixpkgs, so the nixpkgs throw is pre-existing and not descriptor-induced.

WHY THIS IS NOW P1 RATHER THAN A CORNER: owner ruling 2026-07-27 — den-hoag internally dogfoods gen modules EXCLUSIVELY, nixpkgs lib only when translating or testing. As internals move onto gen-merge, the permissive path stops being the rare one and becomes the normal one. Under nixpkgs the redeclaration aborts loud; under gen-merge it is silent and the surviving record can be internally inconsistent.

SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THE DESCRIPTOR CASE. This is about ANY option redeclared across two modules — the descriptor was only the instrument that revealed it. Any consumer relying on nixpkgs' already-declared abort loses it on the gen substrate.

NOT YET DECIDED (needs design, do not implement from this bead): whether gen-merge should adopt nixpkgs' bothHave guard verbatim, adopt a narrower rule (e.g. throw only when the two declarations carry different types), or make the divergence explicit and documented. gen-merge already carries DELIBERATE divergences from nixpkgs, so 'match nixpkgs' is not automatically the answer — see the protocol series 8daa25d..e3ac5e5 and den-hoag-1qh.

Related: den-hoag-y53 (where it was found; its descriptor would be sole authority on a path this makes unreliable), den-hoag-1qh (other gen-merge/nixpkgs divergences).

title: [gen-schema] Registry descriptor: mkInstanceRegistry records kind + index on the declaration
description:
SPEC (pre-review, no code): papers/den-architecture/plans/2026-07-27-kind-binding-structural-recovery-plan.md

GAP (measured 2026-07-27): gen-schema has NO registry-level surface. Schema-level introspection exists (_kindNames/_topology/_edges/_roots/_leaves, entry-type.nix:284-320) and instances are first-class (id_hash, _identity, strict, refs, derive) — but mkInstanceRegistry returns a bare merge.mkOption (instance.nix:476-488). Kinds and instances are introspectable; the registry between them is anonymous.

Consequence for ANY consumer, not just den: 'options.things = mkInstanceRegistry schema.thing {}' — nothing says 'things' holds 'thing', so recovering the kind from a declared surface requires reflecting over instance VALUES and matching id_hash per candidate kind. O(kinds), must be hand-totalised (missing attribute is not a throw, tryEval cannot catch it), and cannot answer for an EMPTY registry.

DESIGN: mkInstanceRegistry's returned option carries __registry = { kind; index.shape = "flat"; }.
On the DECLARATION — not per instance (denormalizes one registry-level fact across N records, grows every consumer's instance surface, still cannot answer for an empty registry) and not on the instance TYPE (that surface composes structurally via mixins/open kinds; a name on it re-nominalizes it). index is the extension point for den-hoag-8rf composite registries, not a constant.

REJECTED ROUTE, recorded: _kind on every instance shipped as gen-schema 66eb255 and was REVERTED (6732239, both on origin) on five owner objections — denormalization; observable surface growth (3 den-hoag fixtures reddened); non-total for empty registries; wrong direction of contamination; re-nominalizing a structurally-composed surface. Do not re-propose it. Also rejected: extending den.schema.<kind> (that is the v1-compat PUBLIC interface), and a den-hoag-owned registry constructor (den-hoag special case where a general library answer exists).

Blocks den-hoag-m0a (which then deletes registryKindOf, registryKindsFor, registryKindsOf, instanceMatchesKind and the probeFor cross-kind widening) and den-hoag-8rf.

NEXT STEP IS REVIEW OF THE SPEC, not implementation — see spec §9 open questions (carrier attribute naming; descriptor survival under two declarations of one option, currently UNMEASURED; whether index earns its place before 8rf; whether the descriptor should carry more than kind).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (2026-07-27): VERDICT REVISE. Nine probes, read-only. Carrier MECHANISM is
sound; three spec claims are false as written and two §6 design decisions are blocking.

F1 — BLOCKING. mkDen-direct has no option surface, and §6's deletion breaks the R9 STRICT-SURFACE GATE.
  compile.nix:1921 folds ing.discoveredRegistryKeys into knownSurfaceKeys; its own comment at :1920 says
  "mkDen-direct fixtures set neither; the discovered set alone classifies". The chain is
  discoveredRegistryKeys <- instanceKeyMap <- discoverKeyFor <- instanceMatchesKind — ALL of which §6
  deletes. Result: every mkDen-direct custom registry namespace becomes an UNKNOWN SURFACE KEY and R9
  ABORTS ON LEGITIMATE CONFIG. Not a mis-key: a hard abort. 44 ci fixtures call mkDen directly, 3 call
  ingest directly. Compounding: flake-module.nix:234-237 evalV1Raw returns .config.den and DISCARDS
  .options, so even a userModule that declared its registry option cannot be read today; and
  ci/tests/compat-host-registry.nix:200-204 hand-builds instances with a literal id_hash and no
  constructor, so there is nothing to attach a descriptor to.
  RESOLUTION: descriptor is the BRIDGE ARM ONLY; value-reflection stays as the mkDen-direct arm.
  ingest.nix:528 ALREADY has the right shape — registryKindsOf v1Decls // (v1Decls._registryKinds or {}),
  bridge wins. Feed the descriptor into _registryKinds and change nothing else. §6's "delete
  registryKindsOf/instanceMatchesKind" and "abort on BOTH paths" both go.

F2 — BLOCKING. §6 contradicts itself on empty registries.
  §6 keeps isInstanceRegistry AND claims empty registries now resolve. isInstanceRegistry requires
  v != {} (ingest.nix:322-326) and BOTH discovery gates filter on it (bridge.nix:271-273,
  ingest.nix:341-350). Measured: empty registry has descriptor_kind="cluster" but
  isInstanceRegistry=false, so the key is filtered BEFORE the descriptor is read. §8's own falsifier
  ("an empty registry resolving") FAILS AS SPECIFIED. The descriptor IS total — §3's design claim and
  §5's objection-3 answer both hold — the §6 GATE is what defeats it.
  RESOLUTION: gate on descriptor presence over declaredDenKeys (bridge.nix:226-228, option-derived,
  measured to contain the key when empty). Demote isInstanceRegistry to the mkDen-direct arm.

F3 — SERIOUS. The descriptor can SILENTLY DISAGREE with the type it describes.
  gen-merge mergeOptionDecls is plain av // bv (gen-merge/lib/modules.nix:100-121) — no throw, no
  typeMerge. Measured: descriptor survives from declaration A while the TYPE survives from B —
  descriptor_says="rack", instance fields are blade's, instance id_hash matches blade_hash exactly. No
  error, no warning. TODAY'S VALUE-REFLECTION GETS THIS RIGHT because it hashes the instance. So on this
  path the descriptor is strictly LESS ROBUST than what it replaces, and once registryKindOf is deleted
  nothing can detect the disagreement — a check that cannot fail. Narrow (needs a double declaration over
  different kinds) but the spec makes the descriptor SOLE AUTHORITY. Keep a cross-check, or make gen-merge
  throw on leaf redeclaration as nixpkgs does.

F4 — §9.2's PREMISE IS FALSE: typeMerge is never reached.
  nixpkgs path (the REAL bridge): two declarations HARD THROW at mergeOptionDecls' bothHave guard
  (nixpkgs/lib/modules.nix:1035-1040) because mkInstanceRegistry sets description AND default AND apply —
  never reaching mergedType = t.typeMerge. POSITIVE CONTROL same instrument same run: two BARE registries
  with no descriptor throw identically, so the throw is PRE-EXISTING, not descriptor-induced.
  gen-merge path: no throw and no typeMerge; descriptor survives from either side (one_desc / desc_then_bare
  / bare_then_desc all present=true kind="rack"; two_bare present=false — the instrument discriminates).
  The spec's contingency ("if lost, the abort fires loud") is accidentally right for nixpkgs (different
  cause) and WRONG for gen-merge (not lost — silently wrong, see F3).

F5 — §4.3 MISQUOTES compile.nix:913 and OMITS a consumer.
  Actual: registryBacked = k: (ing.instanceKeyMap ? ${k}) && (ing.registries.${k} or {}) != {} — a
  CONJUNCTION whose first conjunct is instanceKeyMap membership, and whose own comment at :903-909 calls
  it load-bearing ("TWO signals, both necessary"). NOT "registries ? k". Aside: instanceKeyMap is total
  over customKinds so the conjunct really means "is a custom kind" (the code's own comment is inaccurate,
  pre-existing) — but a DESCRIPTOR-derived map would NOT be total, so substituting changes the predicate's
  meaning. OMITTED CONSUMER: discoveredRegistryKeys (ingest.nix:557 -> compile.nix:1921) — §4.3 lists
  three, there are FOUR, and the fourth is what turns F1's deletion into an abort.

F6 — index.shape is SPECULATIVE; ship { kind }.
  mkInstanceRegistry builds merge.types.attrsOf (mkInstanceType ...) UNCONDITIONALLY
  (gen-schema/lib/instance.nix:477-489) — no other shape is constructible, so the field is a constant with
  one inhabitant emitted by the one constructor that can only produce that value. DECISIVE: the composite
  the spec points at — den.hosts.<system>.<hostname> — is NOT built by mkInstanceRegistry at all. It is
  den-hoag's own mkHostsOption (lib/compat/registry.nix:440-520, preprocessHosts :468, flattenRegistry
  :437). So index.shape on THIS constructor cannot describe the one composite registry that exists. The
  "breaking to add later" argument is weak at a measured 4 declarations, all owner-controlled.

F7 — __registry is SAFE; naming is off-convention.
  Measured safe on every axis: survives nixpkgs getSubOptions + fixupOptionType (modules.nix:1477-1481 is
  opt // {...}); survives gen-merge //; forces nothing; does NOT leak into docs (optionAttrSetToDocList
  emits a fixed record; ? __registry = false); gen-merge/lib/lint.nix has no unknown-attr validation.
  But gen-schema's own introspection convention is SINGLE underscore (_kindNames/_topology/_edges/_roots/
  _leaves, entry-type.nix:284-320 — the exact cite §2 uses). _registry matches the library's convention.

ANSWERED, priority Q2: the descriptor IS reachable without forcing apply or instances — measured with a
LIVE POISON CONTROL (apply = _: throw "APPLY-WAS-FORCED", instance tag = throw): descriptor read
success=true, poison value read success=false. BUT §6 names the wrong function: subOptionsOf
(bridge.nix:274-286) returns the ELEMTYPE's sub-options, one level BELOW where __registry lives. The right
level is denSubOptions.${k} = options.den.type.getSubOptions [ ] at bridge.nix:270, already computed.

SPEC CLAIMS THAT DO NOT REPRODUCE: §4.3's compile.nix:913 (F5); §4.1's "gen-merge submodule" — the real
bridge parent is nixpkgs lib.types.submodule (bridge.nix:447), which is what routes §9.2 to the THROWING
engine. The original probe modeled the wrong engine.
REPRODUCED: §4.1 substance; §4.2 (nix-config exactly 3 declarations — the 39 raw grep hits are .worktrees
copies; den-configs 19 -> 1 nixfos); §4.3's ingest.nix:414/428/554; §2's entry-type.nix cites and the
zero-hit registry-meta grep; §5's "both on origin"; §6's deployment coupling (nix-config declares its own
gen-schema.url at flake.nix:126, locked 103ea8897e10, BEHIND gen-schema HEAD).
TAKEN ON TRUST: §4.2's "den templates 13 -> 0" (no checkout at the expected path; a reachable backup has 10
templates with 0 declarations, so substance holds, count unverified).
CHECKED CLEAN: no consumer of the five discovery functions beyond the four in F5; nix-config's
den.users.registry and den.secretsConfig are NOT false positives for isInstanceRegistry.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (2026-07-27) — DOGFOODING (internals use gen modules exclusively; nixpkgs lib only when
translating or testing) ESCALATES review finding F3 rather than settling it.

F3 measured that gen-merge's mergeOptionDecls (`av // bv`) lets a descriptor survive from one declaration
while the TYPE survives from another, silently disagreeing — and that today's value-reflection gets that case
RIGHT because it hashes the instance. I had scoped that as narrow, on the reasoning that the real bridge
parent is nixpkgs `lib.types.submodule` (bridge.nix:447) and the nixpkgs path throws before merging.

Under the dogfooding ruling that reasoning inverts. As internals move onto gen-merge, the PERMISSIVE path
becomes the normal one, so a descriptor that is SOLE AUTHORITY sits on the engine that cannot detect its own
disagreement. F3 is therefore not a corner case to accept; it is the main path in the direction the codebase
is being taken.

The root is not in this bead's scope — it is gen-merge accepting a redeclared option at all, which affects
far more than descriptors. Filed as den-hoag-00g (P1), and this bead now DEPENDS on it: the descriptor should
not become sole authority on a path where redeclaration is silent.

Interaction with F1's resolution, which points the same way: F1 already reduces this bead to the BRIDGE ARM
ONLY, with value-reflection retained as the mkDen-direct arm (ingest.nix:528 already has the bridge-wins
shape). Keeping value-reflection alive on one arm means the cross-check F3 asks for is largely already there
— it is a question of whether the bridge arm ALSO cross-checks, not of building a new mechanism.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
SECOND INDEPENDENT REVIEW of rev 2 (2026-07-27): VERDICT REVISE (narrow). Twelve probes total. Design sound,
scope shrink right, three concrete defects — ONE INTRODUCED BY REV 2'S OWN F2 FIX.

F8 — BLOCKING, NEW. REV 2's F2 FIX RE-INTRODUCES .8's FAILURE MODE.
  Gating on declaredDenKeys admits EMPTY registries into registryKinds — that is the point of the fix. But
  bridgeKeyFor resolves kind->namespace with builtins.head (builtins.attrNames registryKinds), and attrNames
  is SORTED. Two registries of one kind with the empty one alphabetically first, and the POPULATED one is
  shadowed. Measured, with today's gate as a control in the same run:
      rev2 gate:   instanceKeyMap { rack = "archivedRacks"; }  registries.rack size 0  aborted false
      today:       instanceKeyMap { rack = "rackFarm"; }       registries.rack size 1
  The populated registry SILENTLY VANISHES. That is .8 — empty registries reaching the fleet empty —
  re-introduced by the fix for .8. Today it is masked only because isInstanceRegistry excludes empties.
  Realistic trigger: any rename/migration leaving both den.clusters and den.archivedClusters declared over
  kind cluster. Both legal; the descriptor makes both visible.
  RESOLUTION: the bijection invariant documented at registry.nix:394 must become a RUNTIME GUARD — a kind
  resolving to more than one declared registry is a NAMED ABORT, not `head`. Rev 2 cannot lean on the test
  pin (ci/tests/compat-registry-kind-bijection.nix) because the collision only becomes REACHABLE after this
  change. This is standing rule 5 verbatim: a documented invariant that nothing enforces is a comment.

F9 — THE F3 MITIGATION SENTENCE IS FALSE, and worse than "different code path".
  ingest.nix:539-552 discoverKeyFor binds `hits` in a lazy let and returns `bridged` when non-null, so the
  value-reflection branch is NEVER FORCED — not computed-and-discarded, never computed. Same at :528:
  `registryKindsOf v1Decls // (v1Decls._registryKinds or { })` does not force the left value for a key the
  right side covers. There is no comparison anywhere.
  Measured with a deliberately wrong _registryKinds.rackFarm = "blade" over rack-stamped instances: the SAME
  instance set is ingested under TWO kinds (blade and rack registries both size 1), aborted = false.
  RESOLUTION: DELETE the sentence "value-reflection remains live on the mkDen-direct arm, so the cross-check
  exists". It contradicts the bead's own §9.1. Honest position: the bridge arm has NO cross-check, and
  den-hoag-00g decides whether it needs one.

F10 — THE LOUDNESS CLAIM IS STILL NOT TOTAL, on the very arm rev 2 narrowed it to.
  The abort needs a registry-detector independent of the descriptor. isInstanceRegistry requires v != { },
  so EMPTY + DESCRIPTOR-LESS is INVISIBLE — precisely .8's population (an old-gen-schema consumer with an
  empty registry). Measured over six declared sub-options: clusters (desc, non-empty) fine; archivedClusters
  (desc, empty) fine; staleClusters (no desc, non-empty) aborts correctly; legacyClusters (no desc, EMPTY)
  SILENT.
  CONSTRUCTIVE FIX, measured in the same run: a TYPE-LEVEL structural test — does the option's elemType
  declare id_hash AND _identity — is total and value-free. True for all four real registries including the
  empty descriptor-less one; false for secretsConfig and users. No false positives. Costs nothing:
  bridge.nix subOptionsOf already computes exactly that getSubOptions for the stamps.
  NOTE: this is TYPE-level, not a value-shape heuristic, so it is not the looksLike/isNestedKey antipattern
  the effects audit objects to — but it is close enough in spelling that it must be NAMED to make the
  distinction obvious.

F11 — §6's STATED REASON FOR R9 SAFETY IS NOT THE OPERATIVE ONE.
  R9 on the bridge is carried by _declaredKeys (bridge.nix:360 -> compile.nix:1922), which is independent of
  the registryKinds producer — NOT by "nothing is deleted". And discoveredRegistryKeys DOES change on the
  bridge arm (measured: ["blade","archivedRacks"] vs control) because the PRODUCER is replaced even though no
  function is deleted. Harmless for R9, harmful in F8.
  RESOLUTION: state the operative fact, and give §8's R9 regression falsifier a BRIDGE-ARM TWIN — the
  mkDen-direct fixture it names cannot witness the bridge chain.

F12 — PLAUSIBLE. Rev 2 kept rung B's ORDER but dropped rev 1's deployment-coupling WHY, and the consequence
  is now sharper than rev 1's: nix-config's three registries are non-empty and descriptor-less until its lock
  moves, so under F10's table they hit the staleClusters row — a HARD ABORT ON THE CORPUS, not a soft miss,
  if C lands before B.

ANSWERED — priority 2's specific worry is UNFOUNDED: secretsConfig and users are cleanly excluded by the
descriptor filter (positive controls in the same run: ctl_secretsConfig_structural=false,
ctl_users_structural=false). What moves instead is staleClusters — non-empty, no descriptor — in today's set
and out of rev 2's. Intended, but a behaviour change for NON-empty registries.

SLOPPY CLAIM OF MINE, caught: rev 2 said the _registry rename was "measured safe either way", but rev 1 only
ever measured __registry. The reviewer re-ran it for the renamed form (survives getSubOptions through the
real nixpkgs-parent shape, forces nothing under a live poison control, doc_leaks=false). True now — but it
was asserted before it was measured.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
PARKED BY OWNER RULING 2026-07-27 (full text on den-hoag-4kh.7, which is closed as resolved).

★ THE NEW BLOCKING EDGE ON den-hoag-4kh ENCODES CORRECTNESS, NOT COST. Do not strip it as a cheapness
dependency. This project has previously had two blocking edges removed for encoding cost against the beads'
own text — this is not one of them, and here is the reason in full so a future sweep can check rather than
guess.

THEORY: compat is a THIN VAN WYK MAP ONTO THE KERNEL'S REPRESENTATION. This work hardens a compat seam
(y53: the bridge arm feeding _registryKinds at lib/compat/ingest.nix:528; 8rf: registry shape). A map onto
an unsettled denotation is built against a moving target — constructing a morphism WHOSE CODOMAIN IS STILL
CHANGING. The kernel-purity arc is precisely the work of fixing that codomain. So the dependency is not
"cheaper to do later", it is "the thing this maps onto is not yet defined".

UNPARK CONDITION — AN EVENT, NOT A DATE: when the kernel-purity arc has ruled on the registry/identity
representation these seams map onto.

WHAT DID NOT PARK, and why the distinction matters:
 · den-hoag-m0a STAYS OPEN as the defect record. A declared registry resolving to NO kind, reaching the
   fleet EMPTY with nothing reddening, is MEASURED FACT and belongs in the graph on its own — regardless of
   which remedy is chosen or whether the chosen remedy changes shape. SEPARATE THE DEFECT FROM THE REMEDY.
   Beads hold VALIDATED work: a measured defect qualifies, a proposed fix does not. Same treatment as
   den-hoag-4kh.12.
 · den-hoag-00g PROCEEDS. gen-merge silently right-biasing a redeclared option WHERE NIXPKGS ABORTS is a
   soundness violation in the algebra itself, independent of den-hoag's representation, so no kernel-shape
   risk attaches to fixing it. y53 was blocked on it regardless, so this ordering costs nothing even on the
   parked branch.

title: flake-system has instances in 12/12 configs — den-hoag treats it as instance-less; flake is NOT the same case
description:
flake-system has instances in 12 OF 12 measured configs (1 to 9 each;
nvf-standalone has 9). IT IS THE SINGLE MOST UNIVERSAL ENTITY KIND IN DEN.
den-hoag treats it as a declared kind with ZERO instances.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md (papers 9eb5439),
measured across den's own 13 templates + a sample of external configs from
~/Documents/repos/den-configs (8 templates + 3 external + nix-config produced
full IRs).

★ DO NOT CONFLATE WITH `flake`. The map separates three claims that were being
treated as one:
  flake        NOT a divergence -- v1 also has zero flake scopes in 12/12. The
               flake entity is the ROOT OF RESOLUTION and is excluded from the
               topology BY CONSTRUCTION (capture.nix:105 roots the walk with an
               empty ctx so mkScopeId returns ""; fleet-ir.nix:91 filters "" and
               "__unscoped"). den-hoag MATCHES v1 here.
  flake-system REAL divergence. 12/12 configs. THIS BEAD.
  fleet        real but rare -- 1 instance in 2 of 12, but one is den's own
               fleet-demo template, so it is den-INTRINSIC vocabulary rather
               than a nix-config idiosyncrasy.
  flake-parts  1 of 12 (nix-config only). den-hoag DOES register it
               (lib/compat/builtins.nix:436 flake-parts.isEntity = true).

WHY IT MATTERS: den-hoag-9xo.13's whole "head-less chain" analysis rested on
flake/fleet/flake-system all being instance-less. That is TRUE of flake by
design, and FALSE of flake-system in every config anyone has measured. Any
reasoning that grouped the three needs re-checking against this split.

UNVERIFIED, and stated in the map rather than rounded off: den-hoag's OWN
instance counts were not measured -- den-hoag has no IR emitter and building one
was out of scope, so "declared kinds with ZERO instances" is carried from the
brief, not independently confirmed on den-hoag. SETTLES IT: a den-hoag-side
equivalent of scopeEntityKind, dumped for the same fixtures and compared
kind-by-kind.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: Off-trace guarantee is part law part description: the filter admits inverse and member edges
description:
THE OFF-TRACE GUARANTEE IS PART LAW, PART DESCRIPTION -- and the half that is
description is a live hole.

MEASURED (a15-spike, 2026-07-27; papers plans/2026-07-27-a15-spike.md section 3,
papers 5f825a9).

Law A15's byte-identity is justified "by construction" at lib/default.nix:1871,
:2015, :2621 and concern-relations.nix:69 -- things kept OFF output.edgesForRoot
CANNOT perturb the parity oracle.

MEASURED: a live filter DOES neutralise a spliced FORWARD relation edge. That
half is real mechanism.

BUT THE SAME FILTER:
  - ADMITS that relation's INVERSE edges (D1 -- the inverse-edge hole).
    concern-relations.nix:6 states the design: "NO second kind is registered..."
    The inverse edges produced by the gen-graph transpose are not covered by the
    same filter that covers the forward direction.
  - ADMITS `member` edges.

⇒ HALF THE POOL IS PROTECTED BY MECHANISM, HALF BY THE FACT THAT NOBODY WIRED
IT. The comment reads as a guarantee over the whole pool and is one over part of
it.

This is the arc's own rule caught by measurement: A COMMENT DESCRIBING AN
ABSENCE IS NOT A LAW. "Not spliced into the live trace, so byte-identity holds
by construction" is true of what is currently spliced, not of what may be.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: den-hoag-9xo.30's candidate S declares a
relation `structural` so its forward edges bear reachability. If the inverse
edges of that same relation remain on-trace-eligible while the forward ones are
filtered, the partition is inconsistent -- the relation is half-protected. D1 is
therefore a PREREQUISITE of S, not an adjacent nit.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): extend the filter to cover the transpose's
output for the same relation, so the forward/inverse pair is partitioned
together. Arm it both ways -- a forward edge that must be filtered, and an
inverse edge of the same relation that must be filtered for the same reason.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: Bridge-path registry mis-key is silent; the R9 loud-miss does not hold where the corpus runs
description:
A consumer-declared registry that resolves to NO kind is SILENT on the bridge path, so the R9 loud-miss property the ingest code documents does not hold where the corpus actually runs.

MEASURED, two paths, same defect, different outcomes:
  mkDen-direct: den.siteClusters resolves to no kind -> surface totality (C1) ABORTS NAMED, "unknown den.siteClusters".
  bridge:       den.environments resolves to no kind -> registry silently EMPTY. registries.environment 2 -> 0, scopeRoots 47 -> 45, nixosConfigurations UNCHANGED (7 hosts, exit 0), ci 0 / parity 0 / ship-gate true.

MECHANISM: on the bridge path the namespace is in _declaredKeys (bridge.nix reads the declared sub-option names off options.den and passes them to compile), so surface-totality classifies it legitimate whether or not discovery resolved it. On the mkDen-direct path there are no _declaredKeys, so an undiscovered registry is an unknown key and aborts.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is exactly how den-hoag-9xo.27's four green commits happened. The corpus reaches den-hoag ONLY through the bridge, so the one path that can fail loud is the one the corpus never takes.

CANDIDATE FIX (owner call, behaviour change): a declared den.<key> holding id_hash-bearing instances that matches no kind is, on any real consumer, a defect -- discovery failed. Treating it as an abort rather than an empty registry would restore the loud-miss on the path that matters. The risk to weigh is a consumer that legitimately declares an instance-registry-shaped namespace for a kind it never declares; whether that is a real shape is unmeasured.

NOT the same as den-hoag-9xo.27's fixture work, which is shipped: compat-registry-kind-bijection catches a mis-keying fold at the fold. It cannot catch a mis-key arising anywhere else on the bridge's source derivation, because there is no observable consequence on that path.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ RULING (2026-07-27): THE BRIDGE'S SILENCE IS A PARITY DEFECT. Making the miss
loud is a FIX, not an owner-facing behaviour change to weigh. Measured against
den v1 at 11866c16; full detail papers plans/2026-07-27-v1-registry-namespace-parity.md
(papers af215a9).

Q-A, three rows, one harness, live calibration control:
  namespace + kind DECLARED           -> WORKS, instance readable, kind enumerated
  namespace + kind UNDECLARED, UNREAD -> tolerated; kind list CLEAN, no invented kind
  namespace + kind UNDECLARED, READ   -> ABORTS: attribute 'noSuchKind' missing
THERE IS NO FOURTH ROW. v1 never serves accepted-but-empty.

Q-B: the shape is NOT EXPRESSIBLE in v1, which is stronger than "v1 does not do
it". mkInstanceRegistry TAKES THE KIND VALUE as its argument, so a namespace
cannot exist without a declared kind. Expressibility checked, not
corpus-presence -- the stated parity bar. v1's own surface declares exactly two
built-in registries (options.den.hosts/homes, modules/options.nix:71-72) and
NEITHER uses mkInstanceRegistry (0 hits tree-wide against a positive control of
5 mkInstanceType hits).

★★ BUT THE BINARY UNDERSTATES IT, AND THIS IS THE REAL FINDING.
v1 is neither silent NOR loud about namespace resolution -- IT NEVER PERFORMS
IT. The binding is established WHEN THE REGISTRY IS CONSTRUCTED FROM THE KIND
VALUE. No resolution step, so nothing that can fail. "Parity on the abort axis"
is the wrong axis; the right comparison is OUTCOME: v1 never silently serves a
wrong (empty) answer for a registry the consumer declared. The bridge does.

v1 is kind-first everywhere: schema-util.nix:9-17 filters den.schema._kindNames
by isEntity and that list is what the whole pipeline consumes
(assemble-pipes.nix:327,364; policy/classify.nix:15; provide.nix:151;
compile-conditional.nix:122). Measured: entityKinds = ["home","host",
"siteCluster","user"] -- the KIND name; the namespace "siteClusters" appears
NOWHERE.

⇒ registryKindOf exists to answer "which kind does this namespace hold?" BY
VALUE-REFLECTION. v1 never asks, because it holds the answer STRUCTURALLY. The
uncatchable missing-attr, the four green commits, the silently-emptied
environment registry, and the mkDen-direct/bridge split are ALL DOWNSTREAM OF
ONE DESIGN CHOICE: re-deriving by discovery a binding the constructor already
carries.

★ AND BOTH CONSTRUCTION SITES ALREADY KNOW THE KIND NAME:
  lib/entity.nix:160         reads tree.config.den.schema.${kindName}
  lib/compat/ingest.nix:250  reads tree.config.den.schema.${kindName}

⇒ TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, and the second may dissolve this bead rather than fix it:
  (i)  MAKE THE MISS LOUD -- parity-justified by the above, restores R9 on the
       path the corpus uses. Narrow, safe, does not remove the discovery step.
  (ii) RECOVER THE STRUCTURAL BINDING -- stop discovering what the constructor
       already knows. Would remove registryKindOf's reason to exist and with it
       the whole class. UNEVALUATED; flagged by the investigator, explicitly
       outside its dispatch.
Decide (ii) before implementing (i), or (i) may cement the discovery step it
exists to compensate for.

★ DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE TO RECORD, IN DEN-HOAG'S FAVOUR: v1's abort is a BARE
`attribute 'noSuchKind' missing` -- unnamed, and tryEval CANNOT catch a
missing-attribute error (DL-HS-70 method note (c) -- the exact mechanism by
which .27 shipped green across four commits). den-hoag's errors.nix:188 NAMED
abort is STRICTLY BETTER. Matching v1's OUTCOME while improving its DIAGNOSTIC
is a divergence worth stating rather than discovering.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether some OTHER v1 consumer route reaches
namespace-without-kind. The constructor's signature is the general argument,
but one probe cannot supply a positive control for "some other route exists".

title: Embedding is a real dependency edge den-hoag does not model; half (1)'s rule is not computable without it
description:
BLOCKS den-hoag-9xo.9 half (1). Filed 2026-07-27 from the rev-8 design review
(papers c40569b).

Half (1)'s rule -- "a node materialises iff attached" over scope-root
construction -- IS WRONG AS STATED, because it would delete a root the corpus
needs. cortex-cuda's scope root must survive: its embedder cortex consumes its
RESOLVED MODULES via resolveEntity -> __denNode = "host:cortex-cuda" ->
outputFor."host:cortex-cuda", and cortex.microvm.guests is NON-EMPTY (measured,
length 1). Removing that root breaks cortex TODAY.

CORRECT RULE, both disjuncts:
    a node materialises iff it is ATTACHED **or** REQUIRED BY AN EMBEDDER

THE SECOND DISJUNCT IS NOT COMPUTABLE. den-hoag has no kernel-visible
embedding relation. Measured: ZERO den.relations / den.edges in the corpus, and
host.microvm.guests is `listOf raw` (den-hoag-9xo.16), so the embedding is
opaque to the graph -- it exists only inside an aspect's own value.

⇒ Embedding is a REAL DEPENDENCY EDGE that den-hoag does not model. The
embedder consumes the guest's resolved modules; that is exactly an edge. The
graph cannot see it, so no materialisation rule can respect it.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING (2026-07-27): state the rule with BOTH disjuncts and block
half (1) on this bead. Do NOT:
  - implement the single-disjunct rule and special-case the guest -- that is a
    name list, the shape this arc keeps deleting
  - scope the rule to fleets with no embedding -- a heuristic keyed on "did
    anything happen", already rejected once in this arc
  - weaken scope-root construction to placement -- BUILD and PLACEMENT are
    closed on their own merits (design nit 3) and the closures still hold

WHAT THIS NEEDS: a decision on whether embedding becomes a kernel-visible edge,
and if so what declares it. Adjacent to .16 (which is about the guest DELIVERY
being dead) but NOT the same bug -- .16 breaks something downstream of the
guests list; this is that the list is invisible to the graph in the first
place.

NOT SCHEDULED. Route 2 (the attachment mechanism, design sections 0-4,
SHIP-WITH-NITS) is INDEPENDENT of this and may proceed.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THE PROPOSED FIX (re-type microvm.guests as setOf (ref "host")) DOES NOT
WORK. Investigated read-only; verdict LARGE (new surface), not the one-line
type change the orchestrator proposed. Full detail + controls: papers
plans/2026-07-27-embedding-edge-investigation.md (papers 336a3ed).

FOUR INDEPENDENT BLOCKERS, each measured:

  B1  THE REF WALKER IS FLAT; THE OPTION IS NESTED.
      gen-schema/lib/ref.nix:86-94 is a ONE-LEVEL filterAttrs. `options.microvm`
      has no `.type`, so it is dropped WHOLE. getRefKind recurses type WRAPPERS
      (nestedTypes.elemType) and never the option TREE.
      Three positive controls in the same run -- flat inline, flat listOf, and
      flat-through-`imports` -- ALL THREE FIRE. Handed the nested node directly,
      the SAME walker returns ["guests"]. So nesting alone is the blocker.

  B2  den-hoag builds EVERY registry with `refs = { }` (lib/entity.nix:160,
      lib/compat/ingest.nix:250) and instance.nix:476 FORCES the check:
        error: gen-schema: mkInstanceRegistry: kind 'host' has ref field
        'guests' targeting kind 'host' but no refs.guests binding was provided
      Control (no ref field) -> registry evaluates. host->host is also
      self-referential, so it needs a `deferred` binding (instance.nix:223-237).

  B3  A REF TYPE IS NOT AN excludedType, so the field MOVES from the #70 raw
      channel INTO the deepSeq'd safe stamp -- the exact hazard
      registry.nix:224-232 forbids. Measured: raw -> rawTree={microvm.guests};
      ref -> rawTree={}, guests in safeTree. This makes den-hoag-9xo.16 WORSE.

  B4  `_refEdges` is KIND-level (host --guests--> host, entry-type.nix:359-370).
      .30 needs INSTANCE-level (host:cortex -> host:cortex-cuda). gen-schema has
      no such surface.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE ORCHESTRATOR'S BRIEF:
  - it is NOT an aspect-contributed option. It is den.schema.host.imports
    (microvm.nix:35, option :39-43).
  - that imports path is FULLY TRANSPARENT to the walker and is EXONERATED.

COMPAT DIRECTION IS OPPOSITE TO THE FRAMING. den v1 has ZERO mkInstanceRegistry
calls (control: 5 mkInstanceType hits, same instrument, same pin), and all ref
machinery lives in mkInstanceRegistry. So v1 ACCEPTS a ref type and does NOTHING
with it, while DEN-HOAG ABORTS. The two engines would silently disagree about
what the declaration MEANS. Corpus gen-schema pin 103ea88 already ships
ref/setOf with the IDENTICAL flat walker -- no bump helps.

EXACTLY ONE EMBEDDING in the corpus: hosts/cortex.nix:14, sole authoring site.
Zero-ref-usage confirmed with a control (0 ref hits vs 11 schemaLib. hits).

★★★ BETTER CANDIDATE, ALREADY IN THE TREE, NOT YET EVALUATED:
den-hoag ALREADY declares `den.<kind>.<name>.edges.<rel>` on EVERY kind --
lib/entity.nix:145-151, `schema.mkOption { type = schema.types.raw; default = {}; }`,
description: "Relation edges: `<rel> = <targets>` (§5); each `<rel>` must name a
declared den.relations relation."

That is INSTANCE-level (which B4 says is what .30 needs), den-hoag-OWNED (no
gen-schema change, so B1/B2/B4 do not apply), and `types.raw` (so B3's
safe-stamp hazard does not apply either). It is v1-invisible.

This bead previously recorded ZERO den.relations/den.edges usage in the corpus.
AN ABSENCE IS NOT A LAW -- zero usage is not evidence the surface is inert.
UNVERIFIED: whether edgesFieldModules reaches a consumer, or is inert like
den.schema.<kind>.excludes (den-hoag-9xo.28).
SETTLES IT: trace edgesFieldModules to a consumer, and check whether the
den.relations guard named in the description actually fires.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★ THE FORK IS SETTLED AND THE FRAMING UNDER IT WAS WRONG. Two updates.

1. THE v1 FORK COLLAPSED TO (c). Measured (papers 6cfe558):
   den.relations ABORTS under v1 ("The option `den.relations' does not exist"),
   with a control aborting identically at the same forcing depth. So option (a)
   -- corpus declares both -- is DEAD; the corpus is shared source that must
   evaluate under v1 in production.
   Entity-side .edges DOES ride v1's freeform with a BYTE-IDENTICAL id_hash, for
   a structural reason: v1 hostType is strict = false so the freeform absorbs
   the key, and gen-schema identity reflection covers PRIMITIVE fields only, so
   a list-of-attrsets value is outside the reflected set.
   ⇒ (c): corpus declares only <host>.edges.<rel>; den-hoag owns the relation
   vocabulary. Residual cost: relation names are shim-owned, so a den-hoag-only
   name appears in corpus source and means nothing under v1 (documentation
   hazard, not runtime).

2. ★ THE A15 QUESTION DISSOLVED, and my "two edge pools" framing was WRONG.
   The topology map (papers 9eb5439) measured den's own graph across 12 configs:
   THE LABELLED/UNLABELLED EDGE SPLIT IS A RENDERING ARTIFACT. The 700
   unlabelled edges are 664 aspect-tree + 28 scope-containment + 8 scope->
   host-root -- three semantically distinct relations sharing a style because
   `normal` is the FALLBACK branch of edgeStyle (graph.nix:362-369). The 541
   "provides" labels are a hardcoded literal (graph.nix:501) carrying zero
   information. FIVE OF TWELVE CONFIGS HAVE ZERO LABELLED EDGES AT ALL.
   ⇒ "A design that keys off labelled-vs-unlabelled is keying off den-diagram's
   stylesheet." There are not two populations; there is ONE REPRESENTATION OF
   FIVE RELATIONS.

   Separately, the pool-collapse spike (papers 0073aa4) established the two
   den-hoag edge RECORD TYPES are genuinely different types sharing one field --
   trace records carry content-movement semantics (mode/path/adapt), relation
   edges carry from/to and move no content. Collapsing them would ADD machinery.
   DO NOT COLLAPSE. The available simplification is a DELETION: the projection
   tag (to in {query,materialize,both}) and materializeFilter have NO LIVE
   PRODUCER -- 1587 edges across 47 roots, every one unlabeled, all 9 kinds
   materialize, filter makes zero decisions. Deleting is byte-identical
   including outputFor "host:cortex-cuda", removes 21 lines and one concept, and
   DISSOLVES D1 AND D2 outright.
   ⚠ BUT that "no live producer" was measured on nix-config ONLY. Per
   den-hoag-9xo.33, the templates are the usable witness set and were NOT
   checked for a producer. RE-MEASURE BEFORE DELETING.

STILL OPEN, and it is an INTENT question no measurement can settle: whether a
future user-registered den.edges kind should produce records that stay off the
trace. If yes the tag stays and must be REPAIRED (D1+D2); if no it is deleted.

title: den.schema.<kind>.excludes is INERT — the corpus declares exclusions nothing consumes
description:
den.schema.<kind>.excludes is INERT in den-hoag. The corpus writes it; nothing
consumes it. A consumer's exclusion of a policy therefore does nothing at all,
silently.

MEASURED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY (2026-07-27) -- design-reviewer first, then
reproduced by denhoag-writer with the same four-arm eval at ab1112a rather than
taken on report:

  a_noSchema     ["marker"]
  b_includeOnly  ["__kindInclude__host__policy__0"]   instrument responds
  c_includeExcl  ["__kindInclude__host__policy__0"]   BYTE-IDENTICAL to b
  d_exclOnly     ["marker"]                            no-op

Arm b is the positive control: the instrument does respond to the kind-schema
surface, so c's identity to b is a real negative, not a dead probe.

WHY IT WAS MISSED, and it is instructive: the design cited
lib/compat/compile.nix:714-723 as the displacement consumer. That is
translateAspect reading ASPECT-level aspect.excludes. The corpus writes
KIND-level den.schema.<kind>.excludes -- a different surface. The cited
comment's own next clause says "corpus excludes are policy excludes on kinds",
and the quotation stopped one clause short of the sentence that said so.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this is P1 not a note: any design that relies on a
consumer displacing a den-hoag-provisioned default is unimplementable today.
That is what killed route 1 / A-prime in the .13 default-attachment design
(papers plans/2026-07-27-default-attachment-design.md rev 3, review rev 2 at
papers 64aaed1). Route 1 would have DOUBLE-ATTACHED every corpus host.

NOT SCHEDULED. The decision this bead needs: should kind-level excludes be
implemented (v1 parity -- the corpus already writes it and expects it to work),
or should the corpus's usage be recognised as unsupported and the surface
rejected LOUDLY rather than ignored silently? Silently ignoring a declared
exclusion is the arc's recurring shape: a declared fact the framework does not
read.

title: den-hoag's gates cannot fail on a corpus-breaking change; the .23 blind spot moved up a level
description:
STRUCTURAL: den-hoag's three gates cannot fail on a corpus-breaking change.
A commit can be ci 0 / parity 0 / ship-gate 0-true and leave the corpus
completely unevaluable.

DEMONSTRATED, not theorised (2026-07-27). registryKindOf routing through
identityHashForKind (4986982) dropped a totality the old code had by
construction (first.${n} or null). The marker probes each CANDIDATE kind
against an instance that mostly belongs to another, so the reflection routinely
reads fields the instance lacks -- and A MISSING ATTRIBUTE IS NOT A THROW, so
tryEval does not catch it.

Bisected on the corpus, one process per commit, classified by which error:

  34601cf   8 hosts, green
  4986982   error: attribute 'id' missing        <- abort ENTERS here
  b2e5373   error: attribute 'domain' missing    <- same mechanism, different
                                                    first-missing field (the
                                                    bump widened which options
                                                    count as identity keys)
  51fd4e7   error: attribute 'domain' missing
  3b596d9   7 hosts, green                       <- fixed

ALL THREE GATES WERE GREEN AT EVERY ONE OF THOSE COMMITS. The orchestrator
reviewed and pushed 4986982, then pushed two more commits on top of it. Main
carried a totally-broken corpus across four commits and nothing in the repo
could say so.

WHY THE GATES CANNOT: the corpus arm is dev-time only and unreachable from any
gated path (lib/compat/parity/oracle.nix:527-529, "the one arm that cannot run
purely in den-hoag's own CI"). There is no in-repo driver and no runbook --
this is the same missing harness that makes den-hoag-9xo.20's T1.2 partial. The
prerequisite is now demonstrably not just T1.2's problem.

SECOND-ORDER, AND THE REAL POINT: den-hoag-9xo.23 closed the blind spot where
no fixture built a registry through gen-merge types. THE BLIND SPOT MOVED UP A
LEVEL RATHER THAN CLOSING -- no fixture probes a candidate kind that DECLARES A
FIELD THE INSTANCE LACKS, which is the shape the cross-kind marker probe hits
on every real multi-kind corpus. The narrow case is now pinned in
compat-registry-engine.nix (and without the widening that test does not fail,
it ABORTS the evaluation). The general question is unanswered: what OTHER
corpus-shaped inputs does the suite never construct?

TWO CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, neither scoped:
  1. a gated corpus smoke arm -- even one host's toplevel, even eval-only --
     so a corpus-breaking change cannot be green. Blocked on the same driver
     T1.2 needs.
  2. a shape census: enumerate the input shapes the corpus exhibits (multi-kind
     registries with disjoint option sets; kinds with internal primitives;
     hosts with intoAttr opt-outs) and check which the suite constructs at all.
     Cheaper, and it is the .23 method applied to VALUES rather than to types.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so the next corpus-breaking green does not get discovered
by accident a second time.

title: [gen-schema] identityHashForKind and mkIdentityModule carry SEPARATE primitive lists and have drifted (str)
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-schema. Work in ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen-schema.

identityHashForKind documents itself as the OPTION-LEVEL EXACT TWIN of the
reflection mkIdentityModule performs (lib/identity.nix:50-56, verbatim: "the
SAME reflection mkIdentityModule performs ... Routes through the SAME
hashIdentity, so it can drift from neither").

IT DRIFTS. The two carry SEPARATE hardcoded primitiveTypeNames lists and they
are not equal at gen-schema main.

MEASURED (orchestrator, 2026-07-27):

  gen-schema 103ea88 (main; nix-config pins this)
    lib/identity.nix:60   identityHashForKind   ["string","int","bool"]
    lib/identity.nix:116  mkIdentityModule      ["string","str","int","bool"]
                                                          ^^^^^ only here

  gen-schema 017062cd (den-hoag pins this; ancestor of 103ea88)
    lib/identity.nix:60   ["string","int","bool"]
    lib/identity.nix:112  ["string","int","bool"]     <- AGREE

So "str" was added to the stamper's list without being added to the twin's.
mkIdentityModule's list carries an explicit comment explaining WHY str must be
accepted -- den declares every entity option with nixpkgs lib.types, so a
nixpkgs-str field must reflect or same-named instances collapse to one
id_hash. That reasoning applies verbatim to identityHashForKind and was not
applied to it.

CONSEQUENCE: at gen-schema main, a kind option authored lib.types.str is
counted by the stamper (it IS in the carried id_hash) and NOT counted by
identityHashForKind. Any consumer using the twin to reproduce the hash misses.
Latent today only because nothing on the corpus path calls identityHashForKind
yet -- den-hoag-9xo.23 option 3 is about to put it on that path.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM THE RECENT LOCK BUMP: nix-config c6331f3 -> 103ea88 is an
EMPTY diff for lib/identity.nix. Verified. The bump did not change identity
reflection for the corpus.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): the two lists should not be two lists. One
shared source, or the twin derives from the stamper. A comment asserting two
things cannot drift, beside two independent literals, is the same defect class
as an invariant documented but unenforced (DL-HS-70).

GUARD REGARDLESS: a test that fails when the two lists disagree. That is what
would have caught this, and it is cheap.
close_reason:
ALREADY SHIPPED — closed on evidence, not on work done here. Found by the den-hoag-4kh.5 validation audit (contradiction C1) and independently re-verified twice.

The defect was two drifted primitiveTypeNames lists between identityHashForKind and mkIdentityModule. Both halves are fixed in tree at gen-schema:
  1. ONE hoisted list — gen-schema/lib/identity.nix:33, consumed at :43 and :139; grep -c 'primitiveTypeNames = [' returns 1, both local copies gone. Landed in gen-schema af3dbe9 'fix(identity): one primitive-type list, so the two reflections cannot drift'.
  2. THE EXACT GUARD THIS BEAD ASKS FOR exists — gen-schema/ci/tests/identity-hash-for.nix:88 test-forKind-matches-module-nixpkgs-str, plus den-hoag ci compat-registry-engine::test-identity-reflection-agrees-with-the-stamp.

The fix is credited in den-hoag-lcz's close reason. The work landed under a bead about a DIFFERENT defect while the bead describing it stayed open at P1 — a dedup gap, same class as den-hoag-xf9 (closed as 'Duplicate ... filed by the orchestrator without checking for an existing bead').

title: [gen-merge] protocol divergences: typeMerge unsound, emptyValue 3/3, deferredModule.check silent, getSubOptions stubs remain
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-merge. Work happens in ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen-merge, NOT in
den-hoag. Tracked here because this is where we dispatch from; gen-merge has no
beads workspace.

DO NOT fix any of these in den-hoag compat. den-hoag can WITNESS them; the fix
is upstream. gen-merge already owns the suite for this:
ci/tests/nixpkgs-protocol.nix and ci/tests/compat-nixpkgs-types.nix.

Catalogue found while scoping den-hoag test coverage. Full detail with file:line
and measurements: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-27-suite-type-coverage-scoping.md
section 1 (papers 7029e12).

  section 1.4  typeMerge -- UNSOUND. Highest severity in the set.
  section 1.3  emptyValue -- 3/3 divergent from nixpkgs.
  section 1.2  deferredModule.check -- silent acceptance (accepts what it
               should reject; a check that cannot fail).
  section 1.1  getSubOptions still STUBBED on nullOr and deferredModule.
               8daa25d implemented submodule/attrsOf/listOf only.

NOT IN SCOPE, and explicitly NOT a defect (owner ruling 2026-07-27): the
constructors gen-merge does not ship -- submoduleWith, functionTo, unspecified,
uniq. gen-schema takes a CALLER-SUPPLIED type (schemaFn = description: type: fn,
gen-schema/lib/methods.nix:3) and never constructs them. The corpus passes
NIXPKGS types in (nix-config modules/den/schema/environment.nix:150 uses
lib.types.functionTo where lib is the nixpkgs module arg). So declarative
methods in gen-schema are fully supported without them. Section 1.5 lists them
as a FIXTURE-TRANSLATION fact only -- you cannot mechanically convert a
nixpkgs-authored fixture that spells functionTo. It is NOT an expressiveness
gap and must not be read as one.

DESIGN INTENT (owner, 2026-07-27) that bounds this bead: gen-schema is meant to
work WITH nixpkgs evalModules. "Compat" means opting OUT of / excluding
gen-types entirely -- NOT a bidirectional dual engine. So one-way interop (gen
types mounting inside nixpkgs evalModules) is the DESIGN, not a limitation, and
gen-merge is under no obligation to become a drop-in lib.types replacement.

UNVERIFIED, named with settlement paths in section 1.6 -- do NOT treat as
findings until measured:
  - submodule specialArgs propagation (settle by two-process comparison)
  - nestedTypes deprecation-walk parity (settle by giving a nested type a
    deprecationMessage and checking the walk fires)
close_reason:
All four audited protocol divergences fixed, plus two follow-ups and an oracle extension. gen-merge 8daa25d..f17f2f2, seven commits, all on origin.

  18b05f6  typeMerge was UNSOUND -- pureDefaultFunctor set payload=null on every type, so any same-named partner merged WITHOUT comparing element types. Reachability caveat recorded: mkInstanceRegistry sets description/default/apply and nixpkgs throws on that before the type arm, so the fix is correct and reaches real gen-schema types but the nixpkgs path is pre-empted for the registry shape it matters most for.
  23b4b7c  deferredModule.check silently accepted what its merge could not consume. Four sibling probes were NOT defects (they abort inside merge before check is consulted) -- recorded so they are not re-litigated.
  2a33f81  emptyValue was a field nothing read. Touches the ENGINE, not just the type records.
  548425f  getSubOptions on nullOr. deferredModule's empty answer is CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION (its nixpkgs sub-options are staticModules; gen-merge ships no deferredModuleWith) -- pinned with the reason.
  ebc2a10  cross-pin that check and getSubOptions agree by answering DIFFERENT questions. An agreement pin has no defect to red-line against, so it is armed against three wrong implementations instead.
  e3ac5e5  parametric leaves protocol-completed. A completed leaf REFUSES typeMerge: its parameters live behind closures (__id is name-only -- the A1 intensional ceiling; closure equality is pointer-based). Left nullary it would have REINTRODUCED 18b05f6's unsoundness through the leaves.
  f17f2f2  oracle extended to the empty-definition class. Blindness was INCIDENTAL not structural, measured.

TWO DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES FROM NIXPKGS, both documented rather than left to be found as bugs: deferredModule rejects absolutePathString (admitting it would carry a string through as a module VALUE); enum declarations refuse to merge where nixpkgs unions their value sets (gen-merge cannot read parameters it cannot see).

Every blast radius measured. Every test armed against WRONG IMPLEMENTATIONS, not merely against the unfixed state -- including a break that reddens seven unrelated pre-existing fixtures, which is what shows a break is real rather than test-local.

CARRIED FORWARD to den-hoag-1n3, not actioned: deprecationMessage stored but never read; getSubModules/substSubModules divergent on 4 of 5 containers.

Three of the arc's standing rules came from this work: two guarded paths need two probes and the probe must land on a type with nothing else protecting it; verify a baseline is what it claims to be, by feature presence not by name; a true statement can hide the defect.

title: PREREQ: den-hoag's own gen-merge input is the stubbed rev; align before converting fixtures
description:
den-hoag's OWN lib is still built on the STUBBED gen-merge.

MEASURED (coverage-spec, section 0.2). ci/flake.lock carries FOUR distinct
gen-merge revs live in ONE evaluation, and the two a fixture can reach are
DIFFERENT revs:

  den-hoag -> gen-merge                 gen-merge_4  2701d8bb  getSubOptions STUB
  den-hoag -> gen-schema -> gen-merge   gen-merge_5  8daa25d   implemented
  den-hoag -> gen-aspects -> gen-merge  gen-merge    2701d8bb  stub
  gen -> gen-merge                      gen-merge_9  2701d8bb  stub

2701d8bb is 6 commits behind 8daa25d (git rev-list --count). The bump at
edd4f97 moved gen-merge_5 ONLY -- correct for R2.1's witness, and I explicitly
instructed that the other nodes not move. The consequence was not recorded:
flake.nix:39 (merge = inputs.gen-merge.lib) -> lib/default.nix ->
internal.merge (lib/default.nix:2809-2828) means den-hoag's own lib runs the
stub.

Direct probe, den-hoag's pinned gen-merge vs local 8daa25d:
                        submodule.getSubOptions []   attrsOf(submodule)
  2701d8bb (internal)   []                           []
  8daa25d               ["y"]                        ["y"]
  nixpkgs               ["_module","y"]              ["_module","y"]
Positive control same instrument: getSubModules_isNull == false and
substSubModules_isNull == false on the 2701d8bb submodule, so the probe found a
real gen-merge submodule and read non-default values off it. The [] is a real
negative, not a dead probe.

WHY THIS GATES .23: a fixture written today as
denHoag.internal.merge.types.attrsOf (...) constructs a STUBBED type and can go
green against the very defect class the conversion exists to catch. Converting
fixtures before aligning this input reproduces the exact failure being removed.

SECOND DECISION IN SCOPE: two gen-merge type systems are simultaneously
reachable from a fixture (denHoag.internal.merge vs denHoag.schema.types) at
different revs. The suite should reach gen-merge through ONE name. Honest
default per the spec: denHoag.schema for anything registry-shaped, since that
is the path the consumer's mkInstanceRegistry actually resolves through.

METHOD: per the checkpoint's lock lesson -- bump the chain the consumer
resolves through, then VERIFY the node you named is the node whose rev moved.
Never a bare nix flake update.
close_reason:
CLOSED. den-hoag's own gen-merge input aligned to 8daa25de; ship-gate armed.

FIX: commit 4f3be40 (pushed). Five targeted --update-input calls across three
locks, each verified node-named == node-moved, zero collateral:
  flake.lock         gen-merge_4 (gen-merge)                 2701d8bb -> 8daa25de
  flake.lock         gen-merge_5 (gen-schema/gen-merge)      fa5d5cc2 -> 8daa25de
  ci/flake.lock      gen-merge_4 (den-hoag/gen-merge)        2701d8bb -> 8daa25de
  parity/flake.lock  gen-merge_4 (den-v2/gen-merge)          2701d8bb -> 8daa25de
  parity/flake.lock  gen-merge_5 (den-v2/gen-schema/...)     fa5d5cc2 -> 8daa25de

SCOPE BEYOND THE ORIGINAL BRIEF, and it was necessary:
  - parity's den-v2 is path:.., so parity's gate runs den-hoag's own lib.
    Leaving it stubbed = the parity gate certifies a DIFFERENT den-hoag build
    than ci tests.
  - parity/ship-gate.nix:15 reads builtins.getFlake (builtins.dirOf flakePath)
    = the ROOT flake. The root lock is on the ship-gate's own eval path, not
    merely downstream consumer resolution.

NOT MOVED (other libs' pins of their own dep; their owners' call):
gen-aspects/*, gen-flake/*, and the ci+parity gen-hub nodes.

EVIDENCE 1 -- the bump is real and the probe discriminates on the lock:
              submodule.getSubOptions []   attrsOf(submodule)
  2701d8bb    []                           []
  8daa25de    ["y"]                        ["y"]
  nixpkgs     ["_module","y"]              ["_module","y"]
Positive control same instrument: getSubModules non-null, substSubModules
non-null, _type == "option-type" on the 2701d8bb submodule => real negative,
not a dead probe. Discrimination control: revert ci/flake.lock and ci's
den-hoag reports [] while parity's (not reverted) still reports ["y"].

EVIDENCE 2 -- SHIP-GATE ARMED, all three conjuncts independently.
allEqual is a CONJUNCTION, so one dead conjunct hides inside a true. Each was
perturbed separately (one extra nixos setting delivered on one arm, via a
SCRATCH copy of ship-gate.nix; the repo file was never modified):

  arm                      allEqual  equal  emitting  silent
  A unperturbed            true      true   true      true
  B perturb main shim      FALSE     FALSE  true      true
  C perturb channel igloo  FALSE     true   FALSE     true
  D restore                true      true   true      true
  E perturb channel bare   FALSE     true   true      FALSE

Each flips ONLY its own => none is a constant and they are not one shared value
read three times. `silent` (the emission-free host) stayed true in every other
arm and needed its own perturbation to prove it can fail at all.

Real parity/ship-gate.nix, unmodified, after all of it: true, exit 0.

WEIGHING THE GATES (recorded because it is the argument for .23): ci-green is
WEAK evidence here. The ci check drv is `echo "N tests passed"; touch $out`
with inputDrvs 0, so all asserts are eval-time and the drv encodes only the
count. Per the suite-wide blind spot the suite was structurally incapable of
witnessing gen-merge type behaviour, so green was consistent with the bump
being INVISIBLE, not with it being safe. ship-gate is the non-vacuous check --
3 distinct real drvPaths, all equal, rendered NixOS toplevel unchanged.

TOOLING TRAPS found while arming (for the checkpoint notes):
  - a perturbation added as a SEPARATE module aborts `gen-merge: the option
    'den.aspects' has conflicting definitions` -- the mkDenWith path is
    single-def raw, no v1DeepMerge. Merge into the fixture via
    nlib.recursiveUpdate instead.
  - wrapping channelFixture as a bare `args: ...` lambda ERRORS: mkDenWith
    reads the function's DECLARED FORMALS, so a wrapper must re-declare them
    (`{ den, ... }@args:`). Same formals-matter class as the arm-loss work.
  - builtins.getFlake (toString ./ci) fails `error: 'flake.nix' is too short to
    be a valid store path` (the path:.. trap). Working form:
    builtins.getFlake "git+file:///<abs>/den-hoag?dir=ci" -- reads the dirty
    working tree, confirmed by the revert control.

title: Fixtures must build registries through gen-schema's mkInstanceRegistry, not a nixpkgs look-alike
description:
RESCOPED 2026-07-27 (owner ruling). Was: "convert the suite to gen-merge types."
That was the wrong line. den-hoag's share is ONE thing.

★ THE LINE
  gen-merge   owns protocol conformance. Every divergence in the scoping spec
              section 1. Tracked as den-hoag-wj0, label upstream-gen-merge,
              worked in the gen-merge repo. NOT den-hoag's to fix or to test.
  gen-schema  owns that mkInstanceRegistry produces types that mount in nixpkgs
              evalModules. That is its contract with the consumer.
  den-hoag    owns THIS bead, and only this: its fixtures must construct
              registries THE WAY THE CONSUMER DOES, so the bridge is exercised
              against a real gen-schema registry instead of a nixpkgs
              look-alike.

Rationale: den-hoag was .8's VICTIM, not its owner. A den-hoag suite that
tests gen-merge's protocol is the "route through gen-native, do not
re-implement in compat" principle inverted into testing. Reject that.

★ DESIGN INTENT that bounds the whole bead (owner, 2026-07-27)
gen-schema is meant to work WITH nixpkgs evalModules. "Compat" = opting OUT of
/ excluding gen-types entirely. NOT a bidirectional dual engine. Consequences:
  - one-way interop (gen types mounting inside nixpkgs evalModules) is the
    DESIGN, not a limitation
  - gen-merge is under NO obligation to become a drop-in lib.types replacement;
    its missing constructors are not a gap
  - "correct engine" for a fixture therefore means: gen-schema where gen-schema
    is the authority (registry construction), nixpkgs where the consumer's own
    types are authoritative
  - my earlier overcommit worry (that we might owe a user-selectable dual
    engine, needing nixpkgs types inside gen's evalModuleTree) is WITHDRAWN. We
    do not owe that. Do not scope for it.

★ SCOPE -- approach D from the spec, section 3.2, narrowed
Prerequisite: den-hoag-9xo.24 (den-hoag's own gen-merge input is the stubbed
rev). This bead is BLOCKED on it -- a fixture converted first would construct a
stubbed type and could go green against the defect class it targets.

  1. A shared constructor in ci/tests/_lib/ that CALLS gen-schema's real
     mkInstanceRegistry. Must call it, never imitate it -- a helper that
     re-implements the shape reintroduces exactly the class of lie being
     removed (three of the four wrong-engine fixtures already carry a comment
     ASSERTING their nixpkgs construction is equivalent).
  2. Convert the six exposed files onto it:
       typeless registry: compat-custom-kind, compat-fleet-context
       wrong-engine:      compat-registry-kind-marker (= R2.1),
                          compat-cluster-entity, compat-schema-processing,
                          _lib/den-compat-test  <- one line, 57-fixture blast
                          radius; churn expected and ACCEPTABLE per the
                          standing framing
  3. Leave bucket (iii) ALONE -- 30 of 36 type-constructing fixtures already
     use the right engine. Third-party mocks, flake-parts scaffold,
     consumer-authored kind options, the host path. Converting them would make
     the suite a WORSE model of the consumer.

★ EXPLICITLY NOT IN SCOPE
  - a rule that all den-hoag fixtures use gen-merge types (wrong, breaks 30
    correct fixtures)
  - gen-merge-typed twins for bucket (iii) (that is gen-merge's suite's job)
  - any gen-merge protocol fix (wj0)
  - R2.1 is a DEPENDENCY, not absorbed -- see spec section 5

★ FALSIFIER (spec section 4). Do not grep for the spelling: the original
premise-check missed ci/tests/f1-inputs-self-nodes.nix:34 because
denHoag.schema.types is gen-merge via re-export and "merge.types" cannot see
it. Walk every option type a fixture constructs and read the RESOLVED value
(t._type / t.name). A predicate over a namespace spelling cannot establish an
absence.
close_reason:
CLOSED. Commits 19ffe2e, 34601cf, 4986982 (all pushed).

Six of six exposed fixtures now build registries through gen-schema's real
mkInstanceRegistry via a shared ci/tests/_lib constructor that CALLS it rather
than imitating its shape. Bucket (iii)'s 30 fixtures untouched -- nixpkgs is
the correct engine where the consumer's own types are authoritative.

ARMING FALSIFIER -- proven both directions, pre-conversion control run in a
detached worktree, not reasoned about:

  tree              gen-merge         ci gate
  pre-conversion    2701d8bb stubbed  exit 0  GREEN
  pre-conversion    8daa25de          exit 0
  converted         8daa25de          exit 0
  converted         2701d8bb stubbed  exit 1  RED

The suite COULD NOT witness the stub before and DOES now. Reds are each for
their OWN reason, not one shared abort -- compat-registry-engine's engine pin
still PASSES while its surface pin fails (the type is still gen-merge's, only
getSubOptions is stubbed); compat-custom-kind's discovery still passes while
its surface pin fails; compat-cluster-entity aborts on the empty stamp tree.

HABIT FALSIFIER = 0. No options.den.<key> registry declaration remains outside
the helper.

R2.1 (compat-registry-kind-marker) converted. STOP did not trigger:
  8daa25de   5/5 PASS
  2701d8bb   only test-registry-reaches-fleet-with-marker FAILS
  fa5d5cc2   ABORTS "attribute 'deprecationMessage' missing"

The fa5d5cc2 abort is the exact error the fixture's own header names -- the
gen-merge option crossing into nixpkgs evalModules. A nixpkgs look-alike cannot
produce it. And at 2701d8bb only the end-to-end STAMP arm fails while the
marker assertions pass, which the writer PREDICTED BEFORE the option-3 ruling:
routing through the kind value makes the marker stub-insensitive and the
red-pre-bump property rides stampTreeOf. Prediction stated in advance, then
measured.

SCOPE EXPANSION (authorized): registryKindOf now routes through gen-schema's
own identityHashForKind. identityKeysOf is DELETED, not taught a third
spelling, and its export is gone. That dissolves a compat re-implementation of
a gen capability -- the duplicate had drifted, which is den-hoag-9xo.26.

CONDITION 1 WAIVED ON ITS MERITS. I required the lib change to be its own
commit before the fixture conversions. It cannot be: both orderings were
measured and each produces a red intermediate. lib-first leaves the fixture
calling the old signature with no kind value to supply (supplying one IS the
conversion); fixture-first returns null under the old signature. The reason is
the defect in miniature -- THE FIXTURE'S HAND-STAMPED id_hash AND THE LIB'S
OVER-INCLUSIVE REFLECTION AGREED WITH EACH OTHER, so the fixture was green only
while both were wrong. Two wrong halves that validate each other cannot be
fixed one at a time.

Conditions 2/3/4 met: dependency sweep reported before touching registryKindOf
(only consumer was registryKindOf itself; corpus has zero hits; the one
apparent dependant asserted its own premise); wrong-kind control landed as a
TEST with three arms; arm A stays lib.types.str and HITS.

den-hoag-lcz drift guard shipped as an assertion in compat-registry-engine:
identityHashForKind kv inst == inst.id_hash PLUS the stamp's contents, so a
drift trips two pins. Writing it caught the writer's own wrong expectation --
it had assumed the corpus pin's behaviour, not den-hoag's.

TESTS 1889 -> 1895. Gates ci 0 / parity 0 / ship-gate 0 true.

comments.text:
SCOPING SPEC LINKED: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-27-suite-type-coverage-scoping.md
(papers 7029e12, md5 0e530452fb5fdf196285a04e6ff4cd66, 518 lines)

PREMISE VERIFIED AND CORRECTED. Zero gen-merge STRUCTURAL constructions in

title: slab's nixOnDroidConfiguration is built from environment:dev's droid subtree, not slab's own content
description:
REVEALED by the spawn-placement coherence check (den-hoag 3bd1d4f), NOT fixed by it. A check that makes a
defect loud is not a fix for it.

MEASURED: the only producer of nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab is a parked spawn at node environment:dev:
    node=environment:dev  class=droid  into=nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab  nModules=0
It slices classSubtreeAt at environment:dev -- the ATTACHING node -- so it gathers the ENVIRONMENT's droid
subtree, which is empty. slab's own droid content is not in it.

WHY NOBODY NOTICED. The droid family has no receiver row, so no class terminal contributes slab; there is
no competing producer to collide with and no duplicate to detect. And nix-on-droid's evaluator accepts
zero modules happily, so the configuration MATERIALISES with activationPackage/config/options/pkgs present
-- defaults, not slab's content. A wrong answer that looks like an answer.

Since 3bd1d4f the member aborts NAMED when demanded, instead of silently yielding defaults:
    den: incoherent spawn placement — the spec parked at 'environment:dev' slices that node's own 'droid'
    content but places it at 'nixOnDroidConfigurations.slab', which names a different entity than 'dev'.
Enumeration is unaffected (all five families and every member still enumerate); only forcing that member
fails.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: slab needs a producer that slices at slab. That is a distinct root cause from
den-hoag-ljr's -- ljr was one v1 declaration consumed twice, where the class terminal already produced a
complete artifact and the spawn's empty one displaced it. Here there is NO terminal contribution at all,
so removing the spawn would leave slab with no producer. The question is which mechanism should own a
droid host's configuration: a receiver row for the droid family (making the class terminal produce it, as
it does for nixos and darwin), or a spawn parked at the host itself (the shape colmena.nix:96 already uses
successfully -- host:<h> -> colmenaModules.<h>).

Same shape applies to patch/darwin ONLY in so far as it was ALSO emitted incoherently from
environment:dev; but darwinConfigurations.patch additionally HAS a class-terminal contribution, so it is
covered by ljr's de-duplication and is not part of this bead.

title: id_hash missing in the homeManagerModules channel: A12 producer tie-break unreachable until user cells delivered
description:
FIFTH INSTANCE of pre-existing-code-newly-reachable. CONFIRMED by discriminator, not argued.

DISCRIMINATOR ASKED: does the home-manager path have an id_hash consumer that could not run while
home-manager.users was empty? ANSWER: YES, and it is exact.

THE CONSUMER: lib/attributes/collections.nix:205
    identity = a.content.id_hash;   # aspect identity (id_hash) — the A12 producer key (§A12)
`identity` is forced ONLY by scope-adapter.nix `producerLt` (rank, then identity, then emissionIndex),
which is reached ONLY through `sortByProducer` = map … (prelude.sort producerLt recs).

WHY IT COULD NOT RUN: a sort comparator is never invoked on fewer than two elements. Verified rather
than assumed, with a throwing sentinel:
    builtins.sort cmp [ bomb ]  -> 1   (comparator never called; the throw never forced)
    builtins.sort cmp [ ]       -> 0
So with 0 or 1 producer on a channel, `identity` -- and therefore the id_hash read -- is NEVER forced.

WHY IT RUNS NOW: `homeManagerModules` is a den channel (declared by corpus aspects such as
aspects/apps/*/*.nix, consumed at aspects/core/users/home-manager/home-manager.nix:67). Ledger u16/#53c
records home-manager.users was EMPTY on the host -- the cell-fired user forward never reached it. With
den-hoag-9xo.8 fixed, hosts acquire environment parents, the class terminal's complete configuration wins
the member slot (nHostModules 60 -> 136), and user-cell content now reaches the host. The channel gains
COMPETING producers, sort finally calls the comparator, and the id_hash read executes for the first time.

Trace confirming the path:
  system.build.toplevel -> assertions -> core.impermanence.nixos -> home-manager.users
    -> module argument `homeManagerModules` -> attribute 'id_hash' missing

SO IT IS NOT DAMAGE FROM den-hoag-ljr's FIX. Independent evidence: the family fold is complete and
correct after that fix (all 13 unowned contributions survive, every family materialises, slab kept,
patch resolving, no duplicate-member abort). Nothing was deleted; this defect sits downstream of the fold.

NOT CHASED, per instruction -- filing and stopping. The open question for whoever takes it: WHICH
contribution's `content` lacks id_hash. `a.content` is the aspect record, so a producer whose content is
not an id_hash-bearing aspect (a raw/derived contribution reaching the channel) would explain it. Start
at collections.nix:187-205 where the contribution records are built, and enumerate the homeManagerModules
producers at a host that now has user cells.
