title: ancNodeId silently picks the alphabetically-first coord on a multi-coord slice
description: See notes.
notes:
LATENT SILENT-WRONG-ANSWER DEFECT, independent of the D4 ruling. Found during the D4 stress-test.

`ancNodeId` renders a containment source slice to a parent node id. Definition (now sole-owner at lib/staged-resolution.nix:72 after T1.5; formerly lib/attributes/resolved-settings.nix:115-120):

    ancNodeId = slice: let k = builtins.head (builtins.attrNames slice); in "${k}:${slice.${k}.name}"

It takes `builtins.head (builtins.attrNames slice)` — on a MULTI-COORD slice that is the ALPHABETICALLY-FIRST coordinate, chosen silently.

REACHABLE: `containmentOf` (staged-resolution.nix:190-204) computes `sourceSlice = builtins.removeAttrs a.coords [ containTo ]` — whatever the policy authored, minus the target coord. Nothing constrains the remainder to a single coordinate. A policy emitting `coords = { rack = r1; zone = z1; blade = b1; }` with `containTo = "rack"` yields slice `{ zone; blade }` and renders parent `"blade:b1"` — silently preferring blade over zone on alphabetical order alone.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: pre-rung this fed only the settings ancestor chain. Post-T1.6 the same renderer decides SCOPE PARENTAGE, so a wrong pick becomes the inheritance chain for the node and every cell beneath it.

RELATED, same site: the fixture's claim that cross-kind containment sources are "topology-unreachable" (ci/tests/staged-resolution.nix:198-201) is FALSE — nothing validates that a source's kind is parent(targetKind). The tree's own weaker wording at :220-224 says "By convention", which is the honest one. So both defects share a root: the source slice is taken verbatim and never validated.

FIX SHAPE (deferred until the D4 ruling lands, since they touch the same site): a named abort when a source slice does not render to exactly one coordinate of the target's declared parent kind — i.e. validate the slice instead of trusting `head (attrNames …)`. This is the same validation gap errors.multipleContainmentParents guards from the other direction (too many parents vs an unvalidated single one).

NOT A REGRESSION: present before this arc. Surfaced because T1.6 promotes the renderer from settings-only to parentage.
close_reason: RESOLVED by T4.1 (84fc117), the slice-trichotomy validator. The silent alphabetically-first pick is now structurally impossible: a multi-coord slice aborts at errors.containmentSliceAmbiguous (staged-resolution.nix:230) BEFORE ancNodeId is reached — the validator's own comment names the old behaviour ('alphabetically-first, so it aborts instead'). ancNodeId still calls builtins.head, but only on a slice already proven single-coord (:224-234 sliceOk), and its empty arm aborts by name (containmentSliceEmpty, :82) rather than falling into head []'s bare out-of-bounds. Both halves of the .18 defect closed: the silent multi-coord pick, and the unnamed empty-slice throw. Filed as latent-but-load-bearing once T1.6 promoted the renderer from settings-only to parentage; that promotion happened and the guard preceded it.

title: Corpus microvm guest delivery dead: host.microvm.guests is listOf raw, excluded from the ctx stamp (#70/u19 frontier)
description: See notes.
notes:
LIVE CORPUS DEFECT, verified empirically by orchestrator. The corpus's microvm guest delivery does not work under den-hoag.

FACTS (all VERIFIED):
- nix-config modules/den/hosts/cortex.nix:14 declares `microvm.guests = [ den.hosts.x86_64-linux.cortex-cuda ];`
- cortex.nix:26-47 includes `virtualization.microvm-host` in den.aspects.cortex.includes — the aspect IS enabled.
- `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.cortex.config.microvm.vms --apply builtins.attrNames` => **[]**. The guest is NOT delivered.
- `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations --apply builtins.attrNames` => cortex-cuda IS present as a standalone output, despite hosts/cortex-cuda.nix:5 `intoAttr = [ ]` ("do not emit a standalone nixosConfiguration output").

=> NOT double-materialization. cortex-cuda materializes via exactly the WRONG path (standalone, which it opted out of) and is ABSENT from the right one (embedded into cortex). The embedded microvm never gets built into its host.

★ SEQUENCING CONSEQUENCE FOR 9xo.9: gating `intoAttr = [ ]` ALONE would make cortex-cuda vanish entirely, because the guest path is already broken. The guest delivery must work BEFORE the standalone output is gated. Do not ship the gate as an isolated fix.

THE DELIVERY SHAPE (verified, modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix): guest delivery is ASPECT-LEVEL, not scope-graph-level —
  :38-46 PRODUCE `den.aspects.virtualization.microvm-host.microvm-guests = { host, ... }: map (vm: { inherit (vm) name; osModules = den.lib.aspects.resolve vm.class (den.lib.resolveEntity "host" { host = vm; }); ... }) host.microvm.guests;`
  :62-76 CONSUME `den.aspects.virtualization.microvm-host.nixos = { microvm-guests, ... }: ... microvm.vms = listToAttrs (... guests ...)`
So the guest's modules are re-resolved INLINE from the entity record (den.lib.resolveEntity + den.lib.aspects.resolve) — it needs NO scope node for cortex-cuda. That is why the standalone node is not what feeds it.

HYPOTHESIS (UNVERIFIED — settle before fixing): the produce/consume chain is gated OFF. The consumer destructures `{ microvm-guests, ... }`, and den-hoag's dispatch gates a parametric arm on its destructured args being present in ctx (the resolveArgsSatisfied discipline). If the parametric PRODUCE arm never fires, or its result is never bound into ctx under that name, the `nixos` CONSUME arm is gated off and microvm.vms stays empty — matching the observation exactly.
SETTLING TEST: probe whether `microvm-guests` is bound in cortex's aspect ctx, and whether the parametric produce arm fires at the host node. If it fires but is unbound, the defect is in the produce->ctx binding; if it never fires, the defect is in parametric-aspect dispatch at host scope.

RELATION TO THE ARC: independent of the topology design (9xo.12) — this is aspect-plane, not scope-parentage. But it shares the family diagnosis: corpus-declared intent (guests, intoAttr) that den-hoag's materialization path never consults.
★ DIAGNOSED. My gating hypothesis is REFUTED IN MECHANISM. The consumer is NOT gated off — it fires, bound to an empty list. The defect is entirely PRODUCE-SIDE and narrows to one field: `host.microvm.guests` is `listOf raw`, and raw-typed entity fields are structurally excluded from the ctx-entity stamp.

METHOD CORRECTION (mine): `attrNames microvm.vms == []` structurally CANNOT distinguish "consumer gated off" from "consumer fired with an empty channel" — microvm.vms defaults to {}. Both read []. Same-aspect controls were needed and are what settled it.

WHY NO GATE-OFF IS POSSIBLE HERE: microvm-guests is a DECLARED quirk (nix-config modules/den/quirks/microvm-guests.nix:2), and den-hoag's channel-totality law binds every registered channel at every node — bindingsAt = `… // prelude.genAttrs channelNames (_: [ ]) // channelBindingsAt id // …` (lib/attributes/output-modules.nix:998-1013, law at :968-975). A registered channel is bound EMPTY, never absent.
AND THE PRODUCE GATE IS SATISFIED: isPipelineParametric (collections.nix:61) admits `{ host, ... }:`; wrapGatedFn fires iff every required formal is in ctx (:143-166) and the only formal is `host`. Proof host is in ctx with REAL authored fields — the facter arm (nix-config core/system/facter.nix:4-6, same `{ host, ... }` formals) fired and resolved host.facts to a real store path.
=> gate satisfied, arm fires, returns an EMPTY LIST. resolveParametric's list-SPLIT (collections.nix:170-176) makes one contribution PER ELEMENT, so an empty list yields ZERO contributions, silently. That is why this is empty rather than an error.

THE MECHANISM (orchestrator-VERIFIED at source):
- nix-config modules/den/aspects/virtualization/microvm.nix:40 — `type = lib.types.listOf lib.types.raw;` with `default = [ ]` (:41).
- lib/compat/registry.nix:292 — `stampTreeOf = mkStampTree (v: !excludedType (v.type or { }))`. Raw-class leaves are EXCLUDED from the ctx-entity stamp.
- ★ den-hoag's OWN COMMENT names this exact field as the frontier, registry.nix:294-300 verbatim: "The RAW-FIELD tree (#70, ledger u19's next-link): exactly the leaves `stampTreeOf` EXCLUDES. The exclusion's reason STANDS — raw/deferredModule/anything-class values must never enter deepSeq'd resolution state — but v1 binds the FULL merged host config as the ctx entity (pin 11866c16 assemble-pipes.nix:154), so corpus policy/channel bodies READ these fields (`host.microvm.guests`, microvm-guests.nix:38-59 — the u19 frontier …). They therefore ride a SEPARATE side channel (`_entityRawStamps`, bridge.nix …)".
- Side channel path: rawStampTreeOf (:304) -> _entityRawStamps (bridge.nix:269,336) -> ingest.nix:358-362.

★ THE DIFFERENTIATOR IS TYPE, NOT DECLARATION ROUTE. host.facts is ALSO declared via den.schema.host.imports (nix-config schema/host.nix:160,264-268) — same route, same formals — but its type is `nullOr path`, non-raw, so it lands in the safe stamp and arrives correctly. Same route, opposite outcome, differing only in raw-ness. That is the tightest possible isolation.

FIELD IS PRESENT BUT EMPTY, not absent: stampOf's reads are `or null`/`or { }`-guarded (registry.nix:311-313, "a stamp read may miss, never throw") and there is NO tryEval anywhere on the collection/channel path (verified), so an absent `microvm` attr would have THROWN. Nothing threw => the #70 overlay lands, carrying the option DEFAULT `[]` instead of the authored `[ cortex-cuda ]`.

UNSETTLED — WHY the overlay carries the default rather than the authored value. rawEntityStamps.hosts = stampRegistry hostRawStampTree hostEntries reads flattenRegistry (config.den.hosts or { }) (bridge.nix:243,269), which should hold the authored list. SETTLING EVAL (needs den internals — not reachable from flake outputs; needs a probe rig calling compat.mkDenWith on the corpus module set, or a temporary debug output):
    (den.structural.eval.get "host:cortex" "enriched-context").host.microvm.guests   # expect [] — confirms
    den._entityRawStamps.hosts.cortex.microvm.guests                                  # locates the drop

WORKING COMPARATOR: den-hoag CI already has a green witness for the shape — ci/tests/compat-fleet-context.nix:11-14 arm (B), a `{ environment, host, … }` channel emit resolving to a SET at the emitting node (U9.1 resolveParametric). The corpus's other parametric channel emits (nix-builders roles/nix-builder.nix:8-14, vault-peers services/security/vault.nix:7-11) read only NON-raw fields (host.name, host.ipv4, host.system). **microvm-guests is the ONLY corpus channel emit whose payload is a raw-typed field** — which is exactly why it is the one that fails.

RESOLVERS NOT THE CAUSE: den.lib.aspects.resolve / den.lib.resolveEntity are config-wired via the bridge (resolve-verbs.nix:35,104; bridge.nix:156-173). The inputs.den.lib entries are stubs (flake.nix:193,216) but the corpus reads `den` as a MODULE ARG (microvm-guests.nix:1), which is the wired one. They are never reached anyway — the producer returns [] first.

TWO DEFECTS, INDEPENDENT. The spurious standalone cortex-cuda output is a different mechanism at a different site: buildRoots enumerates every registries.host instance (build-roots.nix:17-45) and never consults intoAttr; v1 gated it in the fleet policy (nix-config policies/fleet.nix:69 `hostCfg.intoAttr != [ ]`), which den-hoag does not run. Registry-enumeration artifact per den-hoag-9xo.9. No shared root.

LOOSE THREAD (flagged, not chased, NOT folded into the finding): eval showed services.avahi.allowInterfaces = null / nssmdns4 = false (nixpkgs defaults) while enable = true, and no include of core.network.avahi exists in roles/ or hosts/. Most likely an upstream module pulling avahi in, not a den defect. Settling check: grep -rn "network.avahi" across nix-config, or inspect cortex's resolved-aspect key set.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
★★ THIS BEAD'S DIAGNOSIS IS REFUTED. Measured live, den-hoag 0d6174c against
nix-config f5f9dc99. Full detail: papers plans/2026-07-27-embedding-edge-investigation.md
(papers 336a3ed).

THE BEAD SAYS the guest fan-out "fires, bound to an EMPTY list" because
host.microvm.guests is listOf raw and excluded from the ctx stamp.

THE LIVE ERROR SAYS OTHERWISE:

  error: attribute 'aspect' missing
    at nix-config .../aspects/virtualization/microvm-guests.nix:43:77

That force is INSIDE `map (vm: ... vm.aspect ...) host.microvm.guests`.
`map f [ ]` CANNOT force f's body. So the guests list is NON-EMPTY AND IS BEING
DELIVERED. The exclusion the bead blames was real but #70 shipped its exact
dual (ledger u20, commit 77cb3c8) -- the field rides `_entityRawStamps`.

THE ACTUAL DEFECT, and it is SMALL and unrelated to the option's type:
den-hoag's baseEntityModule DELIBERATELY OMITS `aspect`
(lib/compat/registry.nix:32-40, :51-53). No corpus host authors it. And a
freeform-only value has no option record, so mkStampTree -- which walks
`options` -- can never stamp it. The guest record arrives without `aspect` and
the consumer reads it.

⇒ THIS IS NOT A DELIVERY BUG. It is a missing field on the delivered record.

NOTE: the ledger (u20) and RESUME-CHECKPOINT:127-129 ALREADY AGREED with this
measurement. THE BEAD WAS THE OUTLIER and nobody reconciled them. Two records
disagreed and the wrong one was the one being planned against -- den-hoag-9xo.30's
design work leaned on this bead's reading for several rounds.

★ AND RE-TYPING THE OPTION MAKES THIS STRICTLY WORSE. A ref type is not an
excludedType, so the field MOVES from the raw channel INTO the deepSeq'd safe

title: SETTLE §2.4: what consumes den.lib.policy.instantiate
description:
Close BEFORE plan-writing (design own call, reviewer concurred; cheap). §3.2 establishes "whoever attaches, instantiates" as an invariant of both topologies (v1 default system-to-os-outputs; corpus env-to-hosts fleet.nix:74) and calls it evidence for the activation gate — but §2.2 covers only resolve.to. What compat does with instantiate is unspecified, while hosts materialize unconditionally TODAY.

Emitted at: corpus fleet.nix:74, clusters.nix:104, batteries/colmena.nix:96.
SETTLING TEST: trace instantiate through lib/declarations.nix to its consumer. Does not gate the P-edge story; does gate den-hoag-9xo.9 (the activation gate).
notes:
VERDICT: DEFINITE on all four questions.

Q1 CHAIN (verified): compile.nix:1009-1012 `else if kind == "instantiate" then [ (declare.spawn { instantiate = effect.value; }) ]` (:992 explicitly separates it from the v1 policy.spawn arm) -> STRATUM structural (declarations.nix:39-47 groups.structural includes "spawn") -> CONSUMER default.nix:2309-2324 instantiateContributions, folded into the output families at :2349-2351.

Q2: OUTPUT/TERMINAL SURFACE — §2.4's assertion is CORRECT. It creates NO node. default.nix:2296-2298 says the spec is "parked"; ledger.md:41 row u4 confirms "declare.spawn { instantiate = spec } PARKS the spec (childless-inert — fleetChildren is membership-driven, so no scope node is added)".

★ Q3: DOES IT INHERIT THE ATTACHMENT'S GATING? **NO — gating must be applied SEPARATELY. This is the den-hoag-9xo.9 answer.** Two independent proofs:
(a) The consumer walks EVERY node: default.nix:2324 iterates builtins.attrNames structural.eval.allNodes and picks up any parked spec in that node's own structural declarations. Nothing consults whether a P edge attached anything; firing is governed solely by the EMITTING POLICY's own gate.
(b) The corpus ALREADY emits instantiate with NO attachment beside it: nix-config modules/den/batteries/colmena.nix:93-104 host-modules-capture is `{ host, ... }`-gated with NO resolve.to in the body; ledger.md:41 confirms it is "UNCONDITIONAL at every host".
=> "whoever attaches, instantiates" (§3.2 consequence 2) is a CORPUS AUTHORING CONVENTION — true of fleet.nix:70-75 because those two emissions sit in one body — NOT a framework guarantee. The design's inference ("instantiation is not a separable concern; it rides the attachment edge") is REFUTED: host-modules-capture is exactly the separable ungated case, and it is live corpus surface. THE ACTIVATION GATE NEEDS ITS OWN MECHANISM. (Corroborating: structural.nix:296-297 guardResolveFamily deliberately passes non-resolve-family declarations, incl. spawn, through untouched.)

★ Q4: WHY DO HOSTS MATERIALIZE UNCONDITIONALLY TODAY? NEITHER hypothesis — a THIRD path. Hosts never go through instantiate at all: registry enumeration -> scope root -> NATIVE NIXOS CLASS TERMINAL. build-roots.nix:12-37 makes every registry instance a scope root; builtins.nix:23-24 verbatim den-hoag "produces nixosConfigurations via the nixos CLASS terminal, NOT the v1 flake->flake-system output chain"; ledger.md:41 "the host resolves CLEAN and nixosConfigurations (CLASS-A) materialize NATIVELY".
=> **THE ACTIVATION GATE MUST GATE THE REGISTRY-ENUMERATION -> ROOT -> TERMINAL PATH, NOT THE instantiate PATH.** Gating instantiate would not touch host materialization at all.

★★ LIVE WITNESS — 9xo.9 IS ALREADY BROKEN TODAY, no design needed. nix-config modules/den/hosts/cortex-cuda.nix:5 sets `intoAttr = [ ]; # do not emit a standalone nixosConfiguration output` (v1's output opt-out; the corpus gates on it at fleet.nix:69 hostCfg.intoAttr != [ ]). In den-hoag the ONLY intoAttr consumers are registry.nix:165-192 (the option DECLARATION), nh.nix:26 (a CLI attr-path builder), and default.nix:2313 (the parked-spec placement path) — NOTHING in the native terminal path reads it as a gate.
ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations --apply builtins.attrNames` over the corpus returns ["axon-01","axon-02","axon-03","bitstream","blade","cortex","cortex-cuda","uplink"] — **cortex-cuda materializes a nixosConfiguration it explicitly opted out of.** Reproducible NOW, independent of the topology arc.

STALE COMMENT FOUND (own bead): declarations.nix:28-31 states verbatim that spawn/spawnShared/emit are "LATENT structural constructors ... nothing in the assembly consumes these kinds; they remain in the vocabulary for surface totality." REFUTED by default.nix:2320 which filters exactly `a.__action == "spawn" && a ? instantiate`. Anyone reading declarations.nix to answer this question gets the WRONG answer.

LEDGER IMPACT: ledger rows u2 (cluster-to-nixidy) and u4 (host-modules-capture) are latent-v1-divergence with specs parked and nixidyEnvs/colmenaModules output families den-hoag-ABSENT (ledger.md:38,41). u2 is inert ONLY because the environment coord is never bound — WHICH THIS DESIGN CHANGES — so u2's nixidyEnvs becomes LIVE under (c). Needs a §8.2 ledger row alongside accessGroups and collectedMembersOf.
close_reason: Settled definitively. instantiate = output/terminal surface at the structural stratum (compile.nix:1009-1012 -> default.nix:2309-2324); creates no node; does NOT inherit attachment gating (colmena.nix host-modules-capture is the live ungated counter-example) => 9xo.9 needs its own mechanism, and it must gate the registry-enumeration->root->terminal path, NOT instantiate. Live witness verified empirically: cortex-cuda materializes a nixosConfiguration despite intoAttr = [ ].

title: [gen-graph] order.nix cites Mokhov 2017 for topological enumeration; the paper contains neither the word nor the claim
description:
CITATION OVERSTATEMENT, verified independently TWICE with positive controls in the same run.

SITE: gen-graph/lib/order.nix:5-6 - THEORY: home-manager dag idiom (generalized strings-with-deps) over Mokhov 2017 section 4 quotient-graph topological enumeration.

OVERSTATES ON TWO COUNTS:

1. THE WORD. topological occurs ZERO times in Mokhov 2017. Source of record: papers/den-architecture/used/markdown/mokhov-2017-algebraic-graphs.md. Positive controls, same file same run: graph = 421 hits, condensation = 2 hits at lines 750 and 755, preorder = 4 hits, stem topolog = 0. So the grep works and the absence is real, not a dead predicate.

2. THE SCOPE, which is the substantive half. Section 4.6 Preorders and Equivalence Relations DERIVES the quotient - it is a construction, not an assumption - but says nothing about enumerating an ORDER over it. Verified exactly: the only occurrences of strongly-connected and scc in the entire paper are THREE LINES of section 4.6 - strongly-connected at 747 and 748, scc at 749. Mokhov explicitly DELEGATES the SCC computation to the containers library, so his contribution is the algebraic representation of the quotient - set-valued vertices, well-typed as Graph g, Vertex g ~ Set Int => g - not an algorithm and not an ordering procedure.

WHAT IS CORRECTLY CITED, for contrast - gen-graph/lib/global.nix:136 cites Tarjan 1972 / Kosaraju for SCCs; Mokhov 2017 section 4 for the quotient-graph idiom. THAT SPLIT IS CORRECTLY APPORTIONED: algorithm to Tarjan/Kosaraju, IDIOM to Mokhov. order.nix collapses the same split into one over-attributed phrase.

ADJACENT, worth reading together - global.nix:131-133 directly above that correct citation DISCLAIMS the algorithm: closure-based O(n squared) ... NOT Tarjan's linear O(V+E) single-DFS - its mutable stack/lowlink is out-of-substrate for pure Nix. So gen-graph is honest at global.nix and loose at order.nix.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A NIT: the gen theory-conformance audit treats provenance as a real gate, and its C5 COORDINATES check - does the cited section actually contain the cited content - has already found two defects in this corpus (Vogt, Mokhov). This is a third, in the same class. The gate's own posture is that prose is load-bearing because implementers act on it.

FIX: restate order.nix:5-6 to cite Mokhov only for what he supplies - the algebraic quotient representation - and attribute the phase-ordering / topological enumeration to whatever actually warrants it, mirroring the correct split already present at global.nix:136. If nothing warrants it, say so rather than borrowing.

PROVENANCE OF THIS FINDING: surfaced during the den-hoag kernel-purity arc while verifying a design that leans on condensation. Confirmed by the orchestrator and again by an independent adversarial reviewer, each with positive controls. The citation the DESIGN leans on - global.nix:136 - holds; this one does not.

title: Re-run W1/W2 with Nix-aware codebase-memory when it lands (owner-signalled)

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
INSTRUMENT VERIFIED AND CALIBRATED (2026-07-27, session resumed with Nix-aware codebase-memory). Read this
BEFORE any agent uses the graph, and treat the two limitations as load-bearing.

VERIFICATION: den-hoag indexed at 3094 nodes / 9279 edges, 2213 Function nodes, edge types incl. CALLS 1461,
USAGE 4182, DEFINES 2730. Positive control PASSED: search_graph "runPrePass" resolves to
lib/staged-resolution.nix:131-446 as a Function. Nix symbols ARE extracted.

★ TRAP 1 — get_architecture's `languages` FIELD DOES NOT LIST NIX. It reports only YAML (3 files) and
Python (1). An agent following the standing instruction "confirm coverage via get_architecture before
trusting a query" would read that field, conclude Nix is uncovered, and fall back to grep — discarding the
whole capability. COVERAGE MUST BE CONFIRMED BY A KNOWN-POSITIVE SYMBOL QUERY, not by the languages list.

★★ TRAP 2 — CALLS EDGES MISS ATTRSET-MEDIATED CALLS, WHICH IS NIX'S DOMINANT IDIOM. Measured:
  trace_path runPrePass inbound  -> ZERO callers
  grep runPrePass                -> lib/default.nix:1097  `prePass = stagedResolution.runPrePass { ... }`
The call is real; the graph does not see it, because the callee is reached through an imported attrset
(module imported as a value, member called off it) rather than by a bare identifier.
POSITIVE CONTROL PROVING THE DIRECTION WORKS AT ALL: trace_path fail inbound -> 23 callers. So caller-tracing
is functional; it is specifically the attrset-mediated cross-module call that is invisible.
⇒ "ZERO CALLERS" FROM THIS GRAPH IS NOT EVIDENCE OF DEAD CODE. Every zero-caller result must be cross-checked
with grep before any conclusion, and especially before any deletion. Within-file CALLS appear reliable;
cross-module CALLS through an attrset are incomplete.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RELAUNCH: the graph is a genuine upgrade for STRUCTURE questions (what exists, what a
function calls, clustering, fan-in ranking) and must NOT be trusted alone for REACHABILITY or
liveness/deadness. The text-search prior from the previous session is not superseded — the two instruments
are complementary, and a disagreement between them is a finding to investigate, not a tie to break by
preferring the newer tool.

SUBSTANTIVE LEAD FOR THE A1 QUESTION, established while calibrating (NOT a verdict):
  - runPrePass is LIVE: lib/staged-resolution.nix:131-446 (315 lines), called at lib/default.nix:1097.
  - Its own header comment, lib/staged-resolution.nix:104, calls it "the transpose carrier. Returns
    { tuples; containmentBindings; containmentAncestors; ... }" — language consistent with the claimed
    dissolution ("runPrePass state-accumulator DISSOLVED -> prelude.groupBy per-target carrier + demand-read").
  - Direct callees per the graph: kindParent, mintedRootId, rootNodeIndex, baseCtxOf, fireFeedAt,
    isContainment, attachmentsOf, foldBindings, ownedBy, deliverCtxOf.
  - Graph clustering puts it in one cluster with mkDen, buildRoots, mintedRootId, ancNodeId (cohesion 1.0).
  ⇒ THE FUNCTION SURVIVED THE RENAME. Whether the ACCUMULATOR SHAPE survived — i.e. SHIPPED-REAL vs
    SHIPPED-RENAMED-ONLY — is exactly the open question and is NOT answered by any of the above. 315 lines is
    a large "carrier". This is the W2 question; do not infer the verdict from the name or the comment.

title: SPIKE (user-guided): does the alternate graph API belong in den-hoag or gen?
description:
NEEDS A USER-GUIDED DESIGN DECISION, and it is a design spike, not a lookup.

THE VISION (owner): an alternate den API that makes graph expressions explicit — a companion to, and alternative to, den's current surface.

THE QUESTION: is that a den-hoag surface, or a den BINDING of a gen-level surface? gen-graph already owns accessor-based query combinators (reachableFrom, canReach, dependentsOf, cycles, condensation, phaseOrder) and gen-select owns a selector algebra over graph positions with 12 constructors and adapters for both gen-scope and gen-graph. A new den API that re-expresses those would be the built-what-exists pattern this project has hit three times.

WHY IT IS GATED: specifying this before the kernel purity audit (W2) reports would design against the CURRENT representation, which is the very thing under question. If W2 finds the kernel carries value-shaped machinery, an API designed on top of it inherits the shape.

INPUT WHEN IT RUNS: the reuse-scan on den-hoag-8rf already inventoried all 20 gen libraries for query surface and found that gen-product supplies coordinate-tuple addressing (cells, coordsOf, fiber, slice, restrict) and that uniformity over a lifted graph is a THEOREM of the existing layering rather than new code. That scan is directly reusable here.

title: W3: drift and lost-context sweep over the 2026-07 corpus

title: __provider identity reconstruction is still live on the bridge path
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger part 2 (row 20.8), 2026-07-27.

REFERENCE.md "Chosen #8" states the __provider shadow-identity layer "is DELETED" and that the only
remaining __provider is "the single v1-reserved literal in key-classification.nix (the reserved-key
exclusion, NOT a reconstruction)".

HALF OF THAT HOLDS: annotate.nix and stamp-provider.nix are gone, and compile does ground identity on
gen-aspects' native .key. But two parts are false as written:

(i) It is NOT the single v1-reserved literal there. builtinStructuralKeys carries __contentValues,
    __providesForwarded, __ctxId, __entityKind, __parametricResolvedArgs, __scopeHandlers, __fn and __args
    alongside it.

(ii) A LIVE IDENTITY RECONSTRUCTION SURVIVES. lib/compat/den-brackets.nix:41-47 tagProvider WRITES
     result // { __provider = path; }. Its own comment says it exists "so the pipeline can compute stable
     identity ... without this, they get anonymous identities and dedup fails". It is wired in as __findFile
     at lib/compat/bridge.nix:171.

So the doc claims a layer is dissolved while a writer for it is still on the bridge path. Whether that
stamp is REMOVABLE is a code question, not a docs question — which is why this is a bead and not a ledger
row correction. The docs fix is downstream of the answer.

Relevant: the north star is dissolving effect-runtime holdovers, and a surviving identity-reconstruction
stamp is exactly that shape. See [[project_denhoag_kernel_primary_surface]] and the effects audit.

title: claim-accessor ships an undocumented queryEdges variant outside the L4 silent/throwing contract
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger part 2 (row 15.9), 2026-07-27.

The claim-accessor ships a THIRD variant, queryEdges, that REFERENCE.md L121 does not mention. The
documented contract is a two-variant capability boundary:
  .query <kind>   SILENT  — a missing or out-of-scope claim kind yields [ ] (the exploratory-query mode)
  .rel.<kind>     THROWING — an out-of-scope kind is REPLACED with a NAMED throw

That silent-vs-throwing split is load-bearing for L4 stratified negation: a negation MUST be read through
the throwing gate, because a negation over a silently-empty predicate cannot distinguish "absent" from
"out-of-scope".

An undocumented third variant is therefore not a doc-completeness nit. If queryEdges is silent and a
consumer writes a stratified negation against it, that is precisely the error the L4 contract exists to
prevent — and the contract cannot warn about a variant it does not name.

NEEDED: establish queryEdges' silent-vs-throwing behaviour, decide whether it belongs in the documented
contract or should be internal, and if it is silent, whether the L4 guidance needs to name it explicitly.
Docs follow the answer.

title: Sweep specs/plans for orphaned pre-beads work
description:
Sweep specs/ + plans/ for DESIGNED OR SCOPED WORK that predates beads adoption and was never tracked —
work that exists as a design document and as nothing else.

CORPUS: 154 specs + 208 plans (+93 .md.tasks.json sidecars from the pre-beads task format) against 73 beads
(42 open / 30 closed / 1 in progress). Most of the corpus predates the tracker.

CLASSIFY each work-scoping document as:
  SHIPPED     — the work exists in the tree (cite the evidence)
  TRACKED     — a bead covers it (cite the id)
  SUPERSEDED  — a later document replaced it (cite which)
  ORPHANED    — designed/scoped, not shipped, not tracked, not superseded  <- THE DELIVERABLE
  HISTORICAL  — a record, review, or decision log that scopes no work

BLOCKED ON den-hoag-9w8 (corpus reorganization). Deliberate: sweeping a flat 362-document corpus costs far
more than sweeping a subject-organized one, and 9w8's manifest — filename, date, first heading, Status line,
subject — is most of the input this sweep needs. Running this first would mean building that manifest twice.

METHOD NOTES, learned this session:
- An ABSENCE claim needs a positive control on the same predicate. The h5d ledger had a predicate false-clean
  on shipped `pipe.<verb>` names because they are defined inside a `pipe = { ... }` block and used only in
  ci/. Confirm each predicate finds a known-positive before reporting nothing.
- "Not implemented" and "cut from scope" are INDISTINGUISHABLE from the tree — the h5d ledger hit this on
  fleet features. Where they cannot be separated, say so; do not pick one.
- Report coverage depth honestly. A partial sweep reported as partial is useful; reported as complete it is
  worse than nothing.

OUT OF SCOPE: gen-rebuild, hola (owner ruling). Also used/, reference-catalog/ (academic PDFs), demos/.
DO NOT create beads from findings — the orphan list comes back for review first, then gets filed.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
SIDECARS ARE THIS BEAD'S PRIMARY EVIDENCE — measured 2026-07-27, and it makes this sweep cheaper.

The 93 plans/*.md.tasks.json sidecars are the PRE-BEADS TASK FORMAT, superseded to the day (last sidecar
2026-07-25, earliest bead 2026-07-26). Their aggregate status:

  360 completed · 38 done · 1 done_except_push · 220 PENDING

220 pending tasks across 93 plans, each already carrying `subject`, `description`, `blockedBy`, and
metadata `files` / `verifyCommand` / `acceptanceCriteria`. That is a structured record of scoped work that
never completed and never migrated to the tracker — exactly what this bead is looking for, without having
to infer it from prose.

METHOD CONSEQUENCE: first pass is a JOIN, not a read. Extract the 220 pending tasks, then classify each as
SHIPPED (the work exists in the tree anyway) / TRACKED (a bead covers it) / SUPERSEDED / ORPHANED. Only the
residue needs document reading. This also means the bead is partly INDEPENDENT of den-hoag-9w8 — the
sidecar join does not need the corpus reorganized first, though the prose-reading residue still benefits.

CAUTION: `pending` in a sidecar means "not marked done in a file nobody updated after 2026-07-25". It is
evidence of an unfinished RECORD, not proof of unfinished WORK — a task may well have shipped with the
sidecar left stale. Every pending item needs a tree check before it is called orphaned, and the count 220
should never be reported as an orphan count.

title: Papers corpus reorganization: subject subfolders + cheap-tier classification
description:
SPEC (pre-review, no files moved): papers/den-architecture/plans/2026-07-27-papers-corpus-reorganization-plan.md

WHY: specs/ (154 files) and plans/ (208 .md + 93 .md.tasks.json sidecars) are flat date-ordered dumps mixing
every subject. gen-specs/ already has 23 subject subfolders and 120 files — the pattern existed and was lost.
A flat corpus makes both the design-vs-tree audit (den-hoag-h5d) and the orphaned-work sweep expensive.

MEASURED: filenames are YYYY-MM-DD-<subject-slug>.md, so the slug carries the subject — that is what makes a
cheap classification tier viable. But slug keywords cover only a MINORITY: hoag 63 / den-hoag 55 (a subset) /
gen-schema 17 / parity 8 / gen-aspects 7 / nix-config 5 / rest <= 4. A large remainder names a TOPIC rather
than a subject (hero-canvas-animation, generic-sidecars, library-decomposition). The residue is what the
cheap tier exists for.

THE HAZARD, and it shapes the design: 185 papers files carry 416 references to 179 DISTINCT specs//plans/
paths; 108 memory files reference them; 14 beads; 2 den-hoag tracked files. A move without a rewrite breaks
all of it. Mitigation is the cheapest tier of all and uses NO model: the move manifest IS the rewrite map,
applied as pure textual substitution, plus a MOVES.md redirect index generated from the same manifest.
ACCEPTANCE TEST: zero references match a specs//plans/ path that no longer exists.

PIPELINE, cheapest first:
  T0  deterministic, no model — build manifest (filename, date, first heading, Status line, sidecar pairing),
      apply an explicit keyword->subject map, emit subject|UNRESOLVED + confidence. A .md.tasks.json sidecar
      ALWAYS moves with its parent and is never classified independently.
  T1  CHEAP AGENT (haiku), manifest METADATA ONLY — never reads file bodies, which is what keeps it cheap and
      makes a small model appropriate. Returns subject + confidence, instructed to answer UNSURE rather than
      guess. Batched.
  T2  orchestrator — adjudicates only UNSURE and disagreements. Input should be tens of files, not hundreds.
  T0' deterministic apply — moves, reference rewrite, MOVES.md. No model.

TAXONOMY: subject names MIRROR the existing 23 gen-specs/ folders so one vocabulary serves both trees, plus
non-library subjects derived from the corpus (den-v1, den-hoag, nix-config, diagram, theory, infra,
unrelated). Recommended layout is subject subfolders INSIDE the artifact-type dirs (specs/<subject>/,
plans/<subject>/), leaving gen-specs/<subject>/ unchanged as living CONTRACTS — folding 63 dated hoag design
docs into gen-specs/den-hoag/ would bury its 6 contract files under their own history.

OUT OF SCOPE: gen-rebuild and hola (owner ruling) — recorded in the manifest as deliberately skipped, not as
unresolved. Also untouched: used/, reference-catalog/ (academic PDFs), demos/, parity/, STATUS/. Content is
never rewritten, nothing is deleted, and SHIPPED-vs-ORPHANED is explicitly NOT decided here — that is the
audit this unblocks, and conflating them would put a judgment call inside a mechanical pass.

OPEN FOR REVIEW (spec §8): (1) subject-inside-artifact-type vs subject-first — expensive to reverse once 416
references are rewritten; (2) does archive/ stay a location or become per-subject, i.e. how do the lifecycle
and subject axes compose; (3) do the 93 .md.tasks.json sidecars survive at all, or are they superseded by
beads — answer BEFORE the move or the work is wasted; (4) is theory a subject or a cross-cutting tag.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER DECISIONS (2026-07-27).

LAYOUT (spec §8.1) — SUBJECT INSIDE ARTIFACT-TYPE. specs/<subject>/ and plans/<subject>/;
gen-specs/<subject>/ stays untouched as living contracts. Smallest move, preserves the artifact-type
distinction that already exists, adds only the missing subject axis.

SIDECARS (spec §8.3) — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, and my framing in the spec was WRONG.
The 93 .md.tasks.json files are SUPERSEDED BY BEADS, confirmed to the day: last sidecar 2026-07-25,
earliest bead 2026-07-26. Schemas map 1:1 — id / subject / status / description / blockedBy /
metadata{files, verifyCommand, acceptanceCriteria} onto bd's issue, dependency and acceptance fields.

But they are NOT dead weight, which is what the spec speculated. Status distribution across all 93:
  360 completed · 38 done · 1 done_except_push · 220 PENDING
220 pending tasks that predate the tracker, already structured, carrying `files` and `acceptanceCriteria`.
That is den-hoag-deb's PRIMARY EVIDENCE, not clutter.
=> ARCHIVE IN PLACE (do not distribute into subject folders, do not delete), and mine them as deb's
   first-pass input. deb is consequently cheaper than specced and partly independent of this reorg.

CORPUS SUBJECT — NO. Only 10 documents mention den-configs, and they are den-hoag work ABOUT the external
corpus rather than work ON it. A tag, not a folder. denconfigs-revalidated resolves to den-hoag.

CLASSIFICATION COMPLETE, 359/359, persisted at plans/2026-07-27-papers-corpus-manifest.tsv (with .bak):
  T0 deterministic 166 · T0b heading-aware +44 · T1 haiku (metadata only) +149 · T2 orchestrator +12
  corrected, 4 held for owner.
  den-hoag 189 · gen-schema 32 · gen-aspects 30 · unrelated 24 · gen 22 · gen-other 12 · parity 7 ·
  nix-config 6 · UNSURE 4 · rest <= 4.
BOTH VALIDATION GATES FOUND REAL DEFECTS: my deterministic tier ran ~14% wrong until sampling caught it
(slug tokens beat headings); haiku ~6-12% with one clear miss (fleet-pipe-visualization -> diagram).
Neither surfaced without sampling a bucket that looked fine in aggregate.

4 STILL HELD FOR OWNER (T2:HOLD-owner): denconfigs-revalidated (now resolved to den-hoag per above),
f1-inputs-self-nodes-design (gen-scope vs den-hoag — the inputs'/self' battery straddles both),
den-server-m1-projection-plan (den-server/gen-lsp vs den-hoag), bitstream-f1-gap-diagnosis (reads like
neither den nor gen).

STILL GATED: T0' (the moves + the 416-reference rewrite) has no remaining blocker except execution.

title: [codebase-memory-mcp] Nix bindings mint no Variable nodes — nix_var_types has no name resolver
description: nix_var_types = {"binding"} is declared in lang_specs.c, but extract_defs.c has a Nix name resolver only for function_expression (line 827, via the parent binding's attrpath). A plain 'x = value;' binding therefore resolves no name and mints nothing. Measured: den-hoag Variable count is 10 on v0.8.1, 10 on HEAD, and 10 on HEAD+the function-header fix — unchanged across all three, and those 10 are not Nix. Fix shape mirrors the existing function resolver: for a 'binding' node take child_by_field_name(attrpath) then its 'attr'. Separate from den-hoag-cah; do not bundle.
acceptance_criteria: A let/attrset binding of a non-function value mints a Variable node with the correct name

title: Point codebase-memory-mcp at its own flake (HEAD) and correct the Nix-coverage hook text
description: nix-config pins pkgs.codebase-memory-mcp from nixpkgs at v0.8.1 (2026-06-12), which predates Nix def/call extraction (landed 0849f28c 2026-06-27, shipped v0.9.0). Measured on den-hoag: v0.8.1 gives 7 Functions (all Python) / 8 CALLS; HEAD gives 39 Nix Functions / 38 CALLS. Switch modules/den/aspects/apps/dev/ai/mcp/codebase-memory-mcp.nix to the upstream flake input (github:DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp) via flake-file.inputs + inputs'.codebase-memory-mcp.packages.default. Also rewrite the SessionStart/SubagentStart hook text: it currently asserts 'NIX IS NOT COVERED ... file-tree-only tier', which is false and steers agents away from a working tool.
acceptance_criteria: nix-config evaluates; claude-code mcpServers.codebase-memory points at the flake package; hook text states actual Nix coverage including the function-header limitation

title: Docs conformance pass: measure den-hoag design docs against the tree
description:
SPEC (pre-review, no edits): papers/den-architecture/plans/2026-07-27-docs-conformance-pass-plan.md

GAP: DEVIATIONS.md and CHANGES.md are both spec-vs-spec (which spec superseded which). NOTHING tracks spec-vs-IMPLEMENTATION, so doc drift has no detector. Same failure shape as den-hoag-9xo.27 at the code level: the only check that exists cannot observe the thing that drifted. The tell is two independent docs carrying the SAME phantom vocabulary (den.collections, spawn/emit) — they were updated from each other, not from the tree.

MEASURED 2026-07-27 vs den-hoag c0aa7be:
- REFERENCE.md 'Shipped vs Spec-Only Status' is INVERTED — lists HOAG eval model / 12 attributes / buildRoots / parseParent / neededBy / bind.wrapAll as NOT IMPLEMENTED; all ship. Only den.collections is absent (0 files) and that is a rename that never happened (den.quirks, 9 files).
- Library inventory: doc says '8 gen libraries'; den-hoag flake has 19. Missing incl. gen-resolve — which the doc's own Phase-5 sections lean on as the one conductor.
- Purity claim reversed: gen-schema/gen-aspects are no longer nixpkgs-lib-tethered (re-hosted on gen-merge).
- 12-attribute table drifted structurally: guard-set no longer exists (folded into resolved-aspects self-circular, default.nix:897); 9 attributes have no row.
- Headline compression claim '~1,010-1,510 lines replacing ~7,000, 4-5x' vs measured lib/ = 24,655 (kernel 13,337 + compat 11,318). Kernel-only is ~10x the estimate. Needs an EXPLANATION, not a silent restatement.
- specs/2026-05-24-unified-vocabulary.md is a redirect to ~/Documents/repos/gen-docs/ — path does not exist. Live: ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen/TERMINOLOGY.md.
- TERMINOLOGY.md is well-maintained on the LIBRARY axis (18 libs, 2026-07-06) but its den-side vocabulary is stale identically to REFERENCE.md. gen-class and gen-link have no entry. gen-link's ABSENCE from den-hoag's lock is CORRECT (verified: no node, no import; origin identity routes through gen-aspects aspectId).

SCOPE: two repos, five files — papers (REFERENCE, new CONFORMANCE.md, CHANGES, the redirect stub) + the gen repo (TERMINOLOGY.md, docs-only commit). NO code changes.

METHOD: every corrected claim sourced to a COMMAND recorded beside it in CONFORMANCE.md. Each drift classified (a) doc wrong (b) intentional evolution -> CHANGES.md (c) genuinely unimplemented, with evidence. Deliverable is a re-runnable ledger, not prose — that is what makes the NEXT drift detectable.

NEXT STEP IS REVIEW OF THE SPEC. See §9 open questions (CONFORMANCE.md separate vs inline; whether the gen-repo commit is its own change; where the line-budget finding lands; whether to drop per-library test counts as a drift class).

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
RESOLVED (owner, 2026-07-27) — spec §9.4: per-library TEST COUNTS are DROPPED as a class, not re-verified.

The integration map's `Tests` column goes away, along with the counts in the shipped list (gen-algebra 144,
gen-schema 379, gen-aspects 130-in-table-vs-67-in-list, gen-graph 110, gen-scope 152, gen-select 103,

comments.text:

synthetics. So it is NOT reframed as an unmeasured design argument (my recommendation was wrong — there is
a basis) and NOT left silently unmeasurable.
