real and validate the MEMOIZATION MODEL — multi-level attribute-dependent synthesis and an independent
replication of the HOAG architecture — but they are not the 500-host table.
=> LEDGER TREATMENT: cite the canonical spec as provenance for the step counts and demos/ as the model
   synthetics; flag the WALL-TIME column ("Milliseconds" / "~1 second" / "Minutes") as the part carrying no
   cited basis. Benchmark harness filed separately as post-ship.

pipe.withConfig (§8.11) — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT: NEVER BUILT ANYWHERE. `git log --all -S withConfig`
returns 0 commits in den-hoag, and den v1 has 0 hits. So it is not a rename of producerConfigs; it is a
design intent that never shipped. Classification (c), not (a). Chosen #5's claim that it "explicitly marks
the expensive path" describes a discipline that has never existed on either side.

meta.substitute (§8.12) — ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT: `git log --all -S 'meta.substitute'` returns 0 commits.
Never built, not cut after building. Classification (c).

title: [gen-schema] Composite registries: grouped indexing + uniform meta-query
description:
den's grammar den.hosts.<system>.<hostname> is a COMPOSITE registry — per-system sub-registries composing one host kind. gen-schema cannot represent it, so den-hoag FLATTENS it (lib/compat/registry.nix preprocessHosts + flattenRegistry) to fit a single attrsOf, and meta-query over the composite then has nowhere to live.

Root gap (measured 2026-07-27): gen-schema has NO registry-level surface at all. Introspection is entirely schema-level (_kindNames/_topology/_edges/_roots/_leaves on the schema option); mkInstanceRegistry returns a bare merge.mkOption. Kinds are first-class, instances are first-class, registries are not.

Depends on the registry DESCRIPTOR landing first (den-hoag-m0a): the descriptor carries index.shape, so grouped registries slot into the same field without a breaking change.

BEFORE DESIGNING: reuse-scan the gen ecosystem — gen-graph query combinators, gen-select selector algebra, gen-resolve. 'Uniform query over a grouped collection' may already exist one layer up. Prior art on building-what-exists is recorded in [[feedback_reuse_scan_before_build]].

Owner framing: pure gen libs must have real usage outside den; prefer a general library solution over den-hoag special-casing.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
REUSE-SCAN COMPLETE (2026-07-27, all 20 gen libs, read-only). Verdict per capability:

CAP 1 — grouped indexing (path/tuple addressing, group coordinate on each entry)
  declaration layer: DOES NOT EXIST.
  graph/query layer: EXISTS FULLY — gen-product. Cells are coordinate tuples; view.nix:161,219-227
  nodeData = coordsOf cellId puts the coordinate on every cell; fiber (default.nix:37-39) addresses one
  group; slice composes fixings (view.nix:249-267); restrict enumerates sparsely without materializing
  the dense product (membership.nix:37-63,132-144). factor.nix:26-40 already accepts a non-id_hash
  key/entryOf pair, so plain system strings are legal coordinates.

CAP 2 — uniform meta-query over the composite: PARTIALLY EXISTS.
  The uniformity MECHANISM ships and does not branch on shape — a product IS an accessor graph, so every
  gen-graph query and gen-select adapter runs unchanged. Missing piece is only the LIFT: gen-graph
  registry.fromRegistry is flat-only BY CONSTRUCTION (gen-graph/lib/registry.nix:11,
  nodes = builtins.attrNames registry).

NESTED-REGISTRY QUESTION — ANSWERED NO, tested both directions. This was the most likely
"it already exists" result and it fails:
  FORWARD: mkInstanceRegistry returns an mkOption, NOT a type (gen-schema/lib/instance.nix:478), so it
  cannot be a freeformType; a nested registry must hang off a NAMED option, yielding
  den.hosts.<sys>.hosts.<name> — not den's grammar. It also requires <system> to be a declared KIND with
  instances; den's keys are lib.systems.flakeExposed strings, and a non-kind can never enter _topology
  (kind-to-kind off a parent collection, entry-type.nix:328-357).
  BACKWARD (cost if forced): drops the ENTIRE apply pipeline — ref-binding validation, deferred coerce,
  refinements, validators, derive. The pipeline is flat-keyed throughout, and validators infer option
  names via attrNames (head (attrValues instances)) (instance.nix:344-348) — on two-level input that
  reads HOST NAMES AS OPTION NAMES. options.name defaults to the immediate submodule key (:54-57), so
  under attrsOf (attrsOf ...) the group coordinate is structurally INVISIBLE to the entry, which is
  exactly why den-hoag hand-injects it (den-hoag/lib/compat/registry.nix:114-121).

THE GAP — two pieces, two libraries, do not build a third thing:
  gen-schema: mkInstanceRegistry needs an INDEX SHAPE parameter — type nests to declared depth,
  applyPipeline walks at that depth instead of assuming one level, group coordinate materializes on
  entries. This is EXACTLY the index.shape field den-hoag-y53's __registry descriptor reserves.
  gen-graph: extend registry.fromRegistry to lift a grouped registry into the accessor-graph convention.
  That is the WHOLE of cap 2 — uniformity is then a theorem of the existing layering, not new code.

NEW SUB-GAP, not previously on this bead: den admits a UNION of two index shapes on ONE option
(den.hosts.slab carrying a system field, OR den.hosts.x86_64-linux.slab). NO gen library models a
declaration accepting two shapes. There is also no general shape-coercion-at-registration mechanism:
mkInstanceRegistry's apply runs POST-merge, too late to reshape input before type-checking. den-hoag's
two-phase workaround (permissive deepMergeAttrs collector, then apply re-merges through the strict inner
type, registry.nix:446-522) is built on the CONSUMER's nixpkgs lib.types — not on the gen substrate at all.

FALSE FRIEND, recorded so it is not mistaken for prior art: gen-flake selectHosts (compose.nix:169-171)
says "nested registry" meaning a registry at a nested option PATH — still a flat attrset, not grouping.

Adjacent, non-transferring: gen-aspects flatten (path-keyed string identity, homogeneous unbounded
recursion); gen-class mkClasses (real partition-by-key, no lookup surface, no member coordinate);
gen-link disjointUnion (composes per-group subgraphs by ID QUALIFICATION, the same move as den-hoag's
node-multiplication ruling, not tuple indexing).

CONSEQUENCE FOR den-hoag-y53: its spec 9.3 asked whether index earns its place before this arc is
designed. Independent evidence says YES — the composite gap lands exactly on that field.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (2026-07-27) — the two index shapes: MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE IS FINE.

The reuse-scan flagged a sub-gap: den admits a UNION of two index shapes on ONE option, and no gen library
models a declaration accepting two shapes. That sub-gap is now OUT OF SCOPE — a registry declares ONE index
shape. The composite arc therefore needs grouped `<system>.<host>` ONLY.

Owner adds: `host.system` (the FLAT form — `den.hosts.slab` carrying a `system` field) is largely
UNDOCUMENTED in den; most external users are still on `system.host` (the two-level
`den.hosts.<system>.<hostname>` grammar).

CONSEQUENCES:
- The shape-coercion-at-registration gap the scan reported (mkInstanceRegistry's `apply` runs post-merge,
  too late to reshape input) does NOT need a general mechanism. den-hoag's `preprocessHosts`
  (lib/compat/registry.nix:468) stays a COMPAT-BOUNDARY coercion for the undocumented flat form, and is a
  deprecation candidate rather than something to lift into gen.
- The arc's declaration surface is single-shape, which is materially smaller than the scan assumed.

DOC CONFLICT TO RESOLVE (feeds den-hoag-h5d): gen-specs/den-hoag/REFERENCE.md calls the TWO-LEVEL form the
"legacy" one and presents the flat form as the enabling feature — the owner's reading is the inverse (the
two-level form is what external users use; the flat form is undocumented). One of those is wrong and the
docs currently assert the one the owner contradicts.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
OWNER RULING (2026-07-27) — DOGFOODING: internally den-hoag uses gen modules EXCLUSIVELY; nixpkgs lib only
when TRANSLATING or TESTING.

This bears directly on the arc. The reuse-scan measured that den-hoag's own host-registry machinery —
`mkHostsOption`'s two-phase trick (permissive `deepMergeAttrs` collector, then `apply` re-merging through the
strict inner type, lib/compat/registry.nix:440-522) — is built on the CONSUMER's nixpkgs `lib.types`, not on
the gen substrate at all. Under this ruling that is a violation, not a detail: it is den-hoag's own registry
construction, not a translation.

So moving `den.hosts` onto the gen substrate is now a REASON for this arc, independent of query uniformity.
The scan's finding that `den.hosts.<system>.<hostname>` is built by `mkHostsOption` and NOT by
`mkInstanceRegistry` is the same fact seen from the other side: the one composite registry den has was built
outside gen because gen could not express it.

Boundary question the arc must answer explicitly rather than assume: the bridge's `options.den` declaration
uses nixpkgs `lib.types.submodule` (lib/compat/bridge.nix:447). That one is plausibly legitimate TRANSLATION
— it is where den-hoag meets the consumer's flake-parts/nixpkgs module system. `mkHostsOption` is not.
Draw the line where the ruling puts it, and state which side each site falls on.

comments.author: Jason Bowman
comments.text:
PARKED BY OWNER RULING 2026-07-27 (full text on den-hoag-4kh.7, which is closed as resolved).

★ THE NEW BLOCKING EDGE ON den-hoag-4kh ENCODES CORRECTNESS, NOT COST. Do not strip it as a cheapness
dependency. This project has previously had two blocking edges removed for encoding cost against the beads'
own text — this is not one of them, and here is the reason in full so a future sweep can check rather than
guess.

THEORY: compat is a THIN VAN WYK MAP ONTO THE KERNEL'S REPRESENTATION. This work hardens a compat seam
(y53: the bridge arm feeding _registryKinds at lib/compat/ingest.nix:528; 8rf: registry shape). A map onto
an unsettled denotation is built against a moving target — constructing a morphism WHOSE CODOMAIN IS STILL
CHANGING. The kernel-purity arc is precisely the work of fixing that codomain. So the dependency is not
"cheaper to do later", it is "the thing this maps onto is not yet defined".

UNPARK CONDITION — AN EVENT, NOT A DATE: when the kernel-purity arc has ruled on the registry/identity
representation these seams map onto.

WHAT DID NOT PARK, and why the distinction matters:
 · den-hoag-m0a STAYS OPEN as the defect record. A declared registry resolving to NO kind, reaching the
   fleet EMPTY with nothing reddening, is MEASURED FACT and belongs in the graph on its own — regardless of
   which remedy is chosen or whether the chosen remedy changes shape. SEPARATE THE DEFECT FROM THE REMEDY.
   Beads hold VALIDATED work: a measured defect qualifies, a proposed fix does not. Same treatment as
   den-hoag-4kh.12.
 · den-hoag-00g PROCEEDS. gen-merge silently right-biasing a redeclared option WHERE NIXPKGS ABORTS is a
   soundness violation in the algebra itself, independent of den-hoag's representation, so no kernel-shape
   risk attaches to fixing it. y53 was blocked on it regardless, so this ordering costs nothing even on the
   parked branch.

title: [v1 defect] policy relation has 70 nodes and 0 edges; and the graph is a forest, not a rooted DAG
description:
V1 DEFECT. A relation exists as a NODE ROLE with NO CORRESPONDING EDGE, in every
config measured. This is "every relation an edge" violated inside v1 itself.

policyEdges (graph.nix:515-530) emits style="policy" ONLY when entry.to != null.
MEASURED on nix-config: `to` is null on ALL 843 nodes, while `from` is non-null
on exactly the 70 isPolicyDispatch nodes. So ZERO policy edges exist in ANY
measured IR, in ANY of the 12 configs.

AND IT WOULD DANGLE IF FIXED NAIVELY: the intended target id (ctx_<kind>) refers
to graph.entityKinds, which fleet-ir.nix never copies into `nodes`. So even with
`to` populated, the edge would point at a node that is not in the graph.

⇒ 70 policy-dispatch nodes, 0 policy edges, and the target vocabulary is not in
the node set.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md (papers 9eb5439).

RELATED, from the same map: the graph is a FOREST, NOT A ROOTED DAG. With the
flake root filtered out (correctly -- see den-hoag-9xo.31), every config has >=1
parentless scope and 3 have more: nix-config has 3 roots (fleet:fleet,
flake-system:aarch64-darwin, flake-system:x86_64-linux), example and fleet-demo
have 2, and nvf-standalone has NINE ROOTS, ZERO EDGES AND ZERO ASPECT NODES --
a valid den template whose entire topology is nine isolated points.

WHY BOTH MATTER: the owner's target is "correct and pure topology -- every
entity a node, every relation an edge". These are the two places v1's own graph
does not meet it. Under the standing instruction, where den-hoag uncovers a real
v1 defect we correct it rather than reproduce it -- so these bound what "parity
with v1" can mean.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: Most external den configs cannot evaluate against their own pin or den HEAD — the templates are the usable witness set
description:
MOST EXTERNAL den CONFIGS CANNOT BE EVALUATED against either their own den pin
or den HEAD. This bounds what "parity with v1" can be measured against.

MEASURED (papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md, papers
9eb5439): of 9 external configs attempted, 3 produced full IRs.

  against their OWN den pin:
    dotfiles, denix, oceangreendev, nixos.den, slashfiles
    -> error: attribute 'capture' missing
    These configs pin den revisions PREDATING den.lib.capture.

  against LOCAL den HEAD (API drift):
    slashfiles      -> option '...users.theutz.id_hash' is read-only, set multiple times
    gwenodai-nixos  -> function 'anonymous lambda' called without required argument 'class'
    oceangreendev   -> option 'perSystem.x86_64-linux.__provider' does not exist
    adda-nixos-config -> attribute 'each' missing

  not den failures:
    nixfos -> private input (ssh://git@github.com/xfo-0/moor), fetch failure
    several -> HTTP 403 from api.github.com after lock deletion (harness artifact)

Templates fared better: 8 of 13 produced IRs. The 5 failures were mostly BY
DESIGN (bogus is deliberately broken; noflake has no flake.nix; ci is a test
harness) plus 2 harness artifacts.

⇒ CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXIT CONDITION. "Parity with v1" has a moving target: the
external corpus largely cannot run against current den, so it cannot serve as a
parity oracle without first resolving which den revision parity is against.
DEN'S OWN TEMPLATES ARE THE USABLE WITNESS SET -- they track den, they are
authored by den, and 8 of 13 evaluate.

⇒ AND IT REFRAMES THE STANDING RULE. "Gate on den-surface expressibility, not
corpus-presence" is right, but the practical corpus is the TEMPLATES plus
nix-config, not the 19 external configs. Claiming a surface is unused should
cite the templates.

Related: reference memory `reference_den_corpus_set`.
NOT SCHEDULED -- this is a constraint to plan around, not a task.

title: [v1 defect] scope tree and aspect graph key on different identities; three of the owner's host scopes are orphans
description:
V1 DEFECT, and it affects the owner's own fleet TODAY.

The scope tree and the aspect graph key on DIFFERENT IDENTITIES, and the aspect
graph silently drops the difference. Scopes are keyed by FULL CTX; aspect nodes
are keyed by host NAME (hostGraphs.<name>, prefixId hostName). Where an entity
has two scopes, lib.findFirst collapses them -- in THREE places:

  fleet-ir.nix:341     picks one host scope per host name for the root edge
  context.nix:67-69    picks one scope per (kind,name) for the projection itself
  fleet-ir.nix:360-364 does it again for pipe-flow endpoints

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE on nix-config: 11 host scopes, only 8 hostRootEdges.
axon-01, axon-02 and axon-03's CLUSTER-PATH SCOPES ARE ORPHANS -- zero children,
no aspect graph, no root edge. They exist as nodes with a containment edge in
and nothing else.

It is the ONLY config in the 12 measured that exhibits it, and it exhibits it
because it is the only one with a `cluster` kind creating a SECOND ROUTE to a
host. So it is a defect that only appears once an entity is reachable by two
paths -- exactly the multi-attachment shape den-hoag's node multiplication was
built for.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-topology-correspondence-map.md (papers 9eb5439).

WHY IT MATTERS FOR den-hoag: this is v1 silently losing a scope. Under the
owner's exit condition (parity with v1) the question is NOT "does den-hoag do
the same" -- the owner's standing instruction is that where den-hoag uncovers a
REAL DEFECT in v1, we CORRECT it. This is one, with a measurement.

NOT SCHEDULED. Adjacent to den-hoag-9xo.9 (cluster-path routes) and to the
node-multiplication arc.

title: edges.nix to-vocabulary is documented and unvalidated; a typo silently degrades to the default arm
description:
edges.nix:97 documents the `to` vocabulary for relation edge targets. THE
VOCABULARY IS NOT VALIDATED -- a typo'd member is accepted silently.

MEASURED (a15-spike, 2026-07-27; papers plans/2026-07-27-a15-spike.md section 3,
papers 5f825a9).

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: den-hoag-9xo.30's candidate S adds a FOURTH member to that
vocabulary --

  structural = false (default) -> to = "query"      (query surface only)
  structural = true            -> to = "structure"  (off-trace AND
                                                     reachability-bearing)

A typo'd "structure" under S would silently fall back to the default arm, so a
relation the author declared as reachability-bearing would be treated as
query-only. THE ROOT WOULD NOT EXIST AND NOTHING WOULD SAY SO -- which is the
exact silent-loss class den-hoag-9xo.8, .26 and m0a are all instances of.

⇒ D2 IS A PREREQUISITE OF S, not an adjacent nit. S amplifies an unchecked
vocabulary from three members to four, and the new member is the one that
decides whether a node materialises.

Note candidate C (relation rows feed containmentAttachments directly) does NOT
touch the vocabulary and so does not amplify this -- one of the reasons C is
cheaper. See the cost table in section 6.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): validate `to` against the declared vocabulary
and ABORT NAMED on an unknown member. Arm both ways -- a valid member that must
pass, and a near-miss typo that must abort FOR ITS OWN REASON rather than by
failing something downstream.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: [gen-schema] mkSchemaOption silently drops unknown kind keys — a typo is indistinguishable from an unsupported field
description:
gen-schema's mkSchemaOption keeps a FIXED KEY SET and SILENTLY DROPS unknown
keys from a kind declaration. No abort, no warning -- the field is simply
absent from the processed kind value.

MEASURED (denhoag-writer, 2026-07-27, while implementing den-hoag-9xo.13's
route 2):

  declared:  den.schema.host = { parent = "env"; parentRef = "environment";
                                 attachIf = "intoAttr"; }

  processed keys: [__functor keySemantics kind methods mixins options parent
                   refinements refs strict validators]

Both new keys absent. An implementation reading them off the processed kind
value gets null for every kind, attaches nothing, AND LOOKS LIKE THE CODE IS
WRONG rather than like the declaration was discarded.

WHY THIS IS THE ARC'S RECURRING SHAPE: a DECLARED FACT the framework accepts
and does not read. Same family as den-hoag-9xo.8 (registry kinds never
resolved), .9 (intoAttr ignored), .26 (instances dropped), and the inert
den.schema.<kind>.excludes bead -- in every case the user wrote something
true, the framework took it without complaint, and nothing consumed it.

ROUTE 2 DID NOT NEED THE FIX: den.attach lives on den's OWN surface, needs no
gen-schema change, and is arguably where attachment resolution belongs anyway.
So this is filed as a defect in its own right, not as a blocker.

DECISION THIS BEAD NEEDS: should mkSchemaOption ABORT on an unknown key rather
than dropping it? A typo in a kind declaration is currently indistinguishable
from a field the framework does not support, and both are silent. Note the
tension: den-hoag's own compat boundary deliberately accepts and ignores some
v1 surface, so a blanket abort may be wrong -- the decision is where the line
sits, and whether an unknown key on a KIND (as opposed to on an instance) is
ever legitimate.

Cross-reference: gen-aspects' Model C already settled the analogous question
for aspect keys -- scalar-undeclared aborts as a typo, attrset-undeclared is
admitted lazily as a nested aspect. That precedent is the obvious starting
point and may already decide this.

NOT SCHEDULED.

title: compat-identity-boundary lint misses bare-id sites it exists to catch; the design's table has grown every review round
description:
ci/tests/compat-identity-boundary.nix is meant to catch bare "${kind}:${name}"
id construction. It does not catch them all, and it is DEMONSTRABLY BLIND to at
least one site the .13 default-attachment design itself lists.

FOUND BY: design-reviewer, rev 6 review (papers bc7981c), while checking whether
the design's hand-maintained site table was trustworthy.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE TABLE. The .13 design has carried a list of
bare-id sites through four review rounds and EACH ROUND ADDED ONE:
  round 1  the original seven -- four of them turned out to be COMMENTS, and
           four real sites were missing (two of which .13 had listed and the
           design silently dropped)
  round 2  structural.nix:225-233 vs :365-367 -- the two consumers ALREADY
           DISAGREE, one aborts on N>1 while the other fans out
  round 3  ancNodeId (staged-resolution.nix:76-87) -- inside the seam the
           design depends on; multiplication was built CHILD-side only, the
           parent side of containment is bare throughout
  round 4  fleet.nix:125 -- __containment from bare coordinate-root ids,
           feeding resolved-aspects.nix:185/:197, so a multi-attached host
           leaves every user cell naming a node that was never built

A list that needs extending every round is not a list, it is a symptom. The
lint is the durable fix and it is the thing that is broken.

THE ARC'S OWN RULE APPLIES TO THE LINT ITSELF: a check that cannot match the
at-risk path is not a check. This one passes while sites it exists to catch go
unlisted -- the same shape as .8 surviving a green suite, one level up.

DECISION THIS BEAD NEEDS: widen the lint's predicate so it finds the sites the
design enumerates, THEN delete the design's table and let the lint be the
authority. Arm it both ways -- a bare construction it must catch, and a
legitimately-single-attachment site it must NOT flag -- otherwise a widened
predicate that flags everything is as useless as one that flags nothing.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so the next round does not add a fifth table entry.

title: [gen-merge] deprecationMessage never read; getSubModules/substSubModules divergent on 4 of 5 containers
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-merge. Two protocol findings surfaced by wj0's work, neither in
wj0's original four, neither actioned.

--- 1. deprecationMessage is stored but NEVER READ ---

gen-merge stores deprecationMessage faithfully on a type record, so a
field-presence check passes. Nothing ever reads it, so the warning is never
emitted.

MEASURED (genmerge-writer, 2026-07-27), direct (non-nested) use of a deprecated
type:
    nixpkgs    warned = 1
    gen-merge  warned = 0

HOW IT WAS FOUND, and why the method matters: this came out of the POSITIVE
CONTROL for a different question. The audit had listed "nestedTypes deprecation
walk parity" as UNVERIFIED. That premise is FALSE -- nixpkgs does not walk
nestedTypes for deprecation at all (lib/modules.nix:1139 reads only
opt.type.deprecationMessage, the outer type's own field; the only nestedTypes
read at :1521 is unrelated). A nested deprecated type warns on NEITHER engine.

Without the direct-use control in the same run, that would have been reported
as "nested deprecation: parity, both silent" -- true, and it would have hidden
that gen-merge cannot emit the warning AT ALL.

Same shape as the original wj0 catalogue: field PRESENT, behaviour ABSENT.
test-protocol-complete asserts presence only.

--- 2. getSubModules / substSubModules, protocol rows 10 and 11 ---

nixpkgs propagates the element's; gen-merge returns null / `_m: null` on
attrsOf, lazyAttrsOf, listOf, nullOr, deferredModule. 4 of 5 divergent.

Outside the getSubOptions scope wj0 covered. gen-merge has shipped the
implemented-getSubOptions / null-getSubModules combination on the containers
since 8daa25d without incident, so this is not urgent -- but it is the same
family and the same presence-vs-behaviour gap.

--- NOT IN SCOPE (owner ruling 2026-07-27, do not re-litigate) ---

specialArgs propagation is NOT a divergence: a parent specialArg read inside a
submodule body fails on BOTH engines for the same reason. gen-merge's submodule
is equivalent to nixpkgs' submodule. The propagating shape is
submoduleWith { specialArgs = ...; }, which gen-merge deliberately does not
ship. Settled, nothing owed.

title: [gen-schema] strict mode names the INSTANCE as the undeclared key when a kind declares zero options
description:
OWNERSHIP: gen-schema. Work happens in ~/Documents/repos/sini/gen-schema.
Tracked here because this is where we dispatch from.

A kind declaring ZERO options reports the INSTANCE NAME as the undeclared key,
so the strict-mode error names the wrong thing and its suggested fix is
nonsense.

Observed (denhoag-writer, 2026-07-27, converting ci/tests/_lib/den-compat-test
onto a real mkInstanceRegistry):

  STRICT MODE: "prod" is not declared on environment.
  Fix: schema.environment.options.prod = mkOption { ... };

"prod" is the INSTANCE name, not a key the author wrote. The suggested fix
would declare an option named after one instance. Correct diagnostic would name
the kind as having no declared options at all, or name the actual undeclared
key.

WORKAROUND IN PLACE, not a fix: the scaffold's environment kind was given a
`domain` option so it has a non-empty option set. den-hoag-9xo.23 does not chase
this.

WHY IT MATTERS beyond cosmetics: strict mode is a guard, and a guard whose
message names the wrong entity sends the reader to the wrong file. This arc has
repeatedly found that a diagnostic naming the wrong thing costs more than no
diagnostic -- see the bare `_type` collision key that named nothing until a path
prefix was threaded through it (DL-HS-70 method note a).

Reproduce: declare a kind with an empty options set, build a registry through
mkInstanceRegistry, instantiate one member, force it.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so it is not re-discovered.
close_reason:
Fixed upstream in gen-schema af3dbe9 (pushed): one hoisted primitiveTypeNames/isPrimitiveOption at lib/identity.nix:33, both local copies deleted. Two copies is HOW they stop agreeing, so the twin's own header claim ('can drift from neither') is now structural rather than aspirational.

den-hoag bumped past it at b2e5373 (three targeted --update-input, node-by-node diff after each, exactly the named node moved). parity's corpus/gen-schema node deliberately NOT moved -- e789c334 is the FROZEN CORPUS's own pin and moving it would invalidate every comparison the parity gate makes.

THE INVARIANT WAS ALREADY UNDER TEST AND THE TEST COULD NOT FAIL. gen-schema's test-forKind-matches-module asserts twin == stamp, but its fixture declares the identity field genMerge.types.int -- and int is the ONE name both type systems share. It stayed green through the entire divergence. Third independent arrival at the same rule in one day, from a new angle: A FIXTURE SAMPLED FROM THE AGREEING CASE CANNOT WITNESS DISAGREEMENT.

New test test-forKind-matches-module-nixpkgs-str, both halves armed:
  fixed                          equality PASS  contents PASS   green
  one shared list, str removed   equality PASS  contents FAIL   red
  twin given a private list back equality FAIL  contents PASS   red
Row 2 is why the contents pin exists: both sides degenerate together, equality
agrees perfectly, and only the contents pin catches it. Neither assertion is
redundant -- demonstrated, not assumed.

The den-hoag drift guard shipped too (compat-registry-engine::test-identity-reflection-agrees-with-the-stamp). It fired for real on the bump: equality held true across the move while only the contents pin shifted, so the two reflections agreed BEFORE and AFTER but now agree on the RIGHT key set instead of a too-small one. Checking WHICH HALF failed before touching either is the discipline; re-baselining both would have destroyed the signal.

title: Identity reflection keys on type.name string membership, so both engines' spellings must be enumerated
description:
Identity reflection decides which kind options are identity keys by testing
opt.type.name against a HARDCODED LIST of primitive type-name strings
(primitiveTypeNames, consumed by gen-schema mkIdentityModule and its
option-level twin identityHashForKind).

That is fragile by construction: the two engines spell the same type
differently.

  nixpkgs lib.types.str  -> type.name == "str"
  gen-types str          -> type.name == "string"    <-- ONLY divergent name
  int / bool             -> identical on both engines

MEASURED (denhoag-writer, real mkInstanceRegistry, 2026-07-27):
  corpus gen-schema  e789c334  primitives ["str","int","bool"]
  den-hoag gen-schema 017062cd primitives ["string","int","bool"]
  (16 commits apart; changed by 39d3d5d0 "re-host gen-schema registry onto
  gen-merge + gen-types")

So a kind option authored lib.types.str is an identity key under one pin and
not the other, and NOTHING RAISES -- the carried id_hash is simply computed
over a different key set, and the consumer's lookup misses.

den-hoag-9xo.23 routes registryKindOf through gen-schema's own
identityHashForKind so den-hoag cannot diverge from whichever list gen-schema
carries. THAT FIX DOES NOT REMOVE THIS FRAGILITY -- it only makes den-hoag
consistent with the list. Any two components that must agree on "is this a
primitive" still agree only by both enumerating the same spellings.

The question this bead exists to settle: should identity reflection key on
type.name at all, or on something that cannot drift between engines (a
structural predicate, a type-level tag, or a single shared source for the
list)? Note gen-types' "string" vs nixpkgs' "str" may itself be worth
reconciling -- but that is a separate decision with its own consumers, and
renaming a type is not obviously the right fix.

NOT SCHEDULED. Filed so the fragility is not re-discovered as a bug later.
Do not chase without a decision.

Origin: papers/den-architecture/specs/2026-07-27-suite-type-coverage-scoping.md
plus den-hoag-9xo.23's conversion of compat-registry-kind-marker.

title: Mixed attrs/fn collision silently drops the attrset arm (den.default.nixos, measured live)
description: See notes. The measured mixed case .20's guard deliberately leaves alone.
notes:
LIVE, MEASURED, and deliberately left alone by the .20 fix. Found by .20's complete census (exclusion-loop enumeration over the bridge path, 2 hits then clean).

THE INSTANCE: ci/tests/den-behavioral/static-include-dup-package.nix:132 declares `den.default.nixos` as a FUNCTION; it collides with an ATTRSET `den.default.nixos` from the scaffold. Measured `shapeAcc=attrs, shapeNew=fn` at v1DeepMerge's `else bv` (bridge.nix:76) => **the ATTRSET arm is silently discarded today.** The test passes because it only asserts the fn arm's content (services.locate.package), so nothing announces the loss.

WHY .20 DOES NOT FIX IT — and this is a scope decision, not an oversight. The .20 fix's collision branch normalizes both sides through `unwrapDeferredModule`, which is LOSSY on an attrset carrying content beside `imports`. Routing a mixed attrs/fn collision through that carrier would keep the fn and GUT the attrset — strictly worse than today's `else bv`, which at least returns one side intact. So .20's guard is deliberately `isFunction && isFunction`, narrower than its census predicate, and mixed collisions stay as they are.

=> This is the pre-existing defect .20's R7 tracked as "unmeasured". It is now MEASURED and NAMED: one live instance, on the `options.default` surface.

WHAT A FIX WOULD NEED (not designed): the attrs/fn case has no obvious correct merge. v1's answer is `aspectContentType` collecting BOTH into `__contentValues` regardless of shape (nix/lib/aspects/types.nix:404+) — so the principled fix is the same one .20 takes for fn/fn, but it cannot use the deferredModule carrier because of the sibling-content loss above. Either the carrier grows an arm for content-bearing attrsets (see den-hoag-9xo.21 — WIDER than it looks, it changes isEmptyDeferredModule's verdict for every caller), or the mixed case gets a different collection shape entirely. Scope before treating as adjacent to .20.

SURFACE NOTE: this is on `options.default` (bridge.nix:684), not `options.aspects` (:765). Both are folded by the SAME `v1DeepMerge`, and `options.default`'s own description calls it "den.default aspect — cross-module folded at the bridge boundary (v1 aspectType parity)" — so it is a class key on an aspect exactly as `den.aspects.<name>.<class>` is. Same defect, same helper, two surfaces.

NOT a regression: present before this arc, surfaced by measuring rather than by failing.

★ FRAMING CORRECTION (rung-writer, measured — supersedes the sharper reading in my filing note).

I wrote that routing this mixed collision through .20's carrier 'would keep the fn and GUT the attrset'. That is the hazard IN GENERAL, but NOT for this instance: the attrs side here has **no `imports` key**, so unwrapDeferredModule returns `[ m ]` — the module is passed through whole, nothing is gutted.

The gutting hazard is specific to CONTENT-BEARING MODULES (an attrset carrying content BESIDE `imports`), and .20's complete census found **none anywhere** — which is also what settled den-hoag-9xo.21's stop-condition as not-triggered.

=> **.22 is a PRESERVED-ARM question, not a data-loss-under-fix question.** The defect is that the attrset arm is silently discarded TODAY (measured: shapeAcc=attrs, shapeNew=fn at bridge.nix:76's `else bv`). Whoever picks it up should not inherit the belief that a carrier-based fix would actively corrupt this instance — for THIS shape it would not. The reason .20's guard stays `isFunction && isFunction` is the general hazard plus scope discipline, not a demonstrated corruption here.

The entanglement with .21 stands but is weaker than I implied: .21's helper limitation is why a carrier-based mixed fix is unsafe IN GENERAL, not why it is unsafe here.

title: unwrapDeferredModule silently drops content sitting beside imports (isEmptyDeferredModule reads it at compile.nix:348)
description: See notes.
notes:
LATENT, pre-existing, surfaced while reviewing the .20 fix design. Not introduced by that work — but the design leans harder on the same helper, which is why it is filed now.

`unwrapDeferredModule` (lib/module-shape.nix:12-17) is LOSSY on an attrset that carries content BESIDE `imports`:

    unwrapDeferredModule = m:
      if builtins.isAttrs m && m ? imports
      then builtins.concatMap unwrapDeferredModule m.imports
      else [ m ];

There is no arm for content sitting next to `imports`, so an ordinary NixOS module —
    { imports = [ ./x.nix ]; services.foo.enable = true; }
— unwraps to `[ ./x.nix ]` and **silently discards `services.foo.enable`**.

THE CONSUMER THAT MAKES IT REACHABLE: `isEmptyDeferredModule` (same file) is
    m: builtins.all (leaf: isAttrs leaf && all (k: hasPrefix "_" k) (attrNames leaf)) (unwrapDeferredModule m)
and it runs TODAY on class-key values at lib/compat/compile.nix:348. So `{ imports = [ { } ]; services.y = 1; }` unwraps to `[ { } ]`, is judged EMPTY, and the class slice is dropped as a declared no-op — losing real content, silently.

REACHABILITY — UNSETTLED, and deliberately not asserted either way. Likely unreachable post-typing, because the typed body is a pure `{ _file; imports }` wrap with no sibling content. BUT compile.nix:348 runs PRE-gen-aspects, on values that may be user-authored. That is the gap.

SETTLING TEST, already scheduled at no extra cost: the .20 design's T0.2 records per-collision ARM SHAPES. **If any class key turns out to be a content-bearing module (an attrset with `imports` AND other keys), this is LIVE** and wants its own fix. If none is, it stays latent and this bead records the shape that would make it live.

RELATION TO .20: the .20 fix's collision branch normalizes through this same helper, which is why its guard must be `isFunction && isFunction` and NOT the `||` its census predicate uses — a mixed fn/content-module collision routed through the carrier would keep the fn and GUT the module, strictly worse than today's `else bv` (which returns the whole module intact and loses the fn). That guard asymmetry is recorded in the .20 design; this bead is the underlying helper limitation it works around.

SCOPING WARNING from the .20 design work — the fix here is NOT symmetrical with .20's, and is wider than it looks.

.20's answer is to keep content-bearing modules OFF the carrier path (the fix's guard is isFunction && isFunction, deliberately narrower than its census predicate). That works because .20 only needs to avoid routing such a module through unwrapDeferredModule.

.21's answer cannot be that. The helper ITSELF has to grow an arm for sibling content — and that changes isEmptyDeferredModule's verdict for EVERY caller, not just the one that surfaced it. module-shape.nix:4-6 lists them: classSliceOf's no-op drop, compile's guard, and the annotate-battery read. A module currently judged EMPTY (because its sibling content is invisible to the unwrap) would start being judged NON-empty, which flips a no-op drop into a live slice at every one of those sites.

So: scope before treating it as a one-liner. The blast radius is the caller set, not the helper.

MEASURED, not inferred (rung-writer, by evaluation rather than inspection):
    unwrapDeferredModule { imports = [ { a = 1; } ]; services.foo.enable = true; }  =>  [ { a = 1; } ]
siblingSurvives = false. The sibling is silently gone.

FREE EVIDENCE INCOMING: .20's T0.2 census now records whether any class-key arm is a content-bearing module (an attrset with imports AND sibling content). If one exists, .21 is LIVE via compile.nix:348's pre-typing path and wants its own arc. If none does, it stays latent and the census is the record of that.

title: Correct den-hoag's recorded FALSE 'deferred gen-resolve change' (concern-productions.nix:270-271)
description:
den-hoag lib/concern-productions.nix:270-271 records VERBATIM: "The full static fix = `resolve.nta` accepting stratum + readsAttrs (a DEFERRED gen-resolve change); until then the demand-order is the honest residual."

The PREMISE is true but the CONCLUSION is FALSE — no gen-resolve change is needed. VERIFIED by orchestrator directly:
- gen-resolve/lib/equation.nix:66-73 — `nta` does hardcode readsAttrs = [] and omits stratum (so stratumOf yields "structural"). Premise correct.
- equation.nix:47-63 — `attr` takes { name; kind; compute; readsAttrs; stratum ? null; } EXPLICITLY.
- equation.nix:8-17 — `stratumOf kind explicit` returns `explicit` FIRST, for ANY kind, before any kind-based default.
- grep for .kind across gen-resolve/lib/ outside equation.nix returns EXACTLY ONE hit: schedule.nix:9 isCircular. `kind` has no other schedule or runtime effect.

=> `attr { name = "children"; kind = "nta"; readsAttrs = [ ... ]; stratum = "..."; compute = spawn; }` is a stratum-declared, read-declared, SCHEDULE-VISIBLE NTA today. `resolve.nta` is sugar for the zero-read case, not a ceiling.

This is a FIFTH instance of the 0-for-4 "needs a new/extended gen primitive" pattern (prior four all expressible via expandPreorder / wrapGatedFn / inheritSet). Fix the comment so it stops advertising a gen gap that does not exist. Per feedback_no_temporal_comments: cite the mechanism (attr/stratumOf), not a task key.
close_reason: Comment corrected @22c78c6. The false 'DEFERRED gen-resolve change' claim removed; premise (resolve.nta hardcodes readsAttrs=[] + omits stratum) retained as true. Gate SEEN: CI_EXIT=0, PARITY_EXIT=0, allEqual=true. Comment-only change (verified: zero non-comment diff lines); nix fmt clean (0 changed).

title: Post-ship: benchmark harness for the Performance Model claims
description:
Post-ship addition, owner-scoped 2026-07-27. NOT part of the docs conformance pass (den-hoag-h5d).

REFERENCE.md's Performance Model carries a 500-host table with wall-time rows (Baseline / Milliseconds /
~1 second / Minutes) and the headline "~10x fewer computational steps". Measured provenance:
  - The 118,000 / 12,800 step counts are an ANALYTIC derivation, stated in the canonical spec
    specs/2026-05-24-den-v2-hoag-architecture.md:740 under a v1-vs-v2 mechanism comparison.
  - demos/hoag-*.nix are real synthetics validating the MEMOIZATION MODEL (multi-level attribute-dependent
    synthesis, an independent replication of the HOAG architecture) — not the 500-host table.
  - The WALL-TIME column has no cited basis in either tree.

No benchmark harness exists in den-hoag or the gen repos, so the conformance ledger records this claim as
having NO POSSIBLE DETECTOR — the exact failure shape that pass exists to eliminate. Owner ruling: track it
as a post-ship addition rather than blocking the docs pass or reframing the claim.

SCOPE WHEN TAKEN UP: a synthetic fleet generator (parameterised host count), measuring eval time and
allocation across the table's four scenarios (no cross-host collections / gather-10 config-free / gather-all
config-free / gather-all config-dependent). Then the ledger row cites the bench command instead of recording
an unmeasurable.

WORTH CHECKING FIRST: the demos/ synthetics may already provide the harness skeleton, and den-hoag's ci
already builds whole-corpus evaluations — a benchmark may be closer to reachable than a from-scratch build.

title: Add a codegraph module to nix-config (user fork + Nix language support)
description:
Follow-up to the codebase-memory-mcp work. codegraph (github:colbymchenry/codegraph, ~63k stars) is a second pre-indexed code-knowledge-graph MCP. Evaluate alongside codebase-memory-mcp, not as a replacement.

CORRECTED BASE (supersedes the first pass of this description):
- PR #1190 is MERGED (2026-07-06, by maintainer colbymchenry). It carries #1084, which superseded #219 and #330. So Nix support is ALREADY IN MAIN — no fork needed for the language, no unmerged-PR base to track.
- PR #330 is still nominally OPEN but functionally dead.
- Vic's branch (vic:codegraph:push-ukzyuslurlxp) is 1 commit, 51-line extractor, 494 commits behind, functionTypes empty (every binding becomes a variable node). Obsolete twice over. Do not base on it.

WHAT #1190 SHIPPED (well beyond our codebase-memory-mcp patch):
- Functions simple/destructured/curried WITH signatures; inherit and inherit (from); exported-vs-private via returned-attrset detection; call refs. Fixed a node-identity bug (=== on web-tree-sitter wrappers is always false, so curried-chain dedup never fired).
- File wiring: import ./path, ./dir to default.nix, NixOS imports = [ ... ] lists, flake-style modules = [ ... ], and callPackage ./pkg.nix { }. Literal paths only — <nixpkgs>, variables, interpolations deliberately unlinked.
- Module-system option wiring synthesizer: a config write (home.file.".gitconfig" = ...) links to the module DECLARING that option path. Longest static-prefix match, >=2 segments, ambiguous declarations bail, every hop labeled heuristic. HIGH relevance to nix-config aspects; NOT relevant to den-hoag/gen-* which are pure lib code with no module-system options.
- Resolution scoping: nix calls resolve lexically or via explicit import wiring only. On nix-darwin this cut calls edges 2013 -> 604, sampled survivors lexically correct.
- Grammar: vendored wasm from nix-community/tree-sitter-nix @3d0173d regenerated at ABI 15; all 54 upstream corpus tests pass.
- Validated to nixpkgs scale: 44,368 files, 1.30M nodes, 3m49s index.

PACKAGING (still on us): npm package @colbymchenry/codegraph v1.5.0, bin.codegraph -> dist/bin/codegraph.js, 10 runtime deps (web-tree-sitter, tree-sitter-wasms, commander, ...), plus a codegraph-kernel/ directory. No flake at repo root. Issue #324 ('Nix flake please?') is CLOSED but #1190 lists it as addressed together with #332 — that conflates language support with packaging, so no flake actually exists. Needs buildNpmPackage + npmDepsHash, plus whatever codegraph-kernel requires.

WORK: package codegraph for nix (fork only if we need carry-patches, which the language support no longer requires); add a den aspect under modules/den/aspects/apps/dev/ai/mcp/ in the codebase-memory-mcp mold; measure head-to-head on den-hoag.

CEILING, STATE UP FRONT: neither tool evaluates Nix. Neither resolves a member across a flake input (prelude.genAttrs). #1190's option wiring closes the module-system half for nix-config but does nothing for gen-lib function surfaces. That gap remains gen-lsp's.
acceptance_criteria: codegraph packaged and wired as an aspect; Function/Variable/CALLS counts on den-hoag measured head-to-head against patched codebase-memory-mcp; a recommendation on running one or both

title: INVERSE doc drift: production-guard.nix denies a user surface default.nix declares
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger, 2026-07-27. Notable because it is the ONLY drift found in the inverse direction: here REFERENCE.md is RIGHT and the CODE COMMENT is the drifted artifact.

lib/production-guard.nix:11 states 'There is NO den.productions.<name> user surface yet'.
lib/default.nix:656 declares options.den.productions.

A stale comment that denies the existence of a shipped surface is worse than a missing one — a reader trusting it concludes the surface must be added, and the guard's own reason for existing reads as speculative rather than live.

Fix is the comment, not the code. Verify no other comment in production-guard.nix rests on the same premise before editing.

title: output-modules.nix is 1,202 lines / 78.8K carrying four concerns
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger, 2026-07-27. lib/attributes/output-modules.nix is the largest
file in den-hoag at 1,202 lines / 78.8K and carries four distinct concerns.

Context that makes it more than a size complaint: REFERENCE.md Open Question 8 — per-class output assembly
properties (the instantiation function, validator behaviour and merge strategy carried on
den.classes.<name>) — is STILL LISTED OPEN while this file has grown to the largest in the tree. Whether the

Also relevant: the ledger measured that output-modules is NOT a registered equation — there is no

POST-EVAL over the final eval. So the "12 attributes" framing does not describe it, and a split should start
from what it actually is rather than from the table.

See [[feedback_refactor_large_files]].

title: gen-dispatch clone directory is still named gen-derive
description:
Found by the den-hoag-h5d conformance ledger, 2026-07-27. The library was renamed gen-derive -> gen-dispatch (a github redirect keeps old refs resolving), but the local clone directory is still named gen-derive.

Consequence: any tooling that resolves a library by DIRECTORY NAME silently misses it or resolves the wrong path. Silent, not loud — which is the failure class this project keeps paying for.

Note the RESUME-CHECKPOINT already records this as a pin ('gen-derive @8f537ec (dir is gen-derive, NOT gen-dispatch)'), so it is known and worked around rather than fixed. Decide: rename the directory and fix the references, or record it deliberately in one place instead of as a per-consumer workaround.

title: errors.nix:188 justifies C1 with a claim about v1 that is false at the level it names
description:
lib/compat/errors.nix:188 justifies the C1 surface-totality check with:

  "a typo'd or unknown `den.*` key is ABSORBED BY THE PERMISSIVE v1 EVAL and
   rejected HERE"

MEASURED AGAINST v1 @11866c16: the top-level half of that claim is FALSE.
v1 does NOT absorb an unknown top-level `den.*` key -- it ABORTS.

  control  den.zzzNoSuchOptionAnywhere
           -> error: The option `den.zzzNoSuchOptionAnywhere' does not exist.
  and independently, den.relations aborted the same way in the .30 fork probe
  (papers 6cfe558 sections 8.2/8.3)

THE COMMENT IS TRUE ONE LEVEL DOWN. Host ENTRY keys are strict = false +
freeform (den v1 entities/host.nix:56), and an unknown key there IS absorbed
inertly -- measured in the same investigation (section 8.4: entity-side .edges
rode v1's freeform with a BYTE-IDENTICAL id_hash).

⇒ TWO LEVELS ARE CONFLATED IN ONE SENTENCE, and C1's stated justification rests
on the half that does not hold.

C1 IS STILL NEEDED -- den-hoag's OWN ingest surface is permissive even though
v1's top level is not, so the check has a real job. But the RECORDED REASON IS
NOT THE REASON, and a reader reasoning from it will conclude v1 is permissive
at a level where it aborts.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this arc has repeatedly been bitten by
planning against a recorded claim that was true when written or true at another
level -- see den-hoag-9xo.13's three stale warnings, and .16's diagnosis
refuted by measurement while the ledger and checkpoint already disagreed with
it. A justification comment is evidence (a comment stating a constraint is
evidence); when it is wrong it is worse than absent because it is load-bearing
for the next reader's reasoning.

FIX: restate C1's justification to name the level it actually holds at (host
entry keys, freeform) and the real reason C1 is needed (den-hoag's own ingest
surface is permissive). Do NOT delete C1.

Source: papers plans/2026-07-27-v1-registry-namespace-parity.md (papers af215a9).
NOT SCHEDULED.

title: Formatter and lib/compat/parity/ledger.md disagree; only surfaces when formatting lib/
description:
The repo formatter and lib/compat/parity/ledger.md disagree, and the
disagreement only surfaces when the formatter is pointed at lib/.

  nix run ./ci#formatter.x86_64-linux -- lib ci/tests

reformats lib/compat/parity/ledger.md:543, escaping a list marker:

  -3) and a fourth asserted one would be worth less than an open question.
  +3\) and a fourth asserted one would be worth less than an open question.

MEASURED: the change is pre-existing drift, unrelated to any code change. Running
the formatter over ci/tests alone reports "0 changed"; adding lib to the paths
reports "1 changed" and that one file is the ledger.

WHY IT MATTERS: a writer who formats broadly before committing picks this up as
an unrelated hunk in an otherwise unrelated commit. It was caught and reverted
once (unstaged, not committed) during the .23 work, but only because the diff was
read line by line. The next broad format is likely to carry it in silently.

RESOLUTION IS A CHOICE, not obvious:
  (a) accept the formatter's output and commit the escape, or
  (b) exclude lib/**/*.md (or the ledger specifically) from the formatter's
      scope, if the ledger is meant to be hand-maintained prose.

Whichever way, the point is that formatter scope and the ledger should agree, so
that "format before committing" is a safe instruction rather than one that
produces unrelated churn depending on which paths you pass.
